items.desc: StellDirVor is an independent consulting, trade and technology company specializing in immersive technologies for healthcare. We support organizations in implementing digital innovations — Virtual, Augmented and Mixed Reality as well as AI — particularly for learning, training and real-time assistance in clinical and care environments. By combining technology and healthcare, we help optimize processes, improve knowledge transfer and enhance quality of care. Supported by a Germany (ZIM) and Taiwanese (GIPIP) partnership grant, we are currently developing ARAIAS — an AR- and AI-based hands-free training and assistance system for chronic wound care. Using AR smart glasses, the system enables 3D capture, AI-supported analysis, and standardized remote expertise and documentation directly at the point of care. As our ML Engineer (Computer Vision & ML Ops), you will build the AI capabilities at the core of ARAIAS: evaluating and fine-tuning computer vision models on smart glasses data, running the ML operations behind them, and applying generative AI to create synthetic medical images for education. We're at an early stage — moving from concept to working prototype — so the near-term focus is on validating models and building toward a proof of concept we can test in real education and clinical settings. As part of a small team, you will own the full data lifecycle end to end — from sourcing, consent and annotation to preparation — alongside model development and deployment. We welcome candidates at different experience levels. What matters most is a solid ML foundation and genuine awareness of the medical imaging domain. Notes: Due to the nature of the project, we can only consider candidates who are already residing in Germany. items.desc: Build the Physical AI powering the next generation of home robots. The next major technological wave is approaching: Robots for the home. Technology is moving beyond the digital world and starting to take action in our physical lives – finally taking on the everyday tasks that smartphones and apps have barely been able to simplify. Mana Robotics develops autonomous robots for everyday life, with the ambition of becoming Europe's leading home robotics brand: innovative, beautifully designed, trustworthy, and relentlessly focused on real-world usefulness. Our first product tackles one of the most time-consuming household tasks: preparing meals every day. Our ultra-compact, autonomous cooking robot "Mana One" prepares meals from fresh ingredients entirely on its own – the biggest leap forward in household convenience since the invention of the dishwasher. After several years of development, research in Physical AI, and eight generations of hardware tested in real-world environments, we are now bringing this new product category to market. At the heart of our technology is a fundamental challenge: Teaching robots to perform complex physical tasks reliably in the real world. From handling ingredients and manipulating kitchen tools to adapting to unfamiliar situations, we believe learning-based robotics will be key to making truly autonomous home robots a reality. That's where you come in! Your Role As a Machine Learning Engineer – Robotics , you will develop, train, and deploy learning-based models that enable our robots to perform complex manipulation tasks autonomously. You'll work at the intersection of Robot Learning, LLMs, and real-world robotic systems , turning cutting-edge research into capabilities that work reliably on our proprietary physical hardware. Together with our robotics and engineering team, you'll take ownership of the full Robot Learning pipeline – from collecting and preparing training data to experimenting with model architectures, evaluating performance, and deploying policies on our robots. An ideal role for someone who is passionate about cutting-edge AI, enjoys solving challenging technical problems, and wants to see their models do more than generate predictions – actually interact with the physical world. What You'll Do You will initially focus on developing and advancing the skills of our autonomous cooking robot, with the opportunity to expand your work to entirely new categories of home robots as we grow. Your responsibilities will include: Robot Learning & Model Development: Research, implement, train, and improve learning-based models for robotic manipulation, including approaches such as Imitation Learning, Behavior Cloning, Diffusion Policies, Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, and whatever groundbreaking approaches emerge next. Data Collection & Training Pipelines: Expand and improve workflows for collecting robotic demonstrations, processing multimodal sensor data, and creating high-quality datasets for model training. Model Training & Experimentation: Design, run, and evaluate experiments with modern learning architectures, pre-trained models, and fine-tuning techniques to improve robotic capabilities. Real-World Robot Deployment: Deploy trained policies onto our robotic systems and bring models from the lab to real-world user environments. Evaluation & Performance Optimization: Develop systematic evaluation methods, analyze model failures, and continuously improve the robustness, generalization, and reliability of learned behaviors. Robotic Manipulation: Work on challenging real-world tasks involving object manipulation, tool use, visual perception, and contact-rich interactions. Research & Innovation: Stay close to developments in Physical AI and Robot Learning, evaluate promising research, and translate new approaches into practical improvements to our product together with a hand-selected passionate team. You'll work closely with our interdisciplinary and technical founding team, with substantial freedom to shape our technical approach to Robot Learning. What You Bring We're looking for an engineer with a strong foundation in Machine Learning who enjoys hands-on experimentation, thinks independently, is driven to understand problems from first principles, and is excited about bringing AI into the physical world. Ideally, you bring: A degree in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Robotics , or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Strong practical experience in Machine Learning , including training, evaluating, and improving neural network models. Proficient programming skills in Python and practical experience with modern ML frameworks. Familiarity with the full ML development workflow, from dataset preparation and experimentation to model evaluation and deployment. A structured, independent, and first-principles thinking approach to solving complex engineering problems. Curiosity, initiative, and a genuine interest in robotics and Physical …

items.desc: About Teton Teton is building the foundational data layer for the point of care, using real-time, multimodal AI to generate a digital twin of the patient and care environment. Our proprietary computer-vision system enables staff to automate documentation, proactively manage resident acuity, and streamline workflows across entire facilities. Our platform delivers unprecedented access to real-time data insights, empowering healthcare providers with actionable intelligence to enhance decision-making and elevate care delivery. The Role We are looking for an AI Research Scientist / Engineer to accelerate the development of Cassandra, our Generative World Model for healthcare. Cassandra is pretrained on sequences of behavioral tokens representing residents' activities, sleep, mobility, vital signs, and care interactions. By learning to predict what happens next, Cassandra learns patterns of human behavior, enabling applications such as predicting falls before they happen and simulating the potential impact of care interventions. Much like large language models, Cassandra learns from large-scale sequential data and exhibits similar scaling laws. However, modeling human behavior introduces unique research challenges, including continuous-time modeling, long-context dependencies, and learning from heterogeneous behavioral signals. Unlike most foundation models trained on publicly available data, Cassandra learns from a proprietary and continuously growing dataset of real-world human behavior. This creates an opportunity to explore fundamental research questions while building technology with direct real-world impact. We are looking for someone with strong technical intuition and hands-on experience training and scaling large sequence models. You will have the opportunity to take ownership of fundamental research challenges and directly shape both the underlying foundation model and the applications built on top of it. Read more about Cassandra: Introducing Cassandra Key Responsibilities In this role, you will own and drive research and development across two main areas: Pre-training and scaling Cassandra. Improve the end-to-end pre-training pipeline, from behavioral data representation and tokenization to model architecture, training objectives, and scaling. Many techniques from the LLM research toolbox are directly applicable, but important challenges remain, particularly around continuous-time event modeling, irregularly sampled data, and long-term dependencies. You will design experiments, develop new approaches, and translate research into improvements in model capabilities. Developing and productionizing downstream applications. Our first application of Cassandra's learned representations is predicting the risk of a resident falling within the next five minutes. You will improve these predictive capabilities and explore new applications, from forecasting changes in resident behavior to simulating the effects of care interventions. The goal is to turn advances in foundation modeling into tangible improvements in personalized, proactive care. What We're Looking For Minimum Qualifications: Hands-on experience training large-scale sequence models, such as Transformers, state-space models, or LLMs. Deep understanding of neural network architectures, optimization, training dynamics, and scaling laws. Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with experience building efficient, reliable training and evaluation pipelines. Ability to independently design experiments, interpret results, and translate research ideas into working implementations. Solid mathematical foundations in machine learning, probability, and statistics. Mindset: Research-driven and hands-on. You enjoy reading papers, challenging assumptions, and implementing ideas yourself rather than stopping at theoretical insights. Strong technical intuition. You can reason about why a model works, identify bottlenecks, and prioritize experiments that are most likely to move the needle. Ownership and autonomy. You are comfortable tackling open-ended problems, navigating uncertainty, and taking ideas from initial hypothesis to production. Pragmatic and ambitious. You care about advancing the state of the art, but ultimately measure success by whether your work enables capabilities that were previously impossible. Time Zone/location: Based in Copenhagen, Denmark, or willing to relocate. Preferred Qualifications: Research or engineering experience with LLM pre-training, including architecture design, data mixtures, training objectives, or scaling experiments. Experience with generative modeling of sequential, temporal, or event-based data. Familiarity with continuous-time models, point processes, time-to-event prediction, or survival modeling. Experience with long-context architectures, such as Mamba, recurrent models, or efficient attention mechanisms. Experience with distributed training, GPU optimization, and performance profiling. A track record of impactful ML …

items.desc:
About us
 Re-architecting Engineering for the Age of Intelligence
PhysicsX is the physics AI company for industrials. The company’s mission is to accelerate hardware innovation by overhauling what industrial engineering and manufacturing look like today. PhysicsX is building a new simulation software stack to deliver deep physics AI enablement across the entire engineering lifecycle. The company partners with leading organisations in aerospace & defence, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy & renewables, supporting them on some of their most critical and complex challenges. PhysicsX is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with offices in London, New York, and Singapore and an expanding presence in the Bay Area.
 The role
 You will own the product capability that lets PhysicsX and its customers improve LLMs for their specific work.
 You will be a hands-on product ML engineer embedded deeply with our Research group and accountable for turning post-training methods into something customers can use. The first goal is to make open models perform strongly on the evals and benchmarks that matter to us. The longer-term goal is a repeatable platform capability through which customers can train models on their own workflows keeping their data, learned behaviour and intellectual property under their control.
 The remit is broader than supervised fine-tuning. You will choose and apply the right post-training methods, including preference optimisation, reinforcement learning, distillation, synthetic data and verifier-based approaches. You will own the capability roadmap and production outcome; Research will be a close partner in developing methods, and platform product teams will be partners in integrating the experience.
 What you will do
 Own the path from a base model and customer workflow to a measured, deployable model improvement.
 Build reliable post-training harnesses covering data preparation, training, evaluation, model artifacts and hand-off to serving.
 Improve open models against PhysicsX's agent and engineering benchmarks, using evidence to decide whether training is better than changes to prompts, tools or the agent design.
 Develop and operate methods spanning SFT, preference optimisation, RLHF/RLAIF, RL with verifiable rewards, distillation, rejection sampling and related techniques.
 Build reproducible synthetic-data and expert-data pipelines, including quality filtering, provenance, licensing and contamination controls.
 Design reward signals, verifiers and rollout workflows while detecting reward hacking, benchmark overfitting, model collapse and unintended regressions.
 Make post-training available through a mix of managed workflows and expert-facing interfaces.
 Ensure customer data and resulting model artifacts can remain within the customer's platform environment across SaaS, VPC and air-gapped deployments.
 Work on cross-product and public benchmarks. Own experiment diagnostics with Research, with shared approval where results support product or external claims.
 Work with the LLM Self-Hosting & Model Routing Lead to move trained models into supported production serving and routing.
 Set the product roadmap for model improvement, balancing research opportunity with customer value, operability and time to production.
 Help determine how this capability should grow and, over time, shape the team around it.
 What you bring
 Where you need to be strongest
 You have measurably improved model behaviour through post-training and turned that work into a capability used in production.
 You are deeply hands-on across data, training, evaluation and debugging; you can take an experiment from hypothesis to deployed artifact.
 You understand modern post-training methods well enough to choose among them based on the task and evidence rather than fashion.
 You have built high-quality training datasets from expert, behavioural or synthetic sources and understand that data design is part of model design.
 You can diagnose training and behavioural failures, including instability, drift, reward exploitation, leakage and overfitting to evals.
 You are product-minded: you start from a user workflow, define success, make trade-offs and build an experience others can operate.
 You can work as the accountable product owner of a technical capability while collaborating closely with research scientists, platform engineers and product teams.
 Foundations
 Strong Python and PyTorch or equivalent model-training frameworks.
 Distributed training, accelerator utilisation, checkpointing, recovery, experiment tracking and reproducibility.
 Evaluation of model and agent behaviour, including controlled experiments and ablations.
 Data governance, privacy, provenance and safe handling of customer-owned training data and artifacts.
 Model packaging and the operational path from training to evaluation and production serving.
 Clear technical writing and communication across research, product, engineering, delivery and …

About The Internship At Barco Labs, you'll work on innovative research projects at the intersection of AI and digital pathology, helping shape the future of medical imaging. During this internship, you will explore how state-of-the-art foundation models and self-supervised learning techniques can be applied to large-scale digital pathology images. items.desc: Back to jobs AI Engineer: Post-Training London About Us Re-architecting Engineering for the Age of Intelligence PhysicsX is the physics AI company for industrials. The company’s mission is to accelerate hardware innovation by overhauling what industrial engineering and manufacturing look like today. PhysicsX is building a new simulation software stack to deliver deep physics AI enablement across the entire engineering lifecycle. The company partners with leading organisations in aerospace & defence, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy & renewables, supporting them on some of their most critical and complex challenges. PhysicsX is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with offices in London, New York, and Singapore and an expanding presence in the Bay Area. The role You will own the product capability that lets PhysicsX and its customers improve LLMs for their specific work. You will be a hands-on product ML engineer embedded deeply with our Research group and accountable for turning post-training methods into something customers can use. The first goal is to make open models perform strongly on the evals and benchmarks that matter to us. The longer-term goal is a repeatable platform capability through which customers can train models on their own workflows keeping their data, learned behaviour and intellectual property under their control. The remit is broader than supervised fine-tuning. You will choose and apply the right post-training methods, including preference optimisation, reinforcement learning, distillation, synthetic data and verifier-based approaches. You will own the capability roadmap and production outcome; Research will be a close partner in developing methods, and platform product teams will be partners in integrating the experience. What you will do Own the path from a base model and customer workflow to a measured, deployable model improvement. Build reliable post-training harnesses covering data preparation, training, evaluation, model artifacts and hand-off to serving. Improve open models against PhysicsX's agent and engineering benchmarks, using evidence to decide whether training is better than changes to prompts, tools or the agent design. Develop and operate methods spanning SFT, preference optimisation, RLHF/RLAIF, RL with verifiable rewards, distillation, rejection sampling and related techniques. Build reproducible synthetic-data and expert-data pipelines, including quality filtering, provenance, licensing and contamination controls. Design reward signals, verifiers and rollout workflows while detecting reward hacking, benchmark overfitting, model collapse and unintended regressions. Make post-training available through a mix of managed workflows and expert-facing interfaces. Ensure customer data and resulting model artifacts can remain within the customer's platform environment across SaaS, VPC and air-gapped deployments. Work on cross-product and public benchmarks. Own experiment diagnostics with Research, with shared approval where results support product or external claims. Work with the LLM Self-Hosting & Model Routing Lead to move trained models into supported production serving and routing. Set the product roadmap for model improvement, balancing research opportunity with customer value, operability and time to production. Help determine how this capability should grow and, over time, shape the team around it. What you bring Where you need to be strongest You have measurably improved model behaviour through post-training and turned that work into a capability used in production. You are deeply hands-on across data, training, evaluation and debugging; you can take an experiment from hypothesis to deployed artifact. You understand modern post-training methods well enough to choose among them based on the task and evidence rather than fashion. You have built high-quality training datasets from expert, behavioural or synthetic sources and understand that data design is part of model design. You can diagnose training and behavioural failures, including instability, drift, reward exploitation, leakage and overfitting to evals. You are product-minded: you start from a user workflow, define success, make trade-offs and build an experience others can operate. You can work as the accountable product owner of a technical capability while collaborating closely with research scientists, platform engineers and product teams. Foundations Strong Python and PyTorch or equivalent model-training frameworks. Distributed training, accelerator utilisation, checkpointing, recovery, experiment tracking and reproducibility. Evaluation of model and agent behaviour, including controlled experiments and ablations. Data governance, privacy, provenance and safe handling of customer-owned training data and artifacts. Model packaging and the operational path from training to evaluation and production serving. Clear technical writing and communication across research, product, engineering, …

You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms. You will develop audio understanding algorithms that enable devices to recognize what is happening in the world around them. Areas of interest include sound event detection and localization (SELD), acoustic scene understanding, unusual or anomalous sound detection, and multimodal context understanding from audio, video, and motion sensors. Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next. Develop robust methods for sound event detection/localization, acoustic anomaly detection, and context-aware audio interpretation. Experience developing and evaluating deep learning models in PyTorch; strong Python skills. Understanding of audio representations, DSP, and evaluation metrics for detection, localization, and generalization. Experience with multimodal fusion (video, IMU, or other sensors) for context understanding is a plus. Experience with efficient inference, causal ML, ONNX/TFLite, embedded ML, or C/C++ is a plus. Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required. At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! We are a proudly independent company—driven by purpose, guided by our values, and united by a belief in the power of sound. As the world leader in audio experiences, we’re creating what’s next—pushing boundaries and delivering transformative sound experiences for people everywhere. Join us and make your next career move a mic-drop. Let’s Make Waves. ‎

items.desc:
Join our Team
 About this opportunity 
 The AI Accelerator within BNEW SAN is on a mission to innovate, incubate, and deliver AI-based solutions that fundamentally redesign Customer Support and Network Deployment — shifting from human-led coordination to composable, agent-centric intelligence. We aim to move beyond simple efficiency gains to create a compounding cycle of optimization, where every interaction generates actionable insights that continuously refine operations, reduce time-to-market, and accelerate the journey toward autonomous network operations.
 We are looking for an LLM Post-Training Engineer to own the process of making foundation models genuinely useful in our domain. Pretrained LLMs are powerful starting points — but it is post-training that transforms a general-purpose model into a reliable, domain-aligned agent capable of operating autonomously in the complex world of telecommunications. You will design and execute the training strategies, reward frameworks, and data pipelines that shape how our models reason, respond, and improve — closing the gap between what a model knows out of the box and what our agents need to do in production.
 What you will do: 
 Domain Knowledge Injection via Fine-Tuning 
 Design and execute supervised fine-tuning (SFT) pipelines that inject domain-specific knowledge into base LLMs across Customer Support and Network Deployment contexts
 Apply parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques — including LoRA, QLoRA, and adapter-based methods — to adapt large models effectively within compute and latency constraints
 Collaborate with the AI & Domain Specialist and AI Data & Integration Engineer to ensure fine-tuning datasets are high quality, domain-representative, and correctly formatted for training objectives
 Maintain a structured catalog of fine-tuned model variants, adapter checkpoints, and associated training configurations to support reproducibility and lifecycle governance
 Policy-Reward Training & Alignment 
 Design and implement policy-reward training pipelines using advanced optimization methods including GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) and SAPO (Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization)
 Define reward models and preference datasets that encode domain-specific quality signals — going beyond generic helpfulness to capture what correct, safe, and operationally appropriate behavior looks like in telco contexts
 Iterate on alignment strategies based on evaluation feedback and production signal — continuously refining model behavior to better match system requirements and domain acceptance criteria
 Stay current with the rapidly evolving post-training research landscape, identifying and assessing new alignment techniques for potential adoption
 Automatic Dataset Curation & Synthetic Data Generation 
 Build and maintain automated pipelines for domain dataset curation — sourcing, filtering, deduplicating, and formatting data at scale for both SFT and reward training
 Design synthetic data generation strategies that augment real-world datasets — producing diverse, high-quality training examples for scenarios where real data is scarce, sensitive, or imbalanced
 Collaborate with domain experts to validate synthetic data quality and ensure generated examples accurately reflect real-world telco operational scenarios
 Implement data quality gates and automated checks that maintain dataset integrity throughout the curation and generation pipeline
 Training Run Management & Experiment Tracking 
 Own the end-to-end management of training runs — including infrastructure provisioning, job scheduling, hyperparameter configuration, and run monitoring
 Maintain a rigorous experiment tracking practice, logging all training configurations, dataset versions, evaluation results, and model artifacts to ensure full reproducibility and informed decision-making
 Define and report on key training metrics — loss curves, reward signal trends, evaluation benchmark scores, and alignment quality indicators — providing clear visibility to the AI System Architect and engineering leadership
 Identify and resolve training instabilities, overfitting risks, and performance bottlenecks across the post-training pipeline
 You will bring: 
 Proven hands-on experience in LLM fine-tuning and post-training, with a track record of adapting large language models for production use cases using SFT, LoRA, or equivalent techniques
 Strong understanding of RLHF, preference optimization, and policy-reward training methods — direct experience with GRPO, DPO, PPO, or similar approaches is highly valued
 Experience building automated data curation and synthetic data generation pipelines for LLM training at scale
 Solid grasp of experiment tracking best practices and tooling — able to maintain a disciplined, reproducible training workflow across multiple concurrent experiments
 Familiarity with distributed training infrastructure, GPU resource management, and compute-efficient training strategies
 …

items.desc: Who we are At Praxa Sense, we are redefining non-invasive health monitoring with our optical innovation ALIS® – a speckle-based biosensor enabling new frontiers in remote vital sign tracking. We are looking for a curious, creative and very sharp Research Scientist who wants to fully understand what the ALIS® sensor measures, from the physics of laser speckle and tissue optics to the underlying physiology. You combine deep understanding with hands-on work: you set up measurements yourself, tinker and explore with the technology, explain what you see, and turn new insights into strong intellectual property. What you will do Deepen our understanding of the physics behind SPG and the Blood Flow Index (BFi): speckle statistics, speckle dynamics, light-tissue interaction and their relation to blood flow. Link the BFi and PPG signals to physiology: microvascular and arterial blood flow, perfusion, and pulse wave characteristics. Design and run experiments with the sensor, on the bench and in-vivo, often against reference methods such as ECG, ultrasound or blood pressure measurements. Analyze the data and explain the observed physical and physiological effects. Develop theoretical and numerical models that link measured signals to physiological parameters. Guide the next steps in IP protection: identify patentable inventions, write invention disclosures and draft patent descriptions and claims together with our patent attorney. Carry out prior-art searches and support freedom-to-operate analyses. What we are looking for Msc or PhD in Physics, Applied Physics, Physical Chemistry or Biomedical Engineering, with a background in photonics, optoelectronics, light-matter interaction or biomedical optics. Experience with speckle, DCS, LSCI or PPG is a strong plus, but not required. Experience translating research into applied health sensing, for example as a research engineer at a medtech or consumer health company. Strong understanding of coherent light scattering and tissue optics, or the ability to master these quickly. Solid knowledge of human physiology, in particular cardiovascular physiology and hemodynamics. Hands-on experimental skills. Data analysis and modelling skills in Python. Demonstrable interest in intellectual property, ideally with experience in invention disclosures or patent texts. Ability to write clear, precise technical text and to separate what is truly novel from what is known. Fluent in English; Dutch is a plus. What we offer Salary matching your experience with potential equity participation. 25 holiday days per year, additional special leave days for big life events such as weddings, moving houses and funerals. 7% of your salary as a contribution to life annuity. Free office lunch on Fridays. Fun company outings, but no unnecessary obligations. If you live more than 5km from the office: travel cost reimbursement of €0,23 per kilometer, also (or especially) when you come by bike. Work-from-home reimbursement so you can also drink quality coffee at home. Hybrid work culture: in-person collaboration at the Groot Handelsgebouw in Rotterdam at least 3 days/week, work from home when you need to focus (or do some laundry). Direct collaboration with experts in optics, signal processing, and data science and very friendly and ambitious colleagues. The satisfaction of contributing to technology that directly improves health monitoring. To apply: Send your CV and motivation to hr@praxasense.com. Submissions without a motivational letter will result in automatic rejection. They reproduce DFT at a fraction of its cost and have become a standard tool to simulate materials. Our team studies how to train these potentials and how to quantify their uncertainty. Different potentials make different predictions, and so does the same potential trained with different random seeds.

Prior Labs | Berlin, Freiburg, NYC | ONSITE | Full-time | https://priorlabs.ai 
We build foundation models for tables. Since July we're an independent lab inside SAP with €1B+ over four years; models stay open-weight and research stays public.
We're hiring engineers:
Infrastructure Engineer - multi-cluster GPU training on Slurm, GCP today and more providers in 2027. The compute budget is tens of millions a year, and you own it.
ML Engineer, Backend - own inference end to end: latency, batching and memory on million-row inputs, across our API, customer VPCs and open weights.
Full Stack Developer - the product where data scientists, agents and our models meet. TypeScript/React + Python/FastAPI.
Also hiring: Research Scientists and Research Engineers (Foundation Model), Applied Scientist (NYC), PhD research interns, GTM and ops roles. We sponsor visas and help with relocation.
~45 people, led by Frank Hutter, advised by Yann LeCun and Bernhard Schölkopf.

items.desc:
Who we are
 Helsing is a defence AI company with the mission is to protect our liberal democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards. We believe we have a responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI and take this responsibility seriously. 
 We are an ambitious and committed team of software and deployment engineers, AI specialists and customer-facing programme managers. We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems today.
 We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications. 
 The role
 At Helsing you will work at the intersection of machine learning and signal processing on RF data, helping build the AI capabilities inside our electronic warfare systems: models that detect, classify, and reason about RF signals in congested, contested spectrum. The data is messy, irregular, and adversarial. Output runs on real platforms, under hard latency and compute budgets. What you build has to survive contact with the deployment target.
 You will own problems end-to-end: read the literature, prototype on real recorded data, push to the edge, watch it run. You will work in a small research team alongside RF and hardware engineers and the operators using the system.
 Current focus areas include self-supervised representation learning on signal data, deinterleaving and emitter identification, mode recognition, and anomaly detection on embedded hardware.
 You should apply if you
 Hold a PhD (or have an equivalent research track record) in ML, signal processing, physics, electrical engineering, or a related field, with publications at NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, ICASSP, or similar venues.
 Have shipped non-trivial ML into a real product - not just notebooks. You know what breaks between research and deployment.
 Are comfortable on irregular, noisy sequence data: temporal models, self-supervised or contrastive methods, calibration under distribution shift.
 Write clean Python, and are willing to pick up Rust where the deployment target demands it.
 Read papers and reimplement them. You can tell which results will hold up and which won't.
 Communicate research clearly to ML peers, RF engineers, and end users.
 We don't expect you to arrive with deep RF expertise. A strong ML or physics background and willingness to learn the domain alongside RF colleagues is enough.
 Note: We operate at an intersection where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points. 
 Nice to have 
 Experience with EW, SIGINT, ESM/ELINT, RWR, or radar concepts.
 Familiarity with RF signal theory at a level sufficient to talk to RF engineers (modulation, propagation, antenna patterns — see modulation-schemes).
 Experience deploying ML to edge or embedded hardware (ONNX, TensorRT, quantisation, profiling on constrained GPUs).
 Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields
 Helsing’s work is important. You’ll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns
 The work is unique. We operate in a domain that has highly unusual technical requirements and constraints, and where robustness, safety, and ethical considerations are vital. You will face unique Engineering and AI challenges that make a meaningful impact in the world
 Our work frequently takes us right up to the state of the art in technical innovation, be it reinforcement learning, distributed systems, generative AI, or deployment infrastructure. The defence industry is entering the most exciting phase of the technological development curve. Advances in our field of world are not incremental: Helsing is part of, and often leading, historic leaps forward
 In our domain, success is a matter of order-of-magnitude improvements and novel capabilities. This means we take bets, aim high, and focus on big opportunities. Despite being a relatively young company, Helsing has already been selected for multiple significant government contracts
 We actively encourage healthy, proactive, and diverse debate internally about what we do and how we choose to do it. Teams and individual engineers are trusted (and encouraged) to practise responsible autonomy and critical thinking, and to focus on outcomes, not conformity. At Helsing you will have a say in how we (and you!) work, the opportunity to engage on what does and doesn’t work, and to take ownership of aspects of our culture that you care deeply about

items.desc: At NXAI, we are building the future of AI from our hub in Linz, Austria. Our mission is to turn advanced research into real-world impact, with a focus on next-generation xLSTM models and their industrial applications. Working at the intersection of research and industry, we are creating a leading center for AI innovation in the region. As a Robotics Research Engineer at NXAI, you will take our next-generation sequence models out of the lab and into the physical world. You will work at the intersection of foundation model research and embodied AI, building the perception, reasoning and action pipelines that let robots understand instructions, interpret their environment and act reliably in real world settings. This is a hands-on research role: you will be as comfortable fine-tuning a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model as you are debugging a policy on real hardware. You will work closely with our core research team to explore how xLSTM can push robotic foundation models beyond today's state of the art. Key Responsibilities Own physical robot and workstation uptime, including the integration of new sensors, compute units, and end-effectors, while iteratively modifying setups to improve experimental throughput. Architect and maintain fault-tolerant, high-throughput pipelines for multi-modal data ingestion, incorporating automated data validation, quality scoring, and versioning. Establish standardized, reproducible real-world evaluation protocols and metrics (success rate, task completion time, out-of-distribution robustness) to systematically benchmark policy progression. Conduct end-to-end root-cause analysis across the entire robotics stack, diagnosing bottlenecks spanning physical sensors, actuators, network/communication overhead, inference runtimes, and training distribution shift. Serve as the critical feedback loop between physical deployment and algorithm design, turning empirical hardware failures and edge cases into actionable research directions and data strategy updates. Fine-tune, optimize, and deploy modern learning-based policies (e.g., imitation learning, diffusion policies, vision-language-action models) into real-time, low-latency control loops on physical hardware. What We Ask 2+ years of industry experience training and deploying robot learning models, or an MSc/PhD with research focused on policy learning. Demonstrated track record of deploying and debugging neural network policies on physical robots (manipulators, mobile bases, or humanoids), including managing safety constraints and hardware/sensor calibration. Advanced proficiency in Python and PyTorch.. Practical proficiency with Linux environments, modern robotics communication middleware (ROS 1/2), and containerization tools (Docker, Singularity). Strong foundational understanding of imitation learning paradigms (e.g., Behavior Cloning, Action Chunking with Transformers [ACT], Diffusion Policy) and dataset curation strategies. Discipline in designing reproducible physical benchmarking protocols (success metrics, failure categorization, out-of-distribution testing). Hardware capabilities (sensing, tooling, compute, and mounting) continuously evolve to directly eliminate data-collection bottlenecks and unlock new research investigations. Data collection: a new operator can collect a usable dataset on a robot within a day, with documented setup, synced cameras and joints, and only a small share of episodes discarded for quality issues. Evaluation and baselines: a written eval protocol with a fixed number of trials per task (e.g., 20+), plus success rates reported for a baseline policy and a VLA fine-tune, reproducible when rerun. Benchmark: a defined set of tasks (e.g., 3–5) with baseline numbers for each, used by the team to compare new methods. items.desc: Paris, 75, FR ABOUT CFM Founded in 1991, we are a global quantitative and systematic asset management firm applying a scientific approach to finance to develop alternative investment strategies that create value for our clients. We value innovation, dedication, collaboration, and the ability to make an impact. Together, we create a stimulating environment for talented and passionate experts in research, technology, and business to explore new ideas and challenge existing assumptions. Your Role The Data-Human-Insights team works across a wide variety of structured and unstructured datasets, from time series to graphs, assessing their predictive power and preparing them for modeling. As data scientists, we work closely with the Research team to extract valuable insights from the data. Accurate and efficient time series forecasting is central to CFM's work, and it sits at one of the most important intersections between the expertise and interests of researchers and data scientists. The literature is large and growing, spanning econometrics, operations research, traditional machine learning, deep learning and generative AI. In recent years, time series foundation models have become a performant and popular option for a wide variety of forecasting tasks. The goal of this internship is to survey and evaluate existing time series foundation models against CFM's needs, and to identify where they can improve on the forecasting methods we use today. Building on this evaluation, you will research, propose and implement techniques to adapt these models to our purposes, and help plan and develop their integration into different workloads across the firm. You will be expected to understand, implement, evaluate and operationalize contemporary research on time series foundation models, and to test it as rigorously out of sample as any other model we use Key Responsibilities Survey the academic and industry literature on time series foundation models and identify the most relevant approaches. Benchmark existing models against current forecasting methods, including classical approaches (ARIMA, GARCH, state space models). Propose and implement techniques to improve these models for CFM's use cases (e.g. fine-tuning with LoRA, quantization, architectural adaptations). Evaluate models rigorously out of sample, avoiding look-ahead bias and data leakage. Aggregate and join heterogeneous data sources and process huge datasets efficiently. Help plan and develop the integration of selected models into different workloads. Write clear documentation and reports on your methodology, results and limitations, and present them to the team and, occasionally, to researchers. Your Skills You are in final year of a Master's degree or engineering school program in data science, statistics, applied mathematics, computer science or a related field. You are proficient in Python, pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch and Matplotlib. You have experience manipulating and modeling time series, with a solid grounding in classical approaches such as ARIMA, GARCH and state space models. You have experience with modern deep learning and generative AI architectures and techniques, such as transformers, attention mechanisms, positional encodings, fine-tuning with LoRA, and quantization. You understand how to evaluate forecasting models out of sample, including how to avoid look-ahead bias and data leakage. You can aggregate and join heterogeneous data sources and manipulate huge datasets. You can conduct independent literature reviews, propose new ideas, and synthesize results, challenges and proposals. You are proactive, with a drive to experiment and propose original ideas. You communicate results and limitations clearly and concisely. You are fluent in English. You are available for a six-month internship. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES STATEMENT We are continuously striving to be an equal opportunity employer and we prohibit any discrimination based on sex, disability, origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, race, or religion. We believe that our diversity, breadth of experience, and multiple points of view are among the leading factors in our success. CFM is a signatory of the Women Empowerment Principles.

items.desc:
OUR MISSION

Aleph Alpha is one of the few companies in Europe doing serious foundation model pre-training like our recently released Kolibri-1 model https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1. Our customers - in finance, manufacturing, public administration - need models that understand German, meet European regulatory requirements, and work reliably in high-stakes settings. We're building that in Heidelberg.



TEAM CULTURE

At Aleph Alpha, we foster a culture built on ownership, autonomy, and empowerment. Teams and individual contributors are trusted to take responsibility for their work and drive meaningful impact. We maintain a flat organizational structure with efficient, supportive management that enables quick decision-making, open communication, and a strong sense of shared purpose.

We believe a strong engineering culture is the key to model training success. We like Extreme Programming and favor trunk-based development. We often mob-program, which keeps us aligned and means we always learn from each other.





ABOUT THE ROLE

As an AI R&D Engineer in Model Training (f/m/d), you will join our model training team in Heidelberg or Berlin. Most of the team is based in Heidelberg. The model training team is building and improving our model training pipeline, which has been used to train Kolibri. 

 - You will work across our full stack. Some weeks you might be optimizing how training loads are scheduled on our cluster and making the pipeline more robust and performant so we can iterate faster. Other weeks, you will be enabling large-scale code execution for reinforcement learning. And at other times, you might dig deep into our evaluation codebase to lift inference throughput on evals.

 - No two days are the same. Things move fast, and your ability to focus and prioritize is what lets you unblock the team day-to-day while designing the high-quality tooling and infrastructure that speeds us up long-term.

 - We're still building out our training pipeline and infrastructure. Some pieces exist, some do not, and you will have real influence on what gets built and how. Your work directly shapes how quickly we can experiment and improve our models.

 - Identifying issues and taking initiative is what drives our day-to-day work.

 - Working mode, design decisions, priorities are all done in your team together with your team mates. 
   The strongest teams often use highly collaborative techniques, like mob or pair programming.

 - Due to the highly collaborative nature of our work you are expected to be on-site at least two days a week. If you are in Berlin, you should expect to travel around every second month for a few days to Heidelberg.

 - We are specifically looking to strengthen the Software Engineering in the teams which are research heavy. Major points include improving the maintainability of our code through tests and design & architecture changes.


REQUIREMENTS

 - At its core, you need to be able to dive into a codebase, change the behavior as necessary, and after the change the code should be better tested and easier to understand than before.

 - As such we look for candidates for an understanding of how to design for low coupling and high cohesion paired with the ability to incrementally refactor.

 - Experience with the following technologies is likely to be helpful:
   
   - Test Driven Development (TDD)
   
   - Trunk based development
   
   - Continuous integration
   
   - Domain Driven Design


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Most of our code is in Python, there is also the occasional Rust codebase.

 - Large parts of our training pipeline are built on top of Kubernetes.

 - We do not hire for skills in a particular technology or language, but rather ability to learn and mindset, yet experience with these technologies is a plus.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Become part of an AI revolution!

 - 30 days of paid vacation

 - Access to a variety of fitness & wellness offerings via Wellhub https://wellhub.com/de-de/

 - Mental health support through nilo.health http://nilo.health/

 - Substantially subsidized company pension plan for your future security

 - Subsidized Germany-wide transportation ticket

 - Budget for additional technical equipment

 - Flexible working hours for better work-life balance and hybrid working model

 - JobRad® https://www.jobrad.org/ Bike Lease

Note: We welcome applicants at every stage of their career. Your drive and willingness to learn are far more important to us than strict experience requirements.

items.desc: Overview: Certara accelerates the potential of bringing medicines to market and to patients using biosimulation software, technology, and services to transform traditional drug discovery and development. Our clients include more than 2,400 biopharmaceutical companies, academic institutions, and regulatory agencies across 70 countries. Our goal is to enable the life sciences industry’s use of data, modeling, and analytics to make better decisions across the various phases of discovery and drug development. Our software and scientists incorporate modern advances in scientific understanding, drug development experience, data analysis, and AI resulting in significant opportunities to decrease the cost and increase the probability of success for new drug approval and commercialization. We have an opening for a highly motivated Research Scientist to work on research and development of mechanistic models for small and large molecules implemented within various Simcyp products. The Scientist will apply physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modelling and in vitro-in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) approaches to translate in vitro, preclinical and clinical data into predictive models for both small molecules and biologics. Suitable candidates will have hands-on experience in PBPK modelling and simulation of small molecules and/or large molecules, including the collation and interpretation of in vitro, preclinical and clinical data, model development, and verification of model performance against observed clinical data. Experience in mechanistic ADME modelling, IVIVE of drug metabolism and transport, target-mediated drug disposition, or the disposition of therapeutic proteins and other novel modalities would be particularly appreciated. The successful candidate is expected to maintain an up-to-date knowledge of the latest scientific developments, disseminate research results, and actively engage with peers and clients within industry, academia and regulatory agencies. The role is a blended research, client facing and software development role. Experience working in drug discovery and development within the pharmaceutical industry is desirable. items.desc: Research Engineer, Reinforcement Learning Seed-stage AI for Science Lab | London (on-site) Compensation: £130k-£220k + equity package Overview RL has pushed coding and maths forward quickly. Biology is harder because evidence is incomplete, feedback is slow, and a model can look like it’s improving while quietly gaming the reward. This role exists to build training setups where that can’t happen. The lab is a small, seed-funded founding team in London. They train frontier models as agents on real scientific work: forming hypotheses, planning experiments, reading results. You’d be one of the first technical hires. There’s no inherited stack, so you’d help set the tooling and research standards. What you’ll do Train agents with RL on multi-step problems across biology, drug discovery and clinical research Build environments where agents query biological data, call scientific tools and act on the output Design reward functions and evals that separate real progress from reward hacking Build rollout, distributed training and eval infrastructure so a few people can run large experiments Own experiments end-to-end, from design through debugging to reproducible results Work with in-house scientists to turn open biological questions into tasks with checkable outcomes What you’ll need Hands-on experience training models or agents with RL A first-principles grasp of reward design, credit assignment, exploration and training stability Strong engineering – you write reliable, fast code and can debug from learning dynamics down to GPU performance Sound experimental judgement: you know why a run failed and what to try next Comfort owning ambiguous problems in a team of a handful of people Willingness to work five days a week in the London office Optional Bonus Agentic systems work: tool use, multi-step reasoning or long-horizon tasks Biology or healthcare background – useful, not expected PhD or publications in RL, post-training or scientific ML Seniority is open, from strong early-career engineers to senior researchers. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted within 48 hours.

items.desc: Job Description Who we are Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables. We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level. We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun. In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years. About The Role You will have ownership over designing, building, and scaling the core systems that bring Prior Labs' foundation models to the world. This is a unique opportunity to make fundamental architectural decisions, establish engineering best practices from the ground up, and profoundly shape the technical direction for serving state-of-the-art AI. TabPFN does its learning in the forward pass, and it now handles datasets in the millions of rows. Making that fast, reliable, and affordable is an exciting engineering challenge. You'll work directly with world-class AI researchers, translating cutting-edge models into scalable production systems. This role offers significant autonomy and impact, with clear paths to specialize in areas you're passionate about (like inference optimization and core backend systems) or grow into a technical leadership position as our team expands. You won't just be implementing features; you'll be building the backbone of our company. What you'll work on Own Inference: Own the serving path end-to-end: latency, throughput, batching, memory behavior on large inputs, and cost per prediction. Our models serve through our managed API, inside customer VPCs, and as self-hosted open weights, and you’ll have an impact across the board. Architect & Design: Design robust, scalable, and secure backend systems and production-grade APIs for serving our foundation models. Build & Implement: Develop high-quality, maintainable code for core backend services. Own Infrastructure: Design, deploy, and manage core infrastructure on cloud platforms, focusing on reliability, monitoring, observability, and cost-efficiency. Ensure Compliance & Security: Implement secure, GDPR-compliant systems, including data storage, access control, usage tracking, and quota management. Champion Best Practices: Drive high standards for testing, CI/CD, documentation, and security within the engineering team. You may be a good fit if you have 3+ years of professional experience in machine learning and backend engineering, with a proven track record of managing production infrastructure. Proven experience deploying and operating machine learning models in production, with a strong understanding of how models behave and fail under real traffic. Strong, hands-on experience designing and building production-grade APIs and backend services. Significant experience building and operating services on cloud platforms, with GCP preferred. Strong, hands-on experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using tools like Terraform. Significant experience with containerization and orchestration technologies (Docker, Kubernetes). Proficiency in Python. What sets you apart Experience building or managing infrastructure specifically for machine learning (MLOps, model serving frameworks, feature stores, data pipelines). Deep experience with inference optimization (quantization, compilation, dynamic batching, caching strategies, interplay with distributed computing). Experience with PyTorch and FastAPI specifically. Contributions to relevant open-source projects. Life at Prior Labs You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right. Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. But great people come from everywhere, and in exceptional cases we're open to remote, which usually means frequent travel to one of our offices. Wherever you're based, the whole company comes together regularly for offsites to build and celebrate together. Our Commitments The best products and teams are built by people with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds. We welcome applications from all identities and walks of life - …

items.desc: We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Research Fellow to join the Salah Elias laboratory at the University of Southampton and lead the experimental research within a BBSRC-funded project investigating mechanisms of mammary epithelial morphogenesis through AI-integrated human organoid models and predictive cell fate mapping. This is an excellent opportunity to shape an innovative project and develop a distinctive interdisciplinary profile at the interface of cell and developmental biology, human organoid models, advanced imaging, molecular phenotyping and computational biology. About The Project The project combines patient-derived mammary organoids, high-resolution 3D/4D imaging, single-cell transcriptomics and AI-driven analysis and modelling to uncover mechanisms governing epithelial morphogenesis. At its core is a fundamental question: how do polarised cell divisions coordinate luminogenesis with cell fate and differentiation to build and maintain functional epithelial architecture? By addressing this question in physiologically relevant human models, the project aims to define how these mechanisms safeguard epithelial integrity and how their disruption leads to abnormal tissue organisation. You will take a central role in the scientific development of this ambitious programme, including experimental design, data analysis and interpretation. You will use patient-derived human mammary organoids and gene loss-of-function approaches, together with high-resolution 3D/4D fluorescence imaging, fate mapping, advanced quantitative analysis, and single-cell RNA sequencing, to connect molecular and cellular mechanisms with cell fate and tissue architecture. A major strength of the project is the integration of experimental and computational biology. Working with computational researchers, you will integrate multimodal imaging and transcriptomic data into AI-driven mechanistic and predictive models to determine how changes at the level of individual cells influence tissue-level organisation and function. About You You will have a PhD, or be close to completing one, in cell biology, developmental biology, stem cell biology or a related discipline. You will have strong experimental experience across several relevant areas of cell and developmental biology, which may include organoid or mammalian cell culture, epithelial biology, high-resolution fluorescence microscopy and molecular biology. Experience in advanced automated or semi-automated quantitative image analysis would be particularly valuable. An understanding of computational or mathematical modelling would be advantageous, but is not essential. You will be a creative and collaborative scientist with a proactive, analytical approach and enthusiasm for interdisciplinary research. You should be able to plan and conduct rigorous experiments, interpret data, troubleshoot methods and communicate findings clearly. Alongside leading the experimental research, you will contribute scientific ideas and interpretation, support collaborative projects, help develop grant proposals, prepare research for publication in international peer-reviewed journals, train colleagues in new methods and advise on scientific protocols. You will bring excellent interpersonal skills and work constructively with colleagues and collaborators across disciplines. What We Offer You will join a collaborative, multidisciplinary and supportive research environment bringing together expertise in mammary biology, organoids, advanced imaging, single-cell biology, AI and computational modelling. You will have access to state-of-the-art microscopy, flow-cytometry and high-performance computing facilities, multidisciplinary training and career-development opportunities. The University of Southampton offers a range of benefits, including a generous holiday allowance and additional University closure days. We support flexible working and a healthy work–life balance, alongside access to the Universities Superannuation Scheme (USS), subsidised health and fitness facilities and a range of staff discounts. The post is offered on a three-year fixed-term basis. For informal enquiries, please contact Dr Salah Elias at S.K.Elias@soton.ac.uk.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Overview Are you a passionate researcher eager to bridge the gap between advanced engineering and clinical practice to tackle a transformative healthcare challenge? We have an exciting opportunity in the School of Mechanical, Aerospace and Civil Engineering for a Research Associate to apply their skills in biomedical engineering to revolutionize haemodialysis and make a profound impact on global health. You will join the Thermofluids Group at the University of Sheffield, working in close collaboration with experts in the School of Medicine and Population Health and Sheffield Teaching Hospitals. As a key member of this interdisciplinary project, you will lead the design, assembly, and clinical validation of a novel dialyser prototype. You will be responsible for testing the prototype using blood-mimicking fluids and, ultimately, human blood to assess cleaning efficiency, clotting risk, and biocompatibility. This role offers a unique opportunity to apply fundamental engineering principles to real-world physiological conditions. You will work in close collaboration with two other Research Associates focusing on numerical simulations and experimental fluid dynamics, contributing directly to a greener, more efficient future for nephrology. Main duties and responsibilities Lead the assembly of the prototype, ensuring tight tolerances for spinning components, robust sealing, and integration of semi-permeable membranes. You will troubleshoot technical issues during assembly to ensure the prototype is ready for testing. Conduct rigorous solute removal efficiency tests using Human Peripheral Simulated Blood Plasma (BZ464). You will measure the clearance rates of key metabolites, including urea, creatinine, and phosphate, to optimize the operational parameters of the dialyser. Manage the ethical procurement and testing of voluntarily donated human blood to assess biocompatibility. You will evaluate the prototype for fibrin strands, check transmembrane pressure, and analyse blood samples for clotting and haemolysis markers, ensuring safety standards are met. Work closely with the fluids engineering PDRAs to translate simulation and experimental results into physiological insights. You will actively participate in weekly meetings with renal clinicians at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals to interpret data and refine the device design based on clinical feedback. Maintain meticulous records of experimental methodologies and results in compliance with clinical governance frameworks. You will contribute to the writing of high-impact journal publications, present outcomes at international medical and engineering conferences, and participate in public engagement events regarding sustainable nephrology. Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post. Person Specification Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and is respected. Even if your past experience doesn't match perfectly with this role's criteria, your contribution is valuable, and we encourage you to apply. Please ensure that you reference the application criteria in the application statement when you apply. Criteria Essential or desirable Stage(s) assessed at A PhD (or nearing completion) in Biomedical Engineering, or a closely related physical science/engineering field. Essential Application Hands-on experience in experimental biomedical engineering, with proven expertise in designing, assembling, troubleshooting complex prototype hardware, and testing medical devices or filtration systems. Desirable Application/Interview Hands-on experience handling biological fluids (including blood and blood substitutes), coupled with practical expertise in biochemical analysis and blood compatibility assays such as hemolysis and clotting markers. Desirable Application/Interview Proven ability to conduct high-level scientific research independently. Essential Application/Interview A proven track record of publishing high-quality scientific papers in reputable journals. Our work at NVIDIA is dedicated towards a computing model focused on visual and AI computing. For two decades, NVIDIA has pioneered visual computing, the art and science of computer graphics, with our invention of the GPU. The GPU has also shown to be spectacularly effective at solving some of the most complex problems in computer science. Today, NVIDIA’s GPU simulates human intelligence, running deep learning algorithms and acting as the brain of computers, robots and self-driving cars that can perceive and understand the world. (f) Advanced multi-agent systems including co-ordination, negotiation and mechanism design. items.desc: The GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences is one of the world's leading institutions in the field of geosciences. As part of the Helmholtz Association, Germany's largest research organisation, we address global challenges such as natural hazards, climate change and the sustainable use of resources. In doing so, we combine cutting-edge research with social relevance. Our international staff - around 1,200 employees and approx. 500 guests - work in a multidisciplinary way and with a unique infrastructure to research the dynamic processes of the Earth system. Our vision: “Taking the pulse of the Earth to safeguard a habitable planet.” For section 1.4 Remote Sensing and Geoinformatics (department “Geodesy”), we are looking for a: Research Scientist (f_m_x) - Radar Remote Sensing of Mining-Induced Deformation and Landslide Hazards Reference Number 11579 Are you an innovative researcher interested in developing next-generation radar remote sensing methods to monitor geohazards? Do you have experience processing and analysing InSAR time series, and are you keen to develop new approaches to evaluate ground-motion hazards related to mining and landslides? Would you like to work with the latest satellite radar missions, including NISAR and ALOS-4, and contribute to developing advanced Earth observation methods for geohazard assessment in Chile? Are you an enthusiastic researcher ready to work in an interdisciplinary and international team? Then we would like to have you on board! Your research will focus on developing and applying advanced radar remote sensing methods to monitor mining-induced ground deformation and landslide hazards in Chile. The project will exploit the rapidly developing capabilities of satellite radar observations, including data from the latest NISAR and ALOS-4 missions, along with established Sentinel-, TerraSAR-X and other SAR datasets for detecting, characterising, and interpreting deformation associated with mining operations and slope instabilities. Your responsibilities: As a researcher, you will develop innovative methods for radar remote sensing of mining-induced deformation and landslide hazards. items.desc: As a public weather and climate expert, Météo-France is at your side to contribute to your day-to-day safety and help you make the best decisions in a changing climate. Faced with dangerous weather episodes that are even more intense and more frequent as a result of climate change, our missions in the service of your safety are crucial. We mobilize our expertise and our scientific and technological excellence to help you anticipate and adapt to challenging weather and climate phenomena. Find us online: https://meteofrance.com/carte-didentite-de-meteo-france The DESR brings together the research entities of Météo-France (mainly CNRM, SAFIRE and LACy), the Ecole Nationale de la Météorologie and the shared administrative and IT support services (PGA). The CNRM is a Joint Research Unit (UMR 3589) under the joint supervision of Météo-France and CNRS. The CNRM conducts research in the field of meteorology and climate, from the observation, understanding and modelling of processes to the development of weather forecasting and climate projection systems that can be transferred to Météo-France's operational services. The GMAP (Groupe de Modélisation et d'Assimilation pour la Prévision - Modelling and Assimilation Group for Forecasting), based in Toulouse, is one of the CNRM's 6 research groups or centres. Its mission is to maintain and develop Météo-France's operational numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems and to conduct research in preparation for future versions. Why join us? Embark on a stimulating adventure in the service of all, alongside men and women committed to the daily challenges posed to our society by the weather and climate. And Enjoy The Following Benefits flexible working hours, RTT, telecommuting, administrative restaurant or luncheon voucher, 75% contribution to public transport, contribution to health insurance, sports and cultural associations depending on the site (climbing, gym, pottery, theater, etc.). Other benefits await you, come and discover them! This position is part of the WeatherGenerator european project (https://weathergenerator.eu/) led by ECMWF. The objective of the WeatherGenerator is to improve weather and climate predictions, enhance renewable energy planning, and provide better tools for mitigating the effect of extreme events like floods and heatwaves. It combines the latest machine learning with high performance computing, creating a robust tool for scientific discovery and real-world applications. Building on the key concepts of large-scale representation learning, WeatherGenerator is meant to be a foundation model, trained on multiple datasets, from reanalyses to satellite observations. The resulting model will be accessible through finetuning for a range of applications in the area of Earth system science. Meteo-France is taking part in this international endeavour and aims at applying the WeatherGenerator framework to regional weather forecasting, with a focus on the accurate modelling of under-meso-scale extreme events over metropolitan France. Building on the WeatherGenerator model, the aim of the present position is to evaluate its capabilities for high-resolution weather forecasting over western Europe. The Main Objectives Are The Following Fine-tune the foundation model on Météo-France Arome data ; Evaluate its performances, and benchmark against other weather forecasting models developed byMeteo-France AI-weather forecasting research team ; Implement and evaluate strategies to use the WeatherGenerator in a probabilistic forecasting setting ; Work collaboratively with the international project partners ; Contribute to workshops and hackathons organized by the projet, and more generally take part to dissemination activities (including the production of project deliverables and scientific publications). Additional information This position is open to people with disabilities. Office hours. Fixed-term contract of 18 months. Remote work available: 1 day a week maximum.

items.desc: Job Title: Member of Technical Staff, Robotics & Embodied AI Research Job Type: Full-time Location: Remote The Role We're hiring a Robotics Researcher to drive frontier research in embodied AI, robot learning, and physical AI systems. This is a hands-on research role focused on advancing vision-language-action (VLA) models, generalist robot policies, world models, and emerging approaches to embodied intelligence. You'll design and execute end-to-end robotics experiments, leveraging real-world data, simulation, and human-in-the-loop systems to evaluate and improve robot performance. You'll independently explore promising research directions and collaborate with leading AI and robotics teams to translate experimental findings into scalable solutions. What You'll Do Lead frontier robotics research across VLA models, generalist policies, world models, and emerging embodied AI approaches. Design end-to-end experimentation systems spanning teleoperation, data collection, simulation, policy deployment, and real-world evaluation. Develop high-fidelity simulations using real-world data to evaluate robot policies and validate performance in physical environments. Leverage flow, our human-in-the-loop annotation platform, to structure and scale robotics datasets from egocentric video, teleoperation demonstrations, and multimodal sensor data. Investigate model limitations, failure modes, and sim-to-real gaps to develop improved datasets, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies. Rapidly prototype and validate novel approaches to robot learning, policy optimization, and embodied intelligence. Independently identify high-impact research opportunities and lead projects from initial exploration through experimentation and scalable implementation. What We're Looking For Strong background in robotics, embodied AI, robot learning, computer vision, or applied machine learning research. Hands-on experience developing, training, or evaluating robot learning models, including VLA models, imitation learning, or generalist policies. Proficiency in Python and experience with robotics or ML frameworks such as PyTorch, ROS, or simulation environments. Experience designing robotics experiments involving real-world data collection, simulation, policy evaluation, or hardware deployment. Understanding of robot learning methodologies, multimodal perception, and sim-to-real transfer challenges. Ability to analyze model behavior, identify failure modes, and translate research findings into measurable performance improvements. Strong research ownership, experimental judgment, and ability to independently execute complex technical projects. Strong technical communication and collaboration skills across research and engineering teams. Preferred Qualifications Experience with world models, reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or diffusion-based robot policies. Hands-on experience with teleoperation, robotics hardware, sensor integration, or real-world policy deployment. Familiarity with robotics simulators such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, or comparable environments. Experience building multimodal robotics datasets from egocentric video, robot trajectories, or sensor data. Prior experience at a leading robotics or frontier AI research lab. Contributions to robotics research publications, open-source frameworks, or benchmark development.
