The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices, for applications such as dynamic awareness, hearing augmentation, agentic perception, voice pickup, content enhancement, and ones we haven’t even thought of yet. You will work with experts
items.desc: At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound. Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation. Job Description Research Scientist — Audio Source Separation Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices, for applications such as dynamic awareness, hearing augmentation, agentic perception, voice pickup, content enhancement, and ones we haven’t even thought of yet. You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms. You will develop next-generation algorithms that isolate, extract, or suppress individual sound sources from microphone recordings, sometimes augmented by other sensor signals. Applications include voice pickup, hearing augmentation, and new audio experiences that must ultimately run in real time on physical devices. Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next. Responsibilities Research, prototype, train, and evaluate novel source separation and extraction algorithms for speech and other real-world sounds. Develop approaches for single- and multi-microphone recordings, including spatial cues and optional auxiliary sensors. Investigate robust separation in challenging conditions such as overlapping talkers, noise, reverberation, and motion. Evaluate perceptual quality, separation performance, generalization, latency, memory, and computational requirements. Collaborate with DSP and embedded software teams to deploy models in real-time demonstrations and product platforms; contribute to patents and conference papers. Education Graduate degree (MS or PhD) in machine learning, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent research experience. Strong knowledge of audio DSP, time-frequency methods, and microphone array or spatial signal processing. Experience training and evaluating audio models in PyTorch; proficiency in Python and familiarity with C/C++ is a plus. Understanding of objective and perceptual evaluation methods and the tradeoffs involved in real-time low-power inference. Experience with multimodal or sensor-conditioned separation, ONNX/TFLite, or embedded deployment is a plus. Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required. The hiring range for this position in the primary work location of Framingham, Massachusetts is: $165,400-$227,500.The hiring range for other Bose work locations may vary. items.title: Research Scientist
items.card: You will play a key role in advancing this technology, applying molecular biology and microbiology approaches to engineer improved Salmonella phage-propagation strains and evaluate phage efficacy in a pig infection model. The research will combine bacterial genetics, phage biology, microbiology and host-pathogen interactions to generate findings with significant potential for translation into practical applications.
items.desc: Applications Close: 04 December 2026 Salary: £39,000 to £46,500 per annum depending on qualifications and experience Contract Length: 24 months Applications are invited for an exciting opportunity to join the research groups of Professor Rob Kingsley and Professor Evelien Adriaenssens at Quadram Institute Bioscience, Norwich. We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Postdoctoral Research Scientist to contribute to an innovative research programme developing novel bacteriophage-based approaches to control Salmonella infections in pigs. The Research Opportunity: Antimicrobial resistance represents a major global challenge and bacteriophages (phages) offer considerable potential as alternative antimicrobials. Our research has established a functional genomics approach to enhance antimicrobial activity. You will play a key role in advancing this technology, applying molecular biology and microbiology approaches to engineer improved Salmonella phage-propagation strains and evaluate phage efficacy in a pig infection model. The research will combine bacterial genetics, phage biology, microbiology and host-pathogen interactions to generate findings with significant potential for translation into practical applications. This is an opportunity to contribute to impactful, translational research within a collaborative academic environment, with the expectation that findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications. The role and responsibilities: As a Postdoctoral Research Scientist, you will lead experimental work to develop, characterise and evaluate improved approaches for bacteriophage production and the control of Salmonella infection. Your responsibilities will include: Applying molecular biology and microbiology techniques to investigate bacterial and phage biology. Evaluating the antimicrobial efficacy of bacteriophage preparations in a pig infection model. Assessing Salmonella infection and efficacy of phage intervention. Analysing, interpreting and communicating experimental findings. You will work closely with the supervisory team and wider project partners, contributing to the development of a promising technology with potential applications in animal health and antimicrobial stewardship. Professional development and career opportunities: This position offers an excellent opportunity to develop your scientific expertise within a leading academic research environment, working at the interface of fundamental microbiology and translational research. You will gain expertise in Salmonella and bacteriophage biology, bacterial genetic engineering and host-pathogen interactions. You will also develop transferable skills in scientific communication, collaborative research, project delivery and the translation of research innovations towards commercial application. We place considerable importance on personal and professional development aligned with your individual research interests, career aspirations and project objectives. The ideal candidate: We are looking for a highly motivated and creative scientist with a PhD in microbiology or a related life sciences discipline, together with an interest in bacterial genetics, bacteriophage biology and host-pathogen interactions. Experience in Salmonella genetics, bacteriophage research or host-pathogen interactions would be advantageous but is not essential. Training and support will be provided in relevant techniques and areas of the research programme. Above all, we are seeking an enthusiastic scientist with a genuine passion for research and innovation. Additional information: This is a full-time post for a contract of 24 months. Salary on appointment will be within the range £39,000 to £46,500 per annum depending on qualifications and experience. A starting salary of £40,100 is guaranteed for candidates who can evidence their PhD certificate at appointment; those awaiting confirmation of their PhD award will be appointed at £39,000 until evidence is provided. For further information and details of how to apply contact the Human Resources team on 01603 450814 or nbi.recruitment@nbi.ac.uk quoting reference 1006242. This role meets the criteria for a visa application, and we encourage all qualified candidates to apply. Please contact the Human Resources Team if you have any questions regarding your application or visa options. We are committed to equity, diversity and inclusion, and welcome applications from all sectors of society. The Institute values of Respect, Innovation, Collaboration and Excellence are at the heart of all we do, and we expect all employees to share and display these values. To support our commitment, we have a range of family, faith and diversity friendly working arrangements to help all staff achieve excellence in their area of work. As a Disability Confident employer, we guarantee to offer an interview to all disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for this vacancy. About the Quadram Institute: The Quadram Institute …

items.desc: About The Role At Together AI, you’ll build and operate one of the world’s largest GPU fleets used for frontier model training and inference. This isn’t a traditional infrastructure role—we’re looking for engineers who love building systems, automating everything, and solving problems at massive scale. If you enjoy writing software more than clicking dashboards, obsess over eliminating manual work, and want to build infrastructure that manages tens of thousands of GPUs autonomously, we’d love to talk. Hybrid at our office in Amsterdam or Remote in the UK. Responsibilites Design and build fleet automation systems that provision, validate, deploy, upgrade, repair, and retire GPU clusters with minimal human intervention. Build AI Infrastructure Agents that automate deployment, root-cause failures, incident triage, and autonomous remediation. Develop Fleet Intelligence platforms that continuously monitor hardware health, firmware, networking, storage, thermals, and workload performance to predict failures before they impact customers. Build software that maximizes GPU availability, utilization, performance, and reliability across thousands of accelerators. Create automated validation systems for GPUs, InfiniBand/RoCE fabrics, NVLink/NVSwitch, storage, and distributed AI workloads. Build internal platforms and developer tools that allow infrastructure to be managed through software—not manual operations. Continuously improve deployment velocity, reliability, and operational efficiency through automation. Partner closely with hardware, networking, platform, and AI teams to push the limits of AI infrastructure. Requirements 3+ years building distributed systems, infrastructure platforms, or large-scale backend software. Strong software engineering skills in Python, Go, or Rust. Experience building platforms, automation systems, or developer infrastructure. Experience with Linux, Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible, or similar infrastructure technologies. Strong systems thinking with the ability to understand problems across hardware and software. A passion for solving complex infrastructure challenges through software. An automation-first mindset—if a task is repeated, your instinct is to build a system to eliminate it. Bonus Experience GPU infrastructure, CUDA, NCCL, NVLink/NVSwitch InfiniBand or RoCE networking Bare-metal provisioning and lifecycle management Large-scale AI training or inference clusters Hardware health monitoring and predictive failure detection Distributed storage systems AI agents and autonomous infrastructure operations About Together AI Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month. Candidates are limited to 6 applications within a 90-day period, and applications beyond that limit will be automatically rejected. You may apply to additional roles 90 days after your last application. items.desc: Job Description We are looking for an AI Inference Engineer to join our growing team. We build and run the inference engine behind every Perplexity query and deploy dozens of model architectures at scale with tight latency and cost budgets. Our stack is Rust, Python, CUDA, and CuTe DSL. Responsibilities New models support. Support transformer-based retrieval, text-generation, and multimodal models in our inference infrastructure, from weight loading, request scheduling and KV-cache management to support in API Gateway. GPU kernels migration to CuTe DSL. Port our in-house CUDA kernels to NVIDIA's CuTe DSL so they run on GB200 today and are portable to Vera Rubin racks tomorrow. Rust-native serving runtime. Develop our internal Rust-based inference server to solve all Python pains and keep up with rapidly growing traffic. Performance optimisation. Profile and fix bottlenecks from network ingress through continuous batching and GPU kernels interleaving. Reliability and observability. Build dashboards, alerts, and automated remediation so we catch regressions before users do. Respond to and learn from production incidents. Who we're looking for Deep experience with GPU programming and performance work (CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS, or similar). Any other deep systems programming experience is a plus. You understand modern LLM architectures and are able to bring them up reliably in a production environment. You've built and operated production distributed systems under real load - ideally performance-critical ones. Comfortable working across languages and layers: Rust for the serving runtime, Python for model code, CUDA/CuteDSL for kernels. You own problems end-to-end. You can read a research paper on Monday, write a kernel on Wednesday, and debug a production incident on Friday. Self-directed. You do well in fast-moving environments where the path forward isn't laid out for you. Nice-to-have ML compilers and framework internals: PyTorch internals, torch.compile, custom operators. Distributed GPU communication: NCCL, NVLink, InfiniBand, RDMA libraries, model/tensor parallelism. Low-precision inference: INT8/FP8/FP4 quantization, mixed-precision serving. Profiling and debugging tools: Nsight Compute/Systems, CUDA-GDB, PTX/SASS analysis. Container orchestration: Kubernetes, GPU scheduling, autoscaling inference workloads. Qualifications 3+ years of professional software engineering experience with meaningful work on ML inference or high-performance systems. Familiarity with at least one deep learning framework (PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow). Understanding of GPU architectures (memory hierarchy, warp scheduling, tensor cores). Understanding of common LLM architectures and inference optimization techniques (e.g. quantization, speculative decoding, prefill-decode disaggregation). Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including experience and expertise. Equity: In addition to the base salary, equity may be part of the total compensation package.

items.desc: At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound. Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation. Job Description Research Scientist — Audio Source Separation Description The goal of our team is to develop novel AI-powered audio processing algorithms. The twist is that our algorithms must run in real time, on physical devices, for applications such as dynamic awareness, hearing augmentation, agentic perception, voice pickup, content enhancement, and ones we haven’t even thought of yet. You will work with experts in ML, DSP, software engineering, and psychoacoustics to prototype and implement new algorithms. You will develop next-generation algorithms that isolate, extract, or suppress individual sound sources from microphone recordings, sometimes augmented by other sensor signals. Applications include voice pickup, hearing augmentation, and new audio experiences that must ultimately run in real time on physical devices. Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge audio technology. We are looking for people passionate about machine learning and audio to help shape what comes next. Responsibilities Research, prototype, train, and evaluate novel source separation and extraction algorithms for speech and other real-world sounds. Develop approaches for single- and multi-microphone recordings, including spatial cues and optional auxiliary sensors. Investigate robust separation in challenging conditions such as overlapping talkers, noise, reverberation, and motion. Evaluate perceptual quality, separation performance, generalization, latency, memory, and computational requirements. Collaborate with DSP and embedded software teams to deploy models in real-time demonstrations and product platforms; contribute to patents and conference papers. Education Graduate degree (MS or PhD) in machine learning, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent research experience. Skills Deep hands-on experience in audio source separation, target sound extraction, speech enhancement, or related neural audio processing. Comfortable tackling complex, open-ended problems where you have to experiment with and discard many ideas before finding the right solution. Strong knowledge of audio DSP, time-frequency methods, and microphone array or spatial signal processing. Experience training and evaluating audio models in PyTorch; proficiency in Python and familiarity with C/C++ is a plus. Understanding of objective and perceptual evaluation methods and the tradeoffs involved in real-time low-power inference. Experience with multimodal or sensor-conditioned separation, ONNX/TFLite, or embedded deployment is a plus. Strong communication skills; publications at conferences such as ICASSP, Interspeech, NeurIPS, or similar are welcome but not required. At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! Our compensation is thoughtfully tailored to your skills, experience, education, and location, and goes beyond base salary. The hiring range for this position in the primary work location of Framingham, Massachusetts is: $165,400-$227,500.The hiring range for other Bose work locations may vary. In addition to competitive base pay we offer rewards including bonus programs, comprehensive health and welfare benefits, a 401(k) plan, plus exclusive perks designed to support your wellbeing, and a generous employee discount where you can immerse yourself in our products and experiences. We are a proudly independent company—driven by purpose, guided by our values, and united by a belief in the power of sound. As the world leader in audio experiences, we’re creating what’s next—pushing boundaries and delivering transformative sound experiences for people everywhere. Join us and make your next career move a mic-drop. Let’s Make Waves. ‎

items.desc:
Who we are 
 Helsing is a defence AI company. Our mission is to protect our democracies. We aim to achieve technological leadership, so that open societies can continue to make sovereign decisions and control their ethical standards. 
 As democracies, we believe we have a special responsibility to be thoughtful about the development and deployment of powerful technologies like AI. We take this responsibility seriously. 
 We are an ambitious and committed team of engineers, AI specialists and customer-facing programme managers. We are looking for mission-driven people to join our European teams – and apply their skills to solve the most complex and impactful problems. We embrace an open and transparent culture that welcomes healthy debates on the use of technology in defence, its benefits, and its ethical implications. 
 The role 
 At Helsing we deliver AI-based capabilities and the enabling foundation that allow machines to perceive and assist human decision-making. You will have the unique opportunity to shape AI capabilities in one of the most challenging sectors, where high generalisation capabilities need to be paired with hardware constraints and real-world robustness.
 You will be part of a team pushing the boundaries of autonomous robotics through reinforcement learning. Your work will focus on designing, training and deploying RL-based controllers for robots operating in complex, unstructured, and dynamic real-world environments — where classical control approaches fall short. This includes enabling robots to perceive and understand their surroundings by fusing rich sensory inputs, including vision, to inform robust and adaptive control. You will own the full pipeline from simulation to deployment, ensuring that learned policies are robust, efficient, and ready for real-world operation under tight hardware constraints. 
 You should apply if you 
 Hold an MSc or PhD in Robotics, Machine Learning, Control Engineering, or a closely related field, with a strong focus on reinforcement learning and robot control.
 Have hands-on experience training and deploying RL-based controllers on real robotic hardware, not just in simulation — you have seen your policies fall, iterate, and ultimately succeed on a physical system.
 Are deeply familiar with modern RL techniques for continuous control, including but not limited to: model-free methods (PPO, SAC, TD3), model-based RL, hierarchical RL, sim-to-real transfer strategies, domain randomisation, and curriculum learning.
 Have a solid understanding of robot dynamics, kinematics, and classical control theory (e.g. PID, model predictive control, trajectory optimisation), and know when and how to combine them with learned approaches. 
 Are proficient in building and working with physics-based simulators (e.g. MuJoCo, Isaac Gym/Isaac Lab, PyBullet, Gazebo) for training and validating RL policies.
 Possess solid software engineering skills, writing clean and well-structured code in Python and/or languages like Rust or modern C++, and have experience deploying AI software to production including testing, QA, and monitoring.
 Have excellent communication skills and the ability to report and present research findings clearly and efficiently, both internally and externally.
 Are passionate about keeping up to date with current research and enjoy re-implementing and extending state-of-the-art papers.
 Note: We operate at an intersection where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points. 
 Nice to have 
 PhD in Robotics, Reinforcement Learning, Control Engineering, or related fields, with publications in top-tier venues (e.g. CoRL, ICRA, NeurIPS, ICLR, IROS, RSS).
 Experience developing controllers for highly dynamic robotic systems operating under complex contact interactions and demanding environmental conditions.
 Experience with vision-based perception for robotics control, such as depth estimation, visual odometry, or visuomotor policy learning.
 Familiarity with low-level motor control interfaces and real-time embedded systems constraints.
 Experience with online adaptation and meta-learning techniques to enable robots to adapt to changing environmental conditions
 Experience with sensor fusion (IMU, proprioception, exteroception, vision) to inform and enhance learned control policies.
 Join Helsing and work with world-leading experts in their fields 
 Helsing’s work is important. You’ll be directly contributing to the protection of democratic countries while balancing both ethical and geopolitical concerns. 
 The work is unique. We operate in a domain that has highly unusual technical requirements and constraints, and where robustness, safety, and ethical considerations are vital. You will face unique Engineering and AI challenges that make a meaningful impact in the world.

items.card: You will work with real IQ data, radio units and production constraints, not only simulations. AI-assisted algorithms are part of the toolbox, but not the objective by themselves. We use them when they deliver a measurable improvement over classical methods in BLER, throughput or latency. Description du poste Your role : You will develop and optimise physical-layer and fronthaul processing for an O-RAN 7.2x system,
items.desc: Description de l'entreprise Free Mobile, part of the Iliad group, designs and deploys its own 5G infrastructure, from O-RAN radio units and distributed units to the user plane and Cloud RAN environment. At the heart of the DU, the physical layer and 5G fronthaul operate under hard real-time constraints. Every 0.5 ms slot must be received from the radio unit over eCPRI, processed on GPU, DSP or SIMD CPU, and delivered to the upper layers on time. This role sits at the intersection of 5G signal processing, embedded software and high-performance networking. You will work with real IQ data, radio units and production constraints, not only simulations. AI-assisted algorithms are part of the toolbox, but not the objective by themselves. We use them when they deliver a measurable improvement over classical methods in BLER, throughput or latency. Description du poste Your role : You will develop and optimise physical-layer and fronthaul processing for an O-RAN 7.2x system, from algorithm design and simulation to real-time implementation and integration with radio units. Your responsibilities will include: Developing the 5G uplink receiver chain: channel estimation, interpolation, MMSE equalisation, MIMO detection, LLR computation and LDPC decoding. Implementing PRACH detection, timing estimation and beamforming for massive MIMO. Processing O-RAN 7.2x C-plane and U-plane traffic, including eCPRI timing windows and IQ compression. Implementing real-time L1 functions in C on Linux and accelerating compute-intensive kernels with CUDA, DSP or SIMD. Building the eCPRI datapath with DPDK using poll-mode I/O, rte_flow, dedicated queues, zero-copy buffers and hardware timestamps. Optimising the complete processing chain for latency, memory usage, cache behaviour and compute load within a 0.5 ms slot budget. Validating algorithms through link-level simulations using 3GPP TDL/CDL channel models, then testing them with real IQ captures and O-RAN radio units. Measuring BLER, throughput, latency and CPU, GPU or DSP load to compare classical algorithms with AI-assisted alternatives. Investigating topics such as neural channel estimation and neural receivers when they can outperform an established baseline. Building regression tests and CI to detect performance or accuracy degradation. Contributing to architecture decisions, including GPU versus DSP or SIMD, hardware selection and accelerator integration. Working closely with radio unit, RAN, core network and operations teams. You will progressively own complete technical topics, from the mathematical model and implementation choices to their validation on the DU test bench. You will also contribute to code reviews, design documentation and open-source projects such as DPDK, Linux and U-Boot. Qualifications Your profile : We are open to both experienced engineers and high-potential graduates with strong foundations in mathematics, signal processing or embedded software. You have: An engineering degree, Master of Science or PhD in telecommunications, applied mathematics, embedded systems, computer science or a related field. Strong foundations in linear algebra, probability and digital signal processing. A good understanding of OFDM, MIMO, Fourier transforms, channel estimation, detection or channel coding. C programming skills on Linux, with an interest in memory layout, multithreading, cache behaviour and performance. Python experience with NumPy and SciPy for simulation, testing and data analysis. An interest in at least one of the following areas: 5G/LTE physical layer, O-RAN fronthaul, real-time embedded software, GPU programming, DSP/SIMD optimisation or AI for signal processing. The ability to turn mathematical concepts into code, define relevant metrics and validate the results experimentally. Good written English for reading specifications, documenting designs and reviewing code. French is a plus. Experience with CUDA, cuBLAS, cuFFT, AVX2, AVX-512, Arm NEON/SVE or fixed-point arithmetic is valuable, but you do not need to master all of them. Knowledge of DPDK, eCPRI, PTP, O-RAN 7.2x, 3GPP channel models or massive MIMO is also a plus. What matters most is your ability to understand difficult technical problems, build measurable solutions and explain the choices behind them. items.desc: About the Role As an AI Security Researcher, you bring deep expertise in AI/ML security, software development in Python, backed by a minimum MSc in Machine Learning, Computer Science, or related discipline. You have hands-on experience with AI workloads, large language models, training frameworks, advanced optimization algorithms, GPU clusters, and ideally SLURM in HPC environments. You excel at modeling AI threats—model/data poisoning, permission escalation, backdoors, data drift attacks, prompt injection—and translating them into practical security defenses. You will be one of Haste's first AI security researchers pioneering defenses for trillion-parameter AI training environments alongside HPC and quantum workloads. Key Responsibilities Adversarial Threat Research: Investigating emerging attack vectors and developing techniques to uncover vulnerabilities in AI models, data pipelines, and infrastructure. Threat Modeling & Risk Analysis: Mapping and characterizing potential threats across the AI lifecycle—from data ingestion to deployment—to prioritize security investments. Developing Defenses & Guardrails: Designing and implementing detection logic and researching mitigation methods to AI threats. Collaborating with Engineering Teams: Translating research findings into actionable, production-grade security requirements for product teams, ensuring threat detection makes sense. Documentation & Reporting: Creating technical reports, whitepapers, and proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits to document vulnerabilities and share findings within the organization or to the public. Monitoring AI Ecosystem Trends: Staying updated on the latest AI security standards, frameworks (e.g., OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, MITRE ATLAS), and academic research. Requirements University degree in AI/ML or relevant discipline. Current residence in Germany or Austria. Full-time availability from December 1, 2026, remote from Germany or Austria only.

items.desc: About The Pirbright Institute The Pirbright Institute is a world-leading centre of excellence for research and surveillance of viral diseases affecting farm animals and viruses that spread from animals to humans. Strategically funded by the UK Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC), the Institute works to enhance national and international capability to predict, detect, contain, control and eliminate economically and clinically important viral diseases through highly innovative fundamental and applied bioscience. Pirbright’s charitable objective is to conduct and promote scientific research into diseases of animals, including exotic diseases, and to develop appropriate methods for their prevention and control. Our mission is to be the world’s leading innovative centre for preventing and controlling viral diseases of livestock, applying scientific research to protect animal and human health and support the economy. Based on a dedicated campus in Pirbright, Surrey, southwest of London, the Institute employs just over 400 staff, with research supported by 52 PhD students and nine interns from a wide range of backgrounds. We pride ourselves on the diversity of our community and on a culture built around our PRIDE values: Passion for the highest standards of quality, delivery and performance; Reliability in everything we do, including leadership, learning, biosecurity and anticipating and containing unexpected events; Innovation as the driving force behind our fundamental and applied science; Dignity and respect for every member of our diverse community; and Excellence in all aspects of our work, from health, safety and biosafety to scientific research, customer service and environmental protection. Pirbright provides national and international capacity to predict, detect, understand and respond to emerging viral diseases of livestock, as well as endemic viruses circulating within and beyond the UK. Our diagnostics, surveillance facilities and specialist expertise form an important national capability, helping to protect the UK from livestock viral diseases that threaten our borders and enabling us to respond decisively and rapidly in the event of an outbreak. Our fundamental research focuses on viruses, hosts and the complex interactions between them, while our wider science addresses key challenges including protecting the UK and global agriculture from viral threats, increasing agricultural efficiency to improve animal health and welfare, mitigating the growing threat of vector-borne diseases driven by climate change, and improving human health through a greater understanding of vaccine-induced protection. With internationally recognised expertise in virology, immunology, diagnostics and surveillance, Pirbright combines fundamental discovery with practical solutions to tackle today's diseases and prepare for the emerging viral threats of tomorrow. Advancing science to improve the world in which we live. Organisation position & Purpose We are seeking a highly motivated and innovative scientist to join the Mucosal Immunology Group at contributing to a transformative research programme supported by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) and BBSRC Institute Strategic Programme Grants. This post offers a unique opportunity to be part of a pioneering One Health research initiative focused on interrupting the transmission of respiratory viruses such as influenza andcoronaviruses, which remain major public health challenges despite the availability of current vaccines and antivirals. The work will utilise the pig as a large, natural host animal model due to its close physiological, anatomical, immunological, and genetic similarities to humans. Pigs not only serve as natural hosts for influenza viruses highly similar to those in humans, but their lung structure and antibody responses also provide a highly relevant platform for translational research. The postholder will investigate the potential of mRNA-encoded antibodies, interferons, and other innate immune stimulators administered to the respiratory tract to prevent infection and interrupt transmission. This will include evaluating their capacity to reduce viral shedding, limit lung pathology, and disease severity. A central element of the project involves comparing different delivery strategies to determine which offer the most effective expression and protection in vivo. The role will also involve the development of porcine influenza-specific monoclonal antibodies following infection or immunisation, with detailed analysis of their specificity, functionality, and repertoire depending on the route of administration. To achieve these objectives, the postholder will apply a broad range of immunological and virological techniques, including ELISA, microneutralisation assays, virus propagation, plaque assays, molecular cloning, antibody repertoire profiling, and bioinformatics. items.desc: Free Mobile, part of the Iliad group, designs and deploys its own 5G infrastructure, from O-RAN radio units and distributed units to the user plane and Cloud RAN environment. At the heart of the DU, the physical layer and 5G fronthaul operate under hard real-time constraints. Every 0.5 ms slot must be received from the radio unit over eCPRI, processed on GPU, DSP or SIMD CPU, and delivered to the upper layers on time. This role sits at the intersection of 5G signal processing, embedded software and high-performance networking. You will work with real IQ data, radio units and production constraints, not only simulations. AI-assisted algorithms are part of the toolbox, but not the objective by themselves. We use them when they deliver a measurable improvement over classical methods in BLER, throughput or latency. Description du poste Your role : You will develop and optimise physical-layer and fronthaul processing for an O-RAN 7.2x system, from algorithm design and simulation to real-time implementation and integration with radio units. Your responsibilities will include: Developing the 5G uplink receiver chain: channel estimation, interpolation, MMSE equalisation, MIMO detection, LLR computation and LDPC decoding. Implementing PRACH detection, timing estimation and beamforming for massive MIMO. Processing O-RAN 7.2x C-plane and U-plane traffic, including eCPRI timing windows and IQ compression. Implementing real-time L1 functions in C on Linux and accelerating compute-intensive kernels with CUDA, DSP or SIMD. Building the eCPRI datapath with DPDK using poll-mode I/O, rte_flow, dedicated queues, zero-copy buffers and hardware timestamps. Optimising the complete processing chain for latency, memory usage, cache behaviour and compute load within a 0.5 ms slot budget. Validating algorithms through link-level simulations using 3GPP TDL/CDL channel models, then testing them with real IQ captures and O-RAN radio units. Measuring BLER, throughput, latency and CPU, GPU or DSP load to compare classical algorithms with AI-assisted alternatives. Investigating topics such as neural channel estimation and neural receivers when they can outperform an established baseline. Building regression tests and CI to detect performance or accuracy degradation. Contributing to architecture decisions, including GPU versus DSP or SIMD, hardware selection and accelerator integration. Working closely with radio unit, RAN, core network and operations teams. You will progressively own complete technical topics, from the mathematical model and implementation choices to their validation on the DU test bench. You will also contribute to code reviews, design documentation and open-source projects such as DPDK, Linux and U-Boot. Qualifications Your profile : We are open to both experienced engineers and high-potential graduates with strong foundations in mathematics, signal processing or embedded software. You have: An engineering degree, Master of Science or PhD in telecommunications, applied mathematics, embedded systems, computer science or a related field. Strong foundations in linear algebra, probability and digital signal processing. A good understanding of OFDM, MIMO, Fourier transforms, channel estimation, detection or channel coding. C programming skills on Linux, with an interest in memory layout, multithreading, cache behaviour and performance. Python experience with NumPy and SciPy for simulation, testing and data analysis. An interest in at least one of the following areas: 5G/LTE physical layer, O-RAN fronthaul, real-time embedded software, GPU programming, DSP/SIMD optimisation or AI for signal processing. The ability to turn mathematical concepts into code, define relevant metrics and validate the results experimentally. Good written English for reading specifications, documenting designs and reviewing code. French is a plus. Experience with CUDA, cuBLAS, cuFFT, AVX2, AVX-512, Arm NEON/SVE or fixed-point arithmetic is valuable, but you do not need to master all of them. Knowledge of DPDK, eCPRI, PTP, O-RAN 7.2x, 3GPP channel models or massive MIMO is also a plus. What matters most is your ability to understand difficult technical problems, build measurable solutions and explain the choices behind them.  About the AI Applications Team: 
 A small, freshly formed team with a very hands-on mission.
 We take early work packages, SDKs, libraries, and tools, integrate them end-to-end, and turn them into something that actually runs on real hardware. Along the way, we close the gaps, finish the missing pieces, and provide direct, practical feedback to the teams building the technology.
 We also build our own reference applications and demos that act as realistic examples, prove ideas, expose issues early, and show what’s possible on the edge!
 What you could be doing as an Intern
 Interns work alongside experienced engineers as part of a development team at Arm’s office in Budapest. You'll have a dedicated mentor and work on tasks that support existing projects, as well as explore and prototype ideas for the future. You'll also receive mentorship and support from other team members and have the chance to work across all aspects of the software creation process.
 Integrating delivered components into working embedded systems
 Debugging firmware, drivers, and application-level issues
 Adapting and extending example code and reference designs
 Building internal demos and proof-of-concept applications
 Giving structured, technical feedback based on real usage
 This is not a “watch from the sidelines” role. The work is hands-on, with plenty of opportunities to experiment, break things, fix them, and learn from the process.
 We are looking for individuals who
 Are currently studying towards a bachelor’s, master’s or PhD in computer science, engineering or a related technical subject.
 Have a strong foundation in C++, and an interest in maintaining developer infrastructures.
 Are interested in developing software libraries, developer tools and applications for AI-powered perception on edge devices.
 Are comfortable communicating and collaborating in English within a small team
 Take a creative yet structured approach to problem-solving
 Have a genuine interest in computing and a strong desire to learn and develop their skills.
 Qualities that will help your application stand out
 Experience with additional languages such as shell scripting, Python or Rust
 Experience integrating neural network models into applications
 Familiarity with neural network models, training, and application areas such as computer vision, LLMs, or audio
 Familiarity with Linux development environments and version control using Git
 Exposure to software testing, debugging and/or performance profiling
 Experience with any automation, DevOps and or CI/CD tools and frameworks
 Experience developing developer tools or example applications with command-line, terminal-based or graphical interfaces
 Additional Information
 We encourage early applications, as we review them on a first-come, first-served basis.
This is a fixed-term internship (approximately 6 months, full time or part time, starting in 2027) designed for students who are in higher education and will be returning to their studies after the internship or placement.
 Please note we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants must have the right to work in the country where the internship is based, without relying on sponsorship by Arm, for the full duration of the internship.
 In Return
 Working on interesting new projects with leaders in the field is exciting, but we also know how important it is to receive support. That's why throughout your internship, you can expect regular feedback and development opportunities, social activities to connect with your peers, an end of internship celebration, plus the opportunity to be *considered for future Graduate positions (*subject to performance). #getreadytogrow
In addition to a competitive salary of HUF 5,250,000 per annum, our on-the-job learning and mentoring/buddy schemes provide unparalleled learning and networking opportunities from the best in the industry.

items.card: The role You own two things at Armature: the research we publish and the evals system behind our results. items.desc: Location: Paris, France. We value working in person, and we stay flexible. You may also get the chance to join us on occasional trips to San Francisco. Language: English is required. You do not need to speak French. The role You own two things at Armature: the research we publish and the evals system behind our results. You work on both hand in hand with our forward deployed engineer and our product engineer. The research we publish. Our studies on how coding agents think and choose are how most customers find us. You decide what we study next, you run the studies behind our public leaderboards, and you publish the findings under your name. The evals system. Everything we tell a customer depends on our evals, so they have to be excellent. You research how to design them to get the best results, and you build what works into the product. This field is young, so many of your questions won’t have an answer yet, and what you find will shape how software gets rebuilt for agents. What you will do Published research Design and run studies on how coding agents choose tools, how models and harnesses differ, and how agents use software. Find the next questions worth asking, and new ways to look at the data we already have. Automate the research runs and the analysis, so each study takes less time than the one before. Write up your findings so developers want to read and share them. Evals system Test the latest research on evals against our own data, and keep what improves our results. Turn the questions our customers ask into better evals. Ship what works into the product with our product engineer. Who we look for You’re an engineer from a top school, and if you’re a new grad, your internships show that you can build things. You build through coding agents every day: you split the work, guide the agents and understand what they produce, and this is the skill we value most. You can go from raw data to a finding on your own. You come with your own ideas, and you like to test them. You have high agency: you move forward without waiting for instructions. Not a fit if You want pure research and nothing to ship. You need a fixed scope before you start. You want to train models more than you want to study how they behave. You prefer to write every line yourself over working through coding agents.

items.desc: At Aspect, we are one of London’s largest property maintenance teams, covering more trades than almost anyone else and operating 24/7. After more than 25 years of serving thousands of residential and commercial customers, we are entering an exciting phase of digital transformation. We are investing heavily in AI, computer vision, automation, and data to rethink how property maintenance is delivered, from diagnosing problems and supporting engineers in the field to improving customer experience and operational efficiency. We are looking for a talented and curious AI Engineer Intern to join our Data & AI team and work on real-world Computer Vision and multimodal AI projects. This is not an internship where you will spend your time preparing presentations or working on artificial exercises. You will work with real data, real operational problems, and modern AI technologies, with the opportunity to build solutions that could ultimately be deployed across the business. The Role As an AI Engineer Intern, you will work closely with our Data & AI team to research, prototype, evaluate, and build AI solutions focused primarily on Computer Vision and multimodal AI . You could be working on problems such as identifying property defects from images, analysing photos and videos from field engineers, extracting information from visual documents, matching images to jobs or assets, or combining images with text and operational data to help automate diagnosis and decision-making. You will gain hands-on experience with modern vision models, Vision-Language Models, deep learning, model evaluation, AI APIs, and production-oriented software development. We are looking for someone who enjoys experimenting, building, and learning quickly. You do not need to know everything already, but you should be comfortable with Python, understand the fundamentals of machine learning, and be excited about turning new AI research into practical applications. Example Projects Depending on business priorities, you may work on projects such as: Building Computer Vision models to identify property defects, damage, equipment, materials, and maintenance issues from photographs. Using Vision-Language Models to understand and describe images captured by customers and field engineers. Developing AI-assisted property diagnosis tools that combine images, customer descriptions, and historical job data. Experimenting with object detection, image classification, segmentation, OCR, visual search, and image similarity. Building systems to automatically assess the quality and completeness of engineer photographs. Identifying objects, tools, components, boilers, plumbing fixtures, electrical equipment, or building materials from images. Creating multimodal AI applications combining vision, text, audio, and structured operational data . Evaluating state-of-the-art models from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta, Hugging Face, and the wider open-source AI ecosystem. Exploring synthetic data generation and data augmentation to improve model performance. Building prototypes that move beyond notebooks and become usable internal applications or APIs. You Will Research, prototype, and evaluate Computer Vision and multimodal AI approaches for real operational problems. Build models and applications using Python, PyTorch, OpenCV, Hugging Face, and modern AI APIs. Work with image and video datasets, including data cleaning, labelling, preprocessing, augmentation, and analysis. Experiment with image classification, object detection, segmentation, OCR, embeddings, and Vision-Language Models. Develop evaluation frameworks to measure model accuracy, reliability, latency, and cost. Compare different models and approaches and clearly communicate the trade-offs between them. Help turn successful experiments into APIs, tools, and production-ready applications. Work with cloud AI platforms and GPU-based development environments. Collaborate with Data, Product, Operations, and field teams to understand real-world problems and translate them into AI solutions. Document experiments, findings, model performance, and technical decisions. Keep up with developments in Computer Vision, multimodal AI, foundation models, and applied machine learning. Contribute ideas and challenge existing approaches, we want interns who are curious and willing to experiment. What We Are Looking For We care more about your ability to learn, build, and solve problems than having years of commercial experience. You should have: Strong Python programming skills. A good understanding of machine learning and deep learning fundamentals. Some experience with Computer Vision through university projects, personal projects, research, competitions, or previous internships. Familiarity with frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, OpenCV, scikit-learn, or Hugging Face . Shape the technical stack, research discipline, and engineering standards as one of the lab's foundational hires. What You Bring Deep, first-principles understanding of reinforcement learning, with demonstrated experience debugging exploration, credit assignment, and reward hacking in large-scale models or complex agents. Strong research engineering instincts, capable of writing performant code and debugging everything from learning dynamics down to distributed systems and GPU performance. items.desc: As an intern at the CEA, you will have the opportunity to work within a world-renowned research environment. Our teams consist of passionate and dedicated experts, providing an ideal setting for learning and collaboration. You will have access to state-of-the-art equipment and top-tier research resources to carry out your assignments. The work conducted may potentially lead to a scientific publication. Context The goal of this internship is to investigate hybrid performance modeling techniques that combine ML-based data-driven models with structured top-down analytical models. What do we expect from you? Using the CVA6, CVA6S, CVA6S+ architectural evolution as a case study, the internship will explore: Hybrid modeling: Combining simulation ML-driven performance insights with analytical architectural models. Transferability: Evaluating whether models developed for one hardware generation can be adapted to subsequent generations with limited retraining or recalibration. Design-space exploration: Assessing the ability of hybrid models to efficiently predict the impact of architectural modifications. The internship aims to develop and evaluate a hybrid modeling methodology that balances accuracy, expressiveness, and transferability across hardware generations. The ultimate objective is to assess its potential for enabling flexible hardware design-space exploration, reducing reliance on costly cycle-accurate simulations. items.desc: The Faculty of Medicine at the University of Southampton invites applications for a three-year, full-time, fixed-term Research Fellow to join Professor Hanieh Yaghootkar’s interdisciplinary precision-diabetes research programme. Based at University Hospital Southampton, you will investigate the biological mechanisms underlying type 2 diabetes by integrating measures of organ health with large-scale genetic and clinical data. Working alongside genetic epidemiologists, clinicians and data scientists, you will apply advanced statistical and machine learning approaches to identify distinct diabetes subtypes, investigate their genetic determinants and improve prediction of disease risk and progression. The role As a Research Fellow, You Will Develop and apply machine learning approaches to identify distinct subtypes of type 2 diabetes using measures of liver, pancreas, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle health. Characterise the clinical, metabolic and genetic profiles of diabetes subtypes and evaluate their reproducibility across populations. Conduct genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of organ-health traits and diabetes subtypes, and apply Mendelian randomisation to investigate potential causal relationships. Develop and evaluate statistical and machine learning models to predict incident type 2 diabetes and disease progression using genetic and clinical data. Analyse large-scale population datasets, including UK Biobank, using robust statistical methods and reproducible computational workflows. Contribute to high-quality scientific publications, conference presentations and the dissemination of research findings. Collaborate with multidisciplinary researchers across genetic epidemiology, genomics, clinical medicine, imaging, statistics and data science. You will have opportunities to develop your research expertise, contribute to innovative analytical approaches and build your publication record within an internationally collaborative research environment. About You You will have: A PhD in in genetic epidemiology, statistical genetics, biostatistics, data science, computational biology or a closely related discipline. Experience analysing large-scale genetic, epidemiological or biomedical datasets, ideally including UK Biobank. Strong statistical and computational skills, including proficiency in R and/or Python and experience working in Linux-based computing environments. Practical experience conducting GWAS and Mendelian randomisation analyses, including appropriate quality control, sensitivity analyses and interpretation. Experience applying machine learning, clustering, predictive modelling or other advanced statistical methods to complex biomedical data. An understanding of genetic epidemiology and the application of statistical methods to investigate complex disease mechanisms. Evidence of high-quality research outputs, including peer-reviewed publications. Excellent analytical, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams. Experience with metabolic disease research would be advantageous. What We Can Offer At Southampton, you will join a supportive, internationally connected research environment at the forefront of genetic epidemiology, data science and precision medicine. We offer: Access to large-scale biomedical datasets, high-performance computing infrastructure and secure analytical environments. Opportunities to work at the interface of human genetics, medical imaging, machine learning and metabolic disease research. Collaboration with leading researchers across clinical medicine, genomics, epidemiology and computational science. Opportunities for high-impact publications, scientific conferences, professional development and career progression. A supportive and inclusive working environment committed to equality, diversity and flexible working, including Athena SWAN principles. A competitive University benefits package, including pension provision and generous annual leave. For informal enquiries, contact Professor Hanieh Yaghootkar (h.yaghootkar@soton.ac.uk). Working At The University Of Southampton Check out the staff benefits and why you should join us at The University of Southampton. A standard DBS check is required for this role.

items.desc: Sobre Predicta (M.IA) Predicta es una plataforma de tesorería con agentes de IA para empresas medianas con tesorería compleja. Colaboramos con grupos de investigación de la Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB) y del IIIA-CSIC en modelos matemáticos, IA explicable y sistemas multiagente aplicados a las finanzas. El puesto Buscamos a una persona con doctorado para el equipo de I+D. Hará investigación avanzada y desarrollo junto al CTO, sobre un producto que ya usan empresas reales. En qué trabajarás Sistemas multiagente y swarm intelligence aplicados a la gestión de tesorería. Gemelos digitales financieros: simulación de escenarios de caja y de efectos de red entre empresas. IA explicable (XAI) para finanzas, para que cada recomendación de los agentes se pueda justificar. Teoría de juegos cooperativos (valores de Shapley) y computación multipartita segura (MPC). Aprendizaje federado y privacidad diferencial, para aprender de varias empresas sin compartir sus datos. Validación científica de los modelos, junto con nuestros socios académicos. Qué buscamos Imprescindible: título de doctor/a ya obtenido. Aceptamos doctorados de distintos campos: IA, informática, matemáticas, física, economía, finanzas cuantitativas u otras disciplinas afines. Valoraremos experiencia en uno o varios de estos ámbitos (no hace falta en todos): agentes de IA y sistemas multiagente, swarm intelligence, matemáticas aplicadas y optimización, economía y teoría de juegos, tesorería y finanzas corporativas, gemelos digitales y simulación basada en agentes. items.desc:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


WHY THIS TEAM?

Internal Infrastructure builds the infrastructure and tools used to train, evaluate, and serve Cohere's foundation models. You will work with AI researchers and ML engineers on stability, scalability, and observability. The work accelerates the models behind Cohere's platform, North.

You will own the developer platform researchers use to write, build, and debug training code: dev environments, container images, CI, and training instrumentation. The role includes a compensated 24x7 on-call rotation.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Run secure developer environments that stay controlled and accelerate developer velocity as the research org scales.

 - Own container image build and CI/CD tooling.

 - Instrument training code and build self-service tooling so researchers can see why a run failed and debug it themselves.

 - Set infrastructure best practices through AI enablement, documentation, and office hours.

 - Troubleshoot production failures and performance problems, and leave the system easier to operate than you found it.

 - Build automation, infrastructure-as-code, and observability so the platform stays maintainable.

We hire at more than one level. We set level based on the scope you've owned and how independently you drive work.


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

 - Run a developer platform in production: CI, image builds, dev environments, or internal tooling that many engineers depend on.

 - Made ML engineers or researchers faster without making the platform fragile.

 - Enough Linux and Kubernetes to debug production systems. Experience operating a GPU cluster is a plus.

 - Written software in Python or Go. You would rather extend a solid open-source project than rebuild it.

 - Worked with researchers, ML engineers, or another team whose goals were not identical to yours.

 - Found a bottleneck, proposed a fix, and driven it in a fast-moving environment.

If this does not line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply.

items.desc: Hybrid in London or remote in the UK We’re looking for a Data Scientist to join our Credit Risk Modelling team. You'll work on the credit models that sit at the core of iwoca's lending business – the models that decide who we lend to, on what terms, and how far the product can grow. The Company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed. We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive. The team The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and customer lifetime value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy. The team is around twelve data scientists, who combined create models to efficiently drive fully automated and human-in-the-loop decision making. This forms the core analytical team that interface with and support smaller analytic functions in other parts of the business. The role As a Data Scientist in Credit Risk Modelling, you'll use iwoca's lending data to answer credit risk and CLtV questions, and build what you find into the team's production models. The work ranges from keeping today's models accurate as conditions change, through incremental improvements, to research that could replace them. You'll help choose the team's projects and put forward your own. With AI, prototyping is cheap enough for you to test ideas that once wouldn't have made the priority list. The R&D share of the role is growing as a result. You'll learn credit modelling in depth from several senior data scientists. Live examples of the work: Causal estimation of offer terms. Estimating the causal effect of amount, duration, and price on customer outcomes. Unifying automated and manual models. Finding a principled way to put the two model families, which optimise slightly different objectives, on a common cost function. IFRS accounting model. Developing a multi-stage model where recovery predictions feed back to improve the upfront loss estimates that International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) require. Generalising credit and CLtV. Exploring whether a single, more general model could replace the separate credit and CLtV models. The Requirements Essential: Applied statistics. You have a background in statistics from a quantitative field – typically a degree or Master's in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, or similar. You've applied it to real-world data, in research or at work. You know when the data breaks a method's assumptions, and what that does to your answer. Probabilistic reasoning. You quantify the uncertainty in each estimate, and treat calibration as a first-order concern. Research mindset. You've tested new modelling ideas of your own, and judged which were worth taking further. Judgement. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right. You defend your reasoning under challenge, and challenge others' when the evidence points elsewhere. Analytical ownership. You've taken ambiguous problems from framing the question to a decision the business acted on. You give an early answer and update it as new evidence comes in. AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it – a prototype, an automation, or a modelling pipeline others use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't. Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience. Bonus: Domain experience. You've worked in credit risk, lending, or customer lifetime value modelling. Production ML. You've built supervised ML models end to end – exploration, training, deployment, and monitoring. Non-linear methods. You can think in terms of the cost function and inductive biases of your models. Bayesian methods. You've used hierarchical models, MCMC, or Bayesian updating in real work. Time series modelling. You've modelled temporal data where autocorrelation, drift, or seasonality mattered. Coding. You can write code for analysis. The team works in Python The salary We expect to pay from £60,000 – £90,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. items.desc: Role Title: AI Benchmark Researcher (Remote) Role Type : Full-time Location: Remote Role Overview We are seeking an analytical researcher and red-teaming specialist to build evidence-based web-research benchmark tasks that reliably expose weaknesses in state-of-the-art (SOTA) AI models (e.g., Claude Opus 5 Max). In this role, you will discover hard-to-surface facts, build precise research tasks around them, test them directly against leading LLMs, and diagnose the exact failure mechanisms in the model's search and reasoning paths. Your work will directly shape AI evaluation frameworks, ensuring next-generation frontier models are tested against rigorous, non-trivial real-world research scenarios. Job Requirements : 1. Core Experience: 1+ years in investigative research, fact-checking, AI benchmark task authoring, red-teaming, or technical QA review. 2. Benchmark Familiarity: Proven experience authoring, testing, or reviewing tasks for AI benchmarks such as GAIA, BrowseComp, SimpleQA, SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, or Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE). 3. Analytical & OSINT Skills: Intermediate-to-advanced web search and Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) skills; ability to navigate academic archives, local records, or obscure databases. 4. Model Trajectory Debugging: Strong analytical capability to inspect model reasoning chains, search logs, and source selection to diagnose root causes of failure. 5. Precision Writing: Ability to author clear, unambiguous benchmark prompts with bulletproof, primary-sourced answer keys. Job Responsibilities: 1. Obscure Fact Discovery: Deeply research niche topics to identify factual ground truths that cannot be surfaced via simple, direct search queries. 2. Source Verification: Rigorously verify facts against primary or highly credible sources, cross-check for contradictory evidence, and document exact source URLs. 3. Task Construction: Draft clear, answerable benchmark tasks designed specifically to expose structural weaknesses in model research strategies. 4. Red-Teaming & Model Testing: Execute tasks against designated SOTA models to confirm they reliably trigger intended model failures. 5. Failure Diagnosis & Debugging: Trace model run logs, search trajectories, and intermediate outputs to pinpoint exactly where and why the model failed (distinguishing genuine model limitations from ambiguous prompts). 6. Pattern Scaling & Review: Apply validated "model-breaking" research patterns across new domains and, for strong performers, review tasks authored by peer trainers. Strong Plus (Preferred Qualifications) 7. Bachelor or higher degree from relevant engineering domain is a must for this position. 8. Prior experience specifically designing prompt-injection or reasoning-trap tasks that break SOTA models. 9. Advanced OSINT capabilities or published investigative/academic research demonstrating deep source verification. 10. Niche domain expertise in areas rich with hard-to-find records (e.g., local government filings, regional sports history, legal archives, historical patents). 11. Experience serving as a lead reviewer, benchmark auditor, or quality owner on AI evaluation projects. Offer Details: 1. Pattern Scaling & Review: Apply validated "model-breaking" research patterns across new domains and, for strong performers, review tasks authored by peer trainers. Strong Plus (Preferred Qualifications) Apply Now!

Familiarity with large language models, coding agents, reinforcement learning, model evaluation, or related AI systems. 5. We develop and embed AI solutions that help organisations better understand their customers, optimise operations, improve forecasting and decision-making, and unlock new opportunities for growth. From supply chains and merchandising to marketing, personalisation, and customer experience, we work with clients to deliver measurable commercial impact through AI. We are proud to combine technical excellence with practical deployment, ensuring solutions create value in complex, real-world environments. About The Role Join us as a Machine Learning Engineer to deliver bespoke, impactful AI solutions for our diverse Retail & Consumer clients. You will be instrumental in bringing machine learning out of the lab and into the real world, contributing to scalable software architecture and defining best practices. Working closely with clients and cross-functional teams, you’ll ensure the technical feasibility and successful delivery of high-quality, production-grade ML systems that drive tangible business outcomes. What you’ll be doing Building and deploying production-grade ML software, tools, and infrastructure. Creating reusable, scalable solutions that accelerate the delivery of AI and machine learning systems across retail and consumer use cases. Collaborating with engineers, data scientists, product teams, and commercial leads to solve critical client challenges. Leading technical scoping and architectural decisions to ensure project feasibility, scalability, and commercial impact. Defining and implementing Faculty’s standards for deploying machine learning systems in production. Acting as a trusted technical advisor to customers and partners, translating complex ML concepts into actionable business outcomes. Applying machine learning to challenges such as demand forecasting, customer analytics, personalisation, pricing, marketing optimisation, inventory management, and operational efficiency. Supporting clients in adopting AI capabilities that improve customer experiences and drive sustainable growth. items.desc: Eldena Eldena développe la couche de données et d’intelligence dédiée à la biologie dynamique de la peau. Nous générons et exploitons des données longitudinales et multimodales afin de modéliser la manière dont la peau évolue selon les individus, les environnements et les interventions. Notre objectif est de développer des modèles capables de représenter l’évolution dans le temps des états cutanés individuels, de prédire les trajectoires de réponse et, à terme, de permettre une expérimentation virtuelle validée pour la recherche biologique et le développement de produits. Détail de l'offre (poste, mission, profil) Corps de texte Le défi technique Il ne s’agit pas d’un problème classique d’IA appliquée. Les données biologiques sont hétérogènes, bruitées, parcellaires et longitudinales. Les mesures sont incomplètes, recueillies selon différentes modalités et échelles temporelles, et les trajectoires individuelles varient considérablement. Le principal défi consiste à apprendre des dynamiques biologiques pertinentes à partir d’observations multimodales incomplètes et à comprendre comment les trajectoires individuelles évoluent dans différentes conditions. Nous recherchons une personne capable d’aller au-delà de l’application de modèles existants et de contribuer à définir le cadre computationnel le plus adapté au problème. Pourquoi Eldena Cette opportunité consiste à contribuer à définir une nouvelle catégorie technologique : les modèles computationnels appliqués à la biologie dynamique de la peau. La peau constitue un système particulièrement adapté à la modélisation. Elle peut être mesurée de manière répétée et non invasive, elle est continuellement exposée à des facteurs environnementaux et individuels, et elle réagit de manière observable aux interventions. Nous générons des données multimodales en conditions réelles et travaillons avec des partenaires scientifiques, cliniques et industriels dans les domaines de la dermatologie, de l’industrie pharmaceutique et de la recherche cosmétique. Le poste Nous recherchons un·e CTO & Cofondateur·rice technique pour prendre en charge la technologie d’Eldena et piloter sa prochaine phase de développement. Eldena ne part pas de zéro. Nous disposons déjà d’un MVP, de premières données et d’une infrastructure de modélisation, ainsi que d’une production active de données et de travaux scientifiques en cours. Votre première responsabilité consistera à comprendre ce qui a déjà été développé, à l’évaluer de manière critique et à définir ce qui doit être renforcé, repensé ou développé par la suite. Vous travaillerez directement avec le CEO, le CSO et les partenaires scientifiques, avec des responsabilités couvrant les données, la modélisation, l’infrastructure, les produits et la gouvernance technique. Il s’agit d’un rôle qui reste très opérationnel. Vous travaillerez directement sur les modèles, les données et l’architecture, tout en construisant progressivement l’organisation technique autour de vous. Vos responsabilités IA et modélisation Définir la stratégie de modélisation d’Eldena pour les données biologiques multimodales et longitudinales. Piloter le développement, l’entraînement et l’évaluation des modèles principaux, notamment en matière d’incertitude, de robustesse et de généralisation. Établir des critères clairs permettant de déterminer quand un modèle est suffisamment mature pour passer de la recherche à une utilisation produit ou scientifique. Validation scientifique Construire des protocoles de validation rigoureux avec le CSO et les partenaires scientifiques. Définir des benchmarks, des modèles de référence, des critères d’acceptation et des jeux de données d’évaluation. Veiller à ce que les scores et prédictions des modèles soient validés par rapport à des mesures pertinentes et à des références scientifiques ou cliniques, et à ce que les performances revendiquées restent étayées par des preuves. Données, plateforme et ingénierie Piloter l’architecture reliant l’acquisition des données, l’infrastructure de données, le développement des modèles et les produits Eldena. Construire des pipelines fiables pour les données multimodales et longitudinales, ainsi que pour l’entraînement, l’inférence, les API, le suivi des expérimentations, le monitoring et la reproductibilité. Prendre des décisions pragmatiques sur ce qu’Eldena doit développer en interne, réutiliser ou développer avec des partenaires. Sécurité, confidentialité et gouvernance technique Intégrer la sécurité, la confidentialité et la gouvernance des données au sein même de l’architecture technique. Mettre en place des contrôles appropriés en matière d’accès, de traçabilité, de protection des données, de gouvernance des modèles et de reproductibilité. Travailler avec le CEO et des spécialistes externes sur les exigences liées au RGPD et préparer l’organisation technique aux futures exigences de qualité, de sécurité et de réglementation à mesure qu’Eldena se développe.
