items.desc: About The Role At Quantum Systems, we are building highly autonomous interceptor systems that must perceive, decide, and act under extreme latency, motion, and environmental constraints. We are looking for a Computer Vision & AI Engineer to drive the perception stack of our Counter-UAS interceptor platform. You will work on low-latency camera pipelines, small-object detection, object tracking, sensor fusion, visual odometry, precision landing, camera calibration, embedded inference, and data pipelines for training and validation. This role is suited for someone with a strong academic or practical background in computer vision, AI, robotics, or perception systems. A Master’s degree is expected; a PhD is a strong plus. We are open to ambitious early-career candidates if they bring strong technical depth, practical implementation skills, and the ability to own complex perception problems. Your Mission You will develop the vision and AI pipeline that turns raw camera data into actionable perception outputs for autonomous flight. This includes low-latency detection and tracking, motion-aware vision, sensor fusion with inertial data, 3D direction-vector estimation, GPS-denied navigation, and precision landing support. What Is Your Day To Day Mission Bring up, optimize, and maintain high-performance camera pipelines, including CSI camera interfaces, raw image access, buffering, synchronization, and latency reduction. Develop detection algorithms for small and difficult-to-see objects in moving and rotating camera images. Combine machine learning and classical computer vision approaches where appropriate. Fuse inertial data, motion information, and visual data to improve detection and tracking in moving image sequences. Build object tracking pipelines that can switch from initial detection to low-latency tracking once a target has been acquired. Optimize perception pipelines for embedded execution on NVIDIA Jetson platforms. Work toward high frame-rate processing targets in the range of 100–300 FPS, where technically feasible. Use camera intrinsics and extrinsics to transform image-space detections into 3D direction vectors or other navigation-relevant outputs. Work on GPS-denied navigation concepts using visual odometry, including approaches with forward-facing camera views rather than only downward-looking cameras. Develop visual support for precision landing, including height estimation, velocity estimation, and motion-state estimation from limited camera perspectives. Build and maintain the data pipeline from onboard recordings to cloud storage, preprocessing, annotation, dataset generation, training, validation, and benchmarking. Work with annotation tools such as SuperAnnotate, CVAT, Label Studio, or comparable systems. Benchmark and evaluate different model and algorithm families, including approaches such as CenterNet, SuperPoint, SuperGlue, optical flow, feature tracking, object detection, and lightweight embedded models. Build deployment pipelines using ONNX, TensorRT, custom inference runners, or comparable embedded inference tooling. Collaborate closely with autonomy, flight control, embedded software, test, and systems engineering teams. What You Bring To The Team Master’s degree or PhD in computer vision, AI, robotics, machine learning, electrical engineering, computer science, aerospace engineering, or a comparable technical field. Strong understanding of computer vision fundamentals, camera geometry, feature detection, object detection, tracking, calibration, and image-space to 3D transformations. Practical experience implementing computer vision or machine learning pipelines in Python and C++ . Experience with embedded inference, ideally on NVIDIA Jetson , CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX, GStreamer, V4L2, or similar technologies. Ability to read, understand, and implement ideas from current research papers. Understanding of latency, throughput, profiling, memory movement, and real-time constraints. Experience with dataset creation, annotation workflows, training/validation splits, metrics, and benchmarking. Strong mathematical intuition and willingness to debug both algorithms and real-world sensor data. Ability to take ownership of a technical area and drive it from research prototype to flight-test-ready software. Experience with UAV perception, robotics perception, visual odometry, SLAM, sensor fusion, or tracking systems. Experience with IMU-camera fusion, ego-motion compensation, rolling-shutter effects, or high-frame-rate cameras. Experience with precision landing, visual navigation, or GPS-denied navigation. Experience building cloud-based ML training and validation pipelines. Publications, thesis work, GitHub projects, demos, or competition results in computer vision, robotics, AI, or autonomous systems. items.desc: Research Associate in Modelling and Robotics About The Role We are seeking a motivated Research Associate to join our research team at the University of Bath, contributing to the ARIA-funded Robot Dexterity Programme. The project aims to advance the fundamental understanding, modelling and control of robotic systems, with a particular focus on developing new analytical and computational frameworks for dexterous soft robotic manipulators. The successful candidate will contribute to ground breaking research at the intersection of computational mechanics, robotics and intelligent modelling, working within a multidisciplinary team to bridge fundamental physical principles and practical robotic applications. Key Responsibilities Include High-fidelity computational modelling: Develop and validate advanced physics-based models of robotic systems, including nonlinear mechanics, structural dynamics, large deformation and multi physics interactions, using numerical simulation tools such as COMSOL, ABAQUS or ANSYS. Robotic modelling and dynamics: Investigate the kinematics, dynamics and actuation of robotic manipulators, particularly soft and continuum robots, and establish computational frameworks that capture their complex physical behaviour. Experimental validation: Design and conduct experiments to validate high-fidelity computational models of robotic systems, integrating experimental measurements with numerical simulations to assess model accuracy, investigate dynamic behaviour and support the development of robotic manipulation and control. Research collaboration and validation: Work closely with researchers in robotics, modelling and control to validate theoretical developments through simulations and experiments, contribute to scientific publications, and support the delivery of project achievements. About You You will have a PhD (or be close to completion) in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Computational Mechanics, Applied Mathematics or a closely related fields. Experience in robotics, finite element analysis, multi physics simulation would be particularly advantageous. This position offers an opportunity to contribute to an ambitious ARIA research programme, combining fundamental engineering science with the development of next-generation intelligent robotic systems. We are looking for a motivated researcher with a strong background in computational modelling and robotics, who enjoys tackling challenging engineering problems and working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary research team. Essential Qualifications, Skills And Experience A PhD (or nearing completion) in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Computational Mechanics, Applied Mathematics or a closely related STEM field, or equivalent relevant research experience. Strong knowledge and practical experience in high-fidelity computational modelling, particularly finite element analysis (FEA), nonlinear mechanics, structural dynamics or multi physics simulation. Experience using numerical simulation software such as COMSOL, ABAQUS or ANSYS, or equivalent computational modelling tools. A good understanding of robotic systems, including kinematics, dynamics, actuation and control. Strong programming and numerical analysis skills, preferably in MATLAB, Python or equivalent environments. Ability to conduct independent research, analyse complex technical problems and communicate findings effectively. Good interpersonal and collaborative skills, with the ability to contribute effectively to a multidisciplinary research team. We welcome applications from candidates with diverse technical backgrounds who can demonstrate relevant expertise and a willingness to develop new skills. Further information The role is offered on a full time (36.5 hours per week) fixed term basis with an expected start date of January/February 2027. items.desc: We are looking for doctors to join our growing community of experts who are available to be matched on an on-going basis to new innovative AI projects with the world's leading AI labs and companies that are bringing to life AI in healthcare. Your medical expertise will shape the way AI understands and processes real-world clinical interactions, workflows, consultations including the delivery of care with software that directly impacts both healthcare professionals and patients. These projects are flexible, fully remote and ideal for clinicians who want to work on shaping the future of AI in healthcare alongside their existing professional or academic commitments. About Mentis AI At Mentis AI, we’re building the next generation of AI systems grounded in real-world clinical expertise. As a clinical expert, you’ll gain hands-on exposure to cutting-edge AI model development, working side-by-side with senior AI researchers and clinicians to translate your medical knowledge into industry-ready clinical solutions to advance healthcare. How It Works Once we have a new project, you will be automatically screened and matched to assess if you are a suitable fit. If shortlisted, we will then invite you to take a skills test (~10-30mins) and if required will also conduct an interview. We are looking to match you based on your skillset, expertise, grade and speciality to make sure it's the right fit for the project! If successful, you will be onboarded onto the platform and can start getting involved in a diverse range of tasks that vary from labelling clinical notes, summarising medical records, annotating images to reviewing and evaluating the performance of AI Models/LLMs. The rapid rise of AI in healthcare means there are so many new and exciting ways to train, review and improve the deployment of AI in healthcare, which you will directly have an impact upon. Key Responsibilities Data labeling and curation: Review clinical notes, audio, videos and other modalities, identifying relations and reasoning steps per guidelines. LLM and model evaluations: Run structured evals (human-in-the-loop) to assess accuracy, safety, clinical relevance and clinical reasoning of models. Prompting and prompt-engineering: Design, test, and iterate prompts to improve performance and reliability. Fine-tuning support: Create high-quality instructions/responses and explore edge-case datasets to enhance models. Feedback and error analysis: Identify critical/failure points, propose strategies to help mediate and document findings. Scoring/Rubrics frameworks: Develop and refine scoring rubrics for quality assurance (e.g., accuracy, clarity, safety, completeness, guideline adherence). Guideline refinement: Collaborate with researchers to improve annotation standards, acceptance criteria, and evaluation protocols. Essential Requirements Doctor based in the UK with an active GMC license. Native or near-native fluency in English (spoken and written). Good understanding of clinical terminology, tools and workflows. Excellent summarisation and written communication skills. Strong attention to detail and commitment to clinical accuracy. Comfortable working independently in an asynchronous environment. What we offer Remote work Asynchronous and flexible scheduling, allowing you to balance work with clinical practice or studies. Competitive compensation based on experience. The opportunity to influence and enhance AI tools that serve healthcare professionals. Experience working at the intersection of medicine and AI, helping shape the future of healthcare. Opportunity to collaborate with clinicians and AI researchers to deepen your own clinical acumen and professional expertise in AI within healthcare.

items.desc:
At Sonova R&D, we are not just developing hearing devices, we are shaping the future of hearing technology. At the heart of this transformation is the deployment and execution of neural networks on our next-generation embedded platform. This requires innovative tools and firmware infrastructure, giving you the opportunity to directly influence the performance of our products. 
 As our new Embedded Software Engineer, you will join a team bringing cutting-edge AI to our hearing devices. Your focus will be on developing the embedded software stack that forms the foundation of our next-generation hearing instruments, bridging the gap between AI and ultra-low-power embedded systems. 
 Are you excited to explore new technological territory and play a pivotal role in shaping Sonova’s edge AI capabilities? Join us and help rethink how embedded software is built to enhance people’s hearing experience and quality of life. 
 More about the role 
 Design, develop and maintain firmware for a deeply embedded platform operating under strict latency, memory, compute, and energy constraints. 
 Debug complex issues directly on target hardware and simulators. 
 Contribute to the integration and deployment process of neural networks in hearing-device firmware, working with AI and DSP experts. 
 Advise AI developers on tailoring neural networks to the embedded platform’s quantization, memory, compute, and power constraints. 
 Work with other engineering teams to develop prototypes, turn them into production-ready features, and integrate them into our system. 
 Ensure high software quality through clean-code practices, code reviews, testing, documentation, maintenance, and root-cause analysis. 
 More about you 
 Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field. 
 Strong hands-on experience developing embedded software in C or C++, including object-oriented design, and practical experience using Python for development tools and automation. 
 Experience profiling embedded software to identify performance bottlenecks and optimizing execution time, memory usage, and energy consumption on resource-constrained systems. 
 Knowledge of embedded tooling (compiler, debugger, simulators, ...). 
 Experience developing and integrating software on resource-constrained embedded systems. 
 Fluent English, with strong written and verbal communication skills. 
 Familiarity with micro-NPU, deployment of neural networks and frameworks such as TensorFlow Lite, ONNX, TVM, or ExecuTorch, is an advantage. 
 Knowledge of audio or digital signal processing is an advantage. 
 Experience in bringing features to products is an advantage. 
 What we offer 
 As one of the world’s leading hearing care providers headquartered in Switzerland, we’re committed to building an inclusive culture. We want to create an environment where you can balance a successful career with your commitments and interests outside of work, through our flexible hybrid working model. We offer a wide range of training opportunities for both your professional and personal development, and there are exceptional growth opportunities with individual development plans. 
 Why Join Sonova? 
 At Sonova, we offer more than just a job — we offer a chance to make an impact. You’ll join a collaborative, inclusive environment where your ideas matter and your leadership shapes how we serve our customers. With our modern office spaces, focus on employee development, and strong company values, you’ll be empowered to grow both personally and professionally. 
 Make an impact that resonates. Join Sonova and help us bring the world closer through better hearing.

Vos missions Au sein de notre équipe de développement, vous serez en charge de : La conception et le développement de solutions basées sur l'IA Le pilotage de projets spécifiques de développement d'outils avec IA pour les PME L'intégration et le déploiement de modèles d'intelligence artificielle dans des applications existantes et nouvelles L'optimisation et la maintenance des algorithmes en production La veille technologique et la proposition d'innovations en IA La rédaction de documentation technique et le partage de connaissances au sein de l'équipe Votre environnement technique IA/ML : TensorFlow, PyTorch Langages : Python (principal), Node.js ou Java selon les projets Outils : Git, GitHub Infrastructure : API REST, Docker, Kubernetes Votre profil Vous disposez d'un diplôme Bac+5 en informatique, data science ou domaine connexe Vous maîtrisez Python et possédez de solides connaissances en mathématiques appliquées Vous avez une expérience concrète du déploiement de modèles IA en production Vous êtes autonome, force de proposition et capable de mener des projets de bout en bout Vous possédez d'excellentes capacités de communication et appréciez le travail en équipe Qui sommes-nous ? Acteam-IT, bien plus qu’un cabinet d’expertise IT, est le catalyseur de transformations digitales, un architecte de solutions techniques et humaines. Notre histoire a débuté en 2014 par un engagement : celui d'accompagner nos clients dans l'atteinte de leurs objectifs. Qu'il s'agisse de développement, d'administration d'infrastructures, de testing ou de gestion de projets, notre palette de solutions est aussi diversifiée que les défis auxquels nos clients font face. Chez ACTEAM-IT, chaque projet est une aventure, chaque client un partenaire pour qui nous déployons des solutions sur mesure. Au cœur de notre démarche, il y a des valeurs fondamentales : l’expertise, l’exigence et la solidarité. Chaque collaboration est bâtie sur la confiance et le respect mutuel. Le tout, nous permet de créer des liens durables avec nos collaborateurs, nos clients et partenaires. Aussi, entreprise engagée et inclusive, nous avons un attachement profond à la diversité et l’équité. Cela se traduit par notre encouragement à recevoir et considérer les candidatures de tous horizons et tous profils. Déroulement des entretiens Un 1er échange téléphonique ou en visio de 15 min 1 ou 2 entretien(s) avec un ou deux membres de l’équipe et la direction de l’entreprise Type d'emploi : CDI Rémunération : à partir de 35 000,00€ par an Avantages : Prise en charge du transport quotidien Titre restaurant Travail à domicile occasionnel Lieu du poste : En présentiel

Contribute to the development and implementation of collaborative research efforts with group members, students, and international research
items.desc: Creating knowledge. Making a difference. Shaping the future. This is what the University of Münster stands for as one of the strongest research-oriented universities in Germany and one of the largest employers in the region. Every day, over 7,000 employees devote themselves to cutting-edge research and excellent teaching. We share more than a workplace. We share the desire to make a real impact – regionally and internationally. Our day-to-day work is distinguished by diversity, openness and space to pursue one’s ideas. Become a part of our team – in academia, a technical or manual trade, or administration. The Department for Quantum Technology of the Faculty of Physics at the University of Münster, Germany, is seeking to fill the position of a Doctoral Research Associate Wissenschaftliche r Mitarbeiter in (salary level E 13 TV-L, 67%) at the earliest possible date. We are offering a fixed-term part-time position (67%) for 3 years. Full-time employees are required to teach 4 hours per week during the semester. Your tasks: Participate in the research activities of the Foundations of Quantum Theory Group at the Department of Quantum Technology, including the planning and execution of scientific projects in the fields of quantum information theory and foundations of quantum theory. Contribute to the development and implementation of collaborative research efforts with group members, students, and international research partners. Publication of original research results in leading scientific journals and presentation of these results at international conferences. Participation in the teaching activities of the Department of Quantum Technology. The position is associated with the completion of a doctoral research project (PhD). Our expectations: A graduate degree (German Diplom or master's degree) in physics is required. Proficiency in spoken and written English is strongly desired. Knowledge in the theoretical foundations of quantum physics and quantum information theory. Research experience in the mathematical structure of quantum theory. You should be team-oriented, have strong communication and organisational skills, scientific writing and presentation skills, and the ability to work independently. Advantages for you: Appreciation, commitment, openness and respect – values which are important to us. Our broad range of diverse work-time models offers great flexibility – also when working from home. If you have family members or young children in your care, our offers concrete support to help you balance your private and professional responsibilities. As an educational institution, we are deeply committed to offering opportunities tailored to your individual needs. From A – Z, Aikido to Zumba, our ensure a healthy work-life balance. As a university employee, you are entitled to numerous benefits afforded to public servants, e.g. an attractive company pension scheme (), an and a position that is shielded from economic fluctuations. The University of Münster strongly supports . We welcome all applicants regardless of sex, nationality, ethnic or social background, religion or worldview, disability, age, sexual orientation or gender identity. We are committed to creating family-friendly working conditions. We actively encourage applications by women. Women with equivalent qualifications and academic achievements will be preferentially considered unless these are outweighed by reasons which necessitate the selection of another candidate. If you have any questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Matthias Kleinmann ). Are you interested? Then we look forward to receiving your application by 2026-11-20 via our online application form. Reference number: 2026_10_42

items.desc: Wat krijg je? Een arbeidsovereenkomst voor een jaar van 32 uur per week, met uitzicht op een vast contract. Salaris conform cao GGZ schaal 60 € 4.544,- tot € 5.901,- op basis van 36 uur, afhankelijk van relevante werkervaring. Vakantiegeld (8,33%) en eindejaarsuitkering (8,33%). 100% vergoeding van je reiskosten wanneer je met het OV reist en/of een reiskostenvergoeding van € 0,25 per km woonwerk wanneer je met de auto komt. Thuiswerkvergoeding van € 2,45 per gewerkte dag. Voor je persoonlijke ontwikkeling kun je een opleiding of training volgen. Balansregeling van € 1.000,- bruto (naar rato) per jaar: keuze tussen uitbetaling /inzet voor scholing naar keuze/of extra verlofuren. Pensioenregeling bij Pensioenfonds Zorg & Welzijn (PFZW). 201 vakantie uren per jaar bij een fulltime dienstverband. Op slechts vijf minuten lopen van trein en metro. Vanaf Amsterdam Centraal, Utrecht Centraal en Gouda ben je in minder dan 20 minuten bij ons. Met de auto? Je kunt gratis parkeren. Wij werken werken hybride, minimaal 50% van de werktijd vanaf kantoor, maandag is onze kantoordag. Wat breng je mee? Je hebt minimaal 5 jaar relevante werkervaring als data scientist met complexe en grote data- en taalmodellen. Dit blijkt zowel uit wetenschappelijke publicaties als toepassingen ervan op organisatieniveau. Je werkt graag zelfstandig, maar zoekt ook actief de samenwerking op met collega’s om tot een goed resultaat te komen. Je bent in staat om complexe (technische) vraagstukken op te lossen en vind het leuk om met je inhoudelijke kennis anderen te begeleiden bij uitdagende projecten. Daarnaast: Heb je een Master of Science (MSc), bij voorkeur (bijna) gepromoveerd in computer science of een andere relevante studierichting. Heb je ervaring met het bewerken en analyseren van grote datasets en het bouwen en beheren van complexe datamodellen en AI-toepassingen. Heb je relevante wetenschappelijke publicaties op het gebied van computer science of aanverwante vakgebieden. Heb je ervaring met de ontwikkeling en invoering van AI-modellen en het verbeteren van bestaande data-infrastructuur. Kun je werken met een of meer van de volgende technieken en systemen: Python, Large Language Models, Machine Learning libraries (pytorch), Microsoft Azure, Linux omgeving en Microsoft Azure. Heb je kennis van kwaliteitsstandaarden, relevante wet- en regelgeving en actuele technische ontwikkelingen op het gebied van AI. Heb je ervaring met het begeleiden van wetenschappelijk onderzoek, het analyseren van onderzoeksresultaten en het schriftelijk vastleggen daarvan. Kun je complexe vraagstukken zelfstandig oplossen, werk je gestructureerd en kun je goed plannen en organiseren. Communiceer je helder en werk je graag samen met collega’s uit verschillende vakgebieden. Heb je affiniteit met suïcidepreventie en wil je met jouw kennis bijdragen aan de ondersteuning van onze hulpverleners. Hoe ziet je agenda eruit? Wie zijn wij? 113 Zelfmoordpreventie streeft naar een land waarin niemand eenzaam en radeloos sterft door zelfdoding. Uit onderzoek weten we dat mensen vaak niet dood willen, maar geen andere uitweg meer zien. 113 is in 2009 opgericht om wel een andere uitweg te bieden door het onderwerp bespreekbaar te maken. 113 heeft een hulplijn; mensen met suïcidale gedachten kunnen dag en nacht anoniem bellen of chatten. Als nationale organisatie voor suïcidepreventie onderzoekt, ontwikkelt en implementeert 113, samen met vele andere organisaties, interventies en campagnes om het aantal zelfdodingen in Nederland omlaag te krijgen. In de zestien jaar dat onze organisatie bestaat, hebben we taboes rondom zelfdoding helpen verminderen en zowel de zorgsector als overheidsinstanties, gemeentes, scholen, families, naasten en uiteraard de hulpvragers hierover geïnformeerd en ondersteund. We zijn trots op wat we hebben bereikt in ons relatief korte bestaan, maar we zijn er nog niet. Wij zijn op zoek naar een Dataspecialist AI. Krijg jij energie van het analyseren van complexe data en het ontwikkelen van slimme AI-oplossingen? En wil je met jouw kennis bijdragen aan het voorkomen van zelfdoding? Bij 113 krijg je de ruimte om onderzoek te doen en AI-toepassingen te ontwikkelen die onze hulplijn helpen verbeteren. Zo verbind je technologie en onderzoek aan een maatschappelijk doel. Wat ga je doen? Als Dataspecialist AI werk je aan belangrijk onderzoek om de 113 Hulplijn klaar te maken voor de toekomst en met nieuwe inzichten de hulpverlening te verbeteren. Je gaat zelf aan de slag met het modelleren en analyseren van complexe data uit onze hulplijn en speelt een belangrijke rol bij evaluatie- en implementatieonderzoek. Samen met een GZ-psycholoog en een senior onderzoeker ben je verantwoordelijk voor de ontwikkeling en invoering van AI-tools die onze hulpverleners kunnen ondersteunen. Je onderzoekt hoe deze toepassingen in de praktijk werken en hoe ze het beste aansluiten bij hun behoeften. Je houdt je onder andere bezig met: Data modelleren en analyseren . Je werkt met …

items.desc: I Posten Bring jobber vi hver dag med å utvikle løsninger som gjør hverdagen enklere og verden litt mindre. Virkelig gode løsninger oppstår når vi klarer å bruke data og maskinlæring til å løse reelle problemer – og få dem helt ut i produksjon. Derfor styrker vi nå vårt data- og maskinlæringsmiljø med en data scientist som vil være med på å utvikle og produksjonssette løsninger som skaper verdi. I Teknologi og sikkerhet blir du en del av sterke fagmiljøer innen teknologi, produktutvikling, data, AI og sikkerhet. Vi jobber tett sammen med forretnings- og driftsmiljøer i konsernet for å levere verdi og resultater for både kolleger og kunder. Området har ansvar for alt fra teknologistrategi, plattformutvikling og arkitektur til digital produktutvikling og sikker og stabil drift. Sammen bygger vi løsninger som ikke blir liggende i en skuff, men som brukes hver dag. Om avdelingen Du blir en del av avdelingen for data og maskinlæring bestående av data scientists, ML/data-ingeniører og dataanalytikere. Kulturen er preget av: Nysgjerrighet og vilje til å lære Åpenhet og samarbeid En pragmatisk tilnærming der vi tester, diskuterer og justerer underveis Vi har ikke alltid fasiten på forhånd – og nettopp derfor er det spennende å jobbe hos oss. Dine viktigste arbeidsoppgaver: Som data scientist hos oss jobber du ende-til-ende med maskinlæringsløsninger – fra idé og analyse til produksjon og videre drift. Du vil blant annet: Jobbe tett med forretningen for å finne og prioritere muligheter der data og ML kan skape verdi Gjøre uklare behov om til konkrete problemstillinger, og vurdere når ML ikke er riktig svar Utvikle, trene og evaluere maskinlæringsmodeller Sette modeller i produksjon og følge dem opp over tid Bygge og bruke datapipelines for analyse og modellering Presentere funn og anbefalinger for ledere og fagfolk uten teknisk bakgrunn Hvem ser vi etter? Vi ser etter deg som har erfaring med å levere maskinlæringsløsninger hele veien fra idé til produksjon. Du har: Minst 3 års erfaring med ML/AI Levert flere ML/AI-løsninger ende-til-ende Erfaring med å drive frem løsninger sammen med forretningen, og med å vise hvilken verdi de har skapt Solid kompetanse innen dataanalyse, eksperimentering og modellutvikling Erfaring med produksjonssetting, monitorering og vedlikehold av modeller God erfaring med Python og relevante ML-biblioteker (f.eks. PyTorch, scikit-learn, pandas, polars) Erfaring med skyplattformer Svært gode muntlige og skriftlige ferdigheter i norsk, svensk eller dansk Det er en fordel om du også har erfaring med MLOps-verktøy, CI/CD, Databricks, Spark, SQL og Terraform. For at du skal lykkes og trives hos oss Har mer fokus på problemet som skal løses og verdien som skal skapes enn på hvilken modell som skal brukes Trives i dialog med folk i forretningen og klarer å forklare komplekse ting på en enkel måte Er nysgjerrig på virksomheten og søker stadig å lære mer om den Tar ansvar for at løsningene faktisk fungerer, også over tid Deler kunnskap og gjerne bygger videre på det andre har laget, i stedet for å starte fra bunne Hva kan vi tilby deg? Store datamengder og høyt potensial for automatisering og verdiskaping Et sterkt fagmiljø med dyktige og hjelpsomme kollegaer En moderne dataplattform tilpasset ML/AI-utvikling Påvirke hvordan vi jobber med data og maskinlæring Fleksibel arbeidshverdag og hybrid løsning Arbeidsplass i Posthuset med Oslos beste utsikt! Konkurransedyktige betingelser og gode forsikrings- og pensjonsordninger Er dette er deg, eller er du klar for å bli denne medarbeideren? Da tilbyr vi deg en stilling der du alltid vil være i utvikling og på vei til nye steder og ansvarsområder. Hos oss vil du få rom til å forme din egen hverdag og karriere. I Posten og Bring tror vi på at når menneskene som jobber her utvikler seg, kan vi som konsern gjøre det samme. Søknadsfrist 29 november Har du spørsmål om rollen, er du velkommen til å ta kontakt med rekrutterende leder Solveig Masvie på telefon 456 749 75 eller Solveig.Masvie@posten.no . For spørsmål om rekrutteringsprosessen kan du kontakte HR Business Partner Diana Rensvala på telefon 412 15 352 eller diana.rensvala@bring.com . Mangfoldet i Posten Bring er vår styrke, og vi mener forskjellighet blant medarbeidere er nøkkelen til nytenkning og innovasjon. Vi ønsker oss derfor et stort mangfold blant søkere. Vi gjennomfører bakgrunnssjekk av aktuelle kandidater via vår samarbeidspartner Semac AS, www.semac.no . Vi ser frem til å høre fra deg! items.desc: Position Details Department of Immunology and Immunotherapy, College of Medicine and Health Location: University of Birmingham, Edgbaston, Birmingham UK Full time starting salary is normally in the range £37,369 to £46,970, with potential progression once in post to £49,798 Grade 7 Full Time, Fixed Term contract up to December 2030 Closing date: 22 nd November 2026 Background A post-doctoral research fellow position is available in the Fungal Immunology Group within the Institute of Immunology & Immunotherapy, College of Medical & Dental Sciences, University of Birmingham , led by Prof Rebecca Drummond. This role is to create and contribute to the creation of knowledge by undertaking a specified range of activities within an established research programme and/or specific research project. We are looking for an enthusiastic and committed scientist to join our project team, which is aiming to better understand organ-specific immune responses against fungal pathogens. The successful candidate will make extensive use of a range of in vivo models of fungal infection and will have access to the wide range of transgenic tools and in vivo immunology techniques established in the Drummond lab. The candidate’s research will focus on characterising immune cells, especially tissue-resident subsets, and how these interact during fungal infection within the central nervous system. This is an exciting opportunity to investigate regulation of antifungal immunity in vivo. As an example of the work the team has previously published, please see Mohamed et al, Nature Communications 2023 and Hain et al, Nature Communications 2025. The position would ideally suit someone with an immunology background with a strong interest in fungal pathogens. The candidate will be based in Drummond lab, which is part of a larger international consortium, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The candidate will join meetings and meet other team members based in Denmark and Uganda. All groups will work closely together during the project. There will be opportunity for additional training for the successful applicant with our collaborators to develop a wide range of technical expertise in immunology, neuroscience and microbiology. Funding for the position is available for 3 years, with possibility of extension. The lab is located within the Institute of Immunology & Immunotherapy at the University of Birmingham, where a collaborative environment exists, rich in immunologists with a range of complimentary research interests. We also closely work with our colleagues in the Institute of Microbiology & Infection who specialise in fungal biology and drug resistance. The candidate should demonstrate a good understanding of immunology and medical microbiology and have excellent written and oral communication skills. They will be expected to help develop new techniques within the laboratory, help supervise project/undergraduate students, and present their data regularly at internal lab meetings and external conferences. All applicants should be ideally proficient with in vivo immunology, flow cytometry, basic tissue culture and molecular biology techniques. Prior experience with microscopy (particularly confocal) and human cell culture would be advantageous. Applicants should be able to demonstrate prior research success; for example, through publications/pre-prints, presentations at conferences and relevant academic prizes/travel awards. Based at University Hospital Southampton, you will investigate why individuals with similar levels of adiposity differ substantially in their risk of developing type 2 diabetes and its complications. Working alongside genetic epidemiologists, clinicians and data scientists, you will apply statistical genetics approaches, including genome-wide association studies (GWAS), Mendelian randomisation and post-GWAS analyses, to identify genetic determinants, investigate causal relationships and uncover biological pathways linking obesity to metabolic disease. As a Research Fellow, you will: Investigate the genetic and biological heterogeneity of obesity and its relationships with type 2 diabetes and related complications. Conduct genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of obesity-related traits, adiposity phenotypes and metabolic outcomes using large-scale genetic and epidemiological datasets. Apply Mendelian randomisation and complementary genetic epidemiological approaches to investigate potential causal relationships between different aspects of adiposity, type 2 diabetes and its complications. Perform post-GWAS analyses, including fine-mapping, functional annotation, gene prioritisation and pathway enrichment, to identify genes and biological mechanisms underlying obesity-related metabolic risk. Investigate the genetic determinants of different obesity-related phenotypes and their associations with metabolic and cardiometabolic outcomes. Contribute to high-quality scientific publications, conference presentations and the dissemination of research findings. Collaborate with multidisciplinary researchers across genetic epidemiology, statistical genetics, genomics, clinical medicine and data science. You will have opportunities to develop your expertise in statistical genetics and genetic epidemiology, contribute to innovative analytical approaches and build your publication record within an internationally collaborative research environment. You will have: A PhD in genetic epidemiology, statistical genetics, bioinformatics, biostatistics, computational biology or a closely related discipline. Experience analysing large-scale genetic, genomic or epidemiological datasets, ideally including UK Biobank. Strong computational skills, including proficiency in R and/or Python and experience working in Linux-based computing environments. Knowledge of GWAS methodology, including genetic data quality control, association testing and interpretation of results. Knowledge of Mendelian randomisation methods, including instrumental variable assumptions, sensitivity analyses and interpretation of findings. Knowledge of post-GWAS approaches, such as fine-mapping, functional annotation, gene prioritisation, colocalisation or pathway analyses. An understanding of genetic epidemiology and statistical methods used to investigate the genetic architecture and biological mechanisms of complex diseases. Evidence of high-quality research outputs, including peer-reviewed publications. Excellent analytical, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams. Experience in obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiometabolic disease research or the genetic analysis of adiposity-related traits would be advantageous. Collaboration with leading researchers across human genetics, genomics, epidemiology, clinical medicine and computational science. Opportunities for high-quality publications, scientific conferences, professional development and career progression. items.title: GPU Kernel and Performance Engineer
items.card: You will join a small research team and turn new model designs into efficient GPU code, then measure how much time and memory traffic they cost on real hardware. Our training runs on NVIDIA GPUs, and we also expect to work with other AI accelerators, so there is scope to learn new chips and programming models as the work develops. We care more about how well you understand hardware and memory than about ML research
items.desc: CommonAI CIC is a non-profit membership organisation, founded on a belief in collaborative engineering for the safe and responsible development of foundational AI technologies. A place where AI startups, enterprises large and small, public sector bodies and academia can share resources and knowledge, to codevelop and grow businesses, fast. We are led by experienced founders, investors and engineers who believe that collaborative engineering drives faster AI innovation and are backed by a mix of UK Government and private funding in order to design, build and deploy innovative AI systems. The Opportunity We are seeking a GPU Kernel and Performance Engineer to make our research models run fast on real hardware, primarily NVIDIA GPUs. Our research team works on reducing the complexity of large language models while retaining their performance. Some of this work informs our analyses of the trade-offs between training and inference costs when scaling inference workloads. The work runs on the UK's national AI supercomputers and on our own compute nodes. You will join a small research team and turn new model designs into efficient GPU code, then measure how much time and memory traffic they cost on real hardware. Our training runs on NVIDIA GPUs, and we also expect to work with other AI accelerators, so there is scope to learn new chips and programming models as the work develops. We care more about how well you understand hardware and memory than about ML research credentials. What You'll Do Write and optimise CUDA and Triton kernels on NVIDIA GPUs for sparse and structured model components, including block-sparse matrix operations and attention variants. Adapt and extend open-source kernels, such as FlashAttention-style and block-sparse attention, to new model designs. Profile training and inference to find where time and memory traffic go, using tools such as NVIDIA Nsight Systems and Nsight Compute. Optimise for the GH200's memory hierarchy on Isambard-AI and for our own GPU nodes. Build tools that measure data movement per generated token, and check analytic cost models against hardware measurements. Test every kernel against reference implementations before it runs at scale. Work with our training infrastructure engineer to raise training throughput, and with researchers to make new designs fast enough to test. Evaluate how our models map onto other AI accelerators, such as TPUs and dataflow, wafer-scale and compute-in-memory architectures, and port key components to them where it is useful. Contribute improvements back to open-source projects where possible. Requirements Proven experience writing and optimising GPU kernels in CUDA or Triton, ideally on recent NVIDIA architectures. A strong understanding of GPU architecture and memory hierarchies (e.g. shared memory, HBM bandwidth, memory coalescing, occupancy). Hands-on experience profiling and optimising performance with tools such as NVIDIA Nsight Compute or Nsight Systems. Strong Python and C/C++. A rigorous approach to testing numerical code (e.g. comparison against reference implementations, mixed-precision error). Openness to learning new hardware architectures and programming models, often from limited documentation. A strong enthusiasm for using LLMs, coding assistants, and agents as core tools in your own software development process. We also value: Experience with attention kernels (e.g. FlashAttention) or sparse kernels (e.g. block sparsity, mixture-of-experts routing). Experience with NVIDIA Hopper features (e.g. TMA, warpgroup matrix instructions) or libraries such as CUTLASS and CuTe. Experience with multi-GPU communication (e.g. NCCL, NVLink). An understanding of LLM inference performance (e.g. KV caching, memory-bound decoding, quantisation). Experience with other AI accelerators (e.g. AMD GPUs, TPUs with JAX and Pallas, or dataflow, wafer-scale and compute-in-memory architectures). Experience with compiler stacks for AI hardware (e.g. MLIR, XLA, TVM). A background in computer architecture, HPC, graphics or game engine programming. Experience with hardware/software co-design, or with hardware performance modelling and simulation. Contributions to performance-critical open-source projects (e.g. PyTorch, Triton, JAX, vLLM). Benefits A collaborative and supportive work environment The opportunity to have a high impact in a growing organisation Competitive salary package and pension Professional development opportunities Networking opportunities with influential people from across the tech sector, financial services, and academia A vibrant office environment located a few minutes' walk away from Cambridge train station CommonAI CIC is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workplace.

Remuneration will be based on the applicable provisions of the institution's collective bargaining agreement and, subject to the candidate's personal qualifications, may be assigned to salary grade U13 . The institute for Translational Surgical Oncology (TSO) at the NCT Dresden conducts research in the area of computer- and robot-assisted surgery. Our focus lies on surgical navigation, robotics, simulation and training. Our group develops AI systems that fuse live endoscopic video streams with preoperative 3D CT or MRI data and display the results in an augmented-reality fashion to the surgeons. The AI methods perform tasks such as segmentation, depth-estimation, feature tracking and registration in real‑time. To control these systems, we are building semi‑automatic methods with intuitive user‑interfaces that are ready to be operated inside the OR. In this context, the current role would aid with the translation of AI‑systems into the operating room. This requires active research topics such as endoscopic video processing, camera calibration, real‑time computing and phantom validation in our experimental operating room. The candidate would help in the translation of current research topics into clean, high‑quality medical applications, which includes the documentation according to requirements by regulatory authorities (no prior knowledge required) and they would help PhD students integrate new AI solutions into the pipeline. Depending on the candidate's preferences, further topics can include rendering, augmented reality and registration, as well as student supervision. items.desc: Soigner Former Chercher Avec plus de 2 100 lits et places, le CHU Grenoble Alpes est le 12e hôpital de France. Il emploie plus de 11 500 professionnels dont 1 700 médecins sur 3 sites : site Nord (hôpital Michallon et hôpital Couple-Enfant, site Sud, site de Voiron). Il dispose d’un plateau technique performant et dispense des soins hautement spécialisés. Plus de 100 corps de métiers se côtoient chaque jour pour contribuer directement ou indirectement à sa vocation de soin, d’enseignement, de recherche et de prévention. Les 3 Missions Essentielles Du CHUGA Sont Soigner Former Chercher Le Poste Contexte du poste Le CHU Grenoble Alpes (CHUGA) est un établissement public de santé situé à Grenoble au cœur des Alpes. Premier Trauma Center de France, il regroupe de nombreuses spécialités médicales, une activité recherche reconnue, ainsi qu’un entrepôt de données de santé (EDS) PREDIMED, destiné à réutiliser des données récoltées dans le cadre de la prise en charge des patients, notamment, à des fins de recherche. La Cellule d’Ingénierie des Données de Santé du CHUGA (CIDS), regroupant l’Entrepôt de Données de Santé1 (EDS) et les data scientists du Centre d’Investigation Clinique - Innovation Technologique² (CIC-IT) est une structure de recherche du CHUGA. Sa mission est centrée sur l’extraction et l’analyse de données de santé pour l’évaluation des technologies de santé innovantes. Le CHUGA a été lauréat d’un appel à projet visant à l’organisation d’une compétition en sciences des données3 (data challenge). Cette compétition sera ouverte via une plateforme à des compétiteurs extérieurs au CHUGA. La problématique clinique proposée aux participants portera sur la prédiction du besoin de transfusion per-opératoire à partir des données de santé disponibles en consultation d’anesthésie. Pour cela une base de données rétrospective multicentrique entre le CHUGA et les Hospices Civils de Lyon (HCL), partenaire du projet, devra être constituée à partir des entrepôts de données de santé des centres. Elle devra ensuite être anonymisée par des techniques de génération de données synthétiques afin de pouvoir être mise en libre accès, conformément au RGPD. Placé sous la responsabilité du responsable de la CIDS et en lien avec les porteurs du projet, l’Ingénieur.e Data Science recruté(e) aura pour mission de collecter et anonymiser les données nécessaires au projet et mettre en place la plateforme de compétition sur un méso-centre de calcul. Ce travail sera réalisé avec l’appui des experts anesthésistes-réanimateurs des centres participants et des partenaires du projet apportant leurs expertises complémentaires en données massives et analyse (laboratoire TIMC4), confidentialité des données (INRIA, équipe Privatics5) et mise en place de plateformes de data challenge (GRICAD6). Missions principales Élaboration des algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle Concevoir, mettre en œuvre et qualifier les algorithmes de génération de données synthétiques afin d’anonymiser les données structurées et non-structurées (traitement automatique du langage) ; Concevoir et mettre en œuvre le protocole d’évaluation de la performance des modèles et de l’anonymisation des données mobilisant les métriques adéquates ; Documenter des modèles (GIT) ; Capitaliser et documenter des résultats et des méthodes d’évaluation de la qualité des modèles. items.desc: Position: Operations Research/Data Scientist Department: Technology Location: Berlin Ready for a challenge? Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience. Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe. About This Role As an Operations Research/Data Scientist on the Assignments team, you will help build, maintain, and scale the algorithms/models that power our global delivery network. In this role, you will work at the intersection of mathematical optimization, machine learning, and software engineering. You will collaborate closely with senior scientists and software engineers to translate business rules into robust mathematical formulations, build predictive models that inform dynamic parameters, and ship production-ready Python services. You will take ownership of discrete algorithmic components, run historical simulations, and help monitor live system performance to ensure our assignment engine remains fast, reliable, and cost-effective. These are some of the key components to the position: Solid working knowledge of combinatorial optimization concepts, particularly Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) formulations, Vehicle Routing Problems (VRP), and heuristic search methods. Practical experience applying statistical methods and machine learning algorithms (e.g., supervised learning, unsupervised learning) to generate inputs, estimate operational states, or refine optimization parameters. Strong proficiency in Python with a solid grasp of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), design patterns, type hinting, and writing clean, testable, and modular code. Knowledge of Java is a plus. Hands-on experience with Python optimization modeling libraries or solver APIs (e.g., Pyomo, PuLP, OR-Tools) and familiarity with commercial or open-source solvers (e.g., Gurobi, SCIP, HiGHS). Practical experience deploying models or algorithmic services to production, with an understanding of runtime constraints, latency, and setting up basic telemetry to monitor solution quality and performance. Hands-on experience querying relational databases and data warehouses with SQL to pull, clean, and validate data for model training, benchmarking, and offline simulation. Good working knowledge of standard development practices, including version control with Git, automated testing (unit/integration tests), Docker containerization, and participating in code reviews. Experience in the logistics and last-mile delivery domain is highly beneficial. What will you bring to the team? A curious, analytical approach to solving operational problems under real-world constraints (e.g., delivery windows, driver availability, travel times). Growth mindset with an eagerness to learn production OR & DS techniques, system architecture, and trade-offs from experienced peers. Ability to test hypotheses rigorously using historical trace data, evaluating results through clear metric tracking. Collaborative communication style, comfortable explaining model logic, edge cases, and trade-offs to engineers, data scientists, and product managers. Pragmatic mindset focused on shipping clean, working solutions rather than over-engineering. At JET, This Is How We Play Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment. Being the best at what we do isn’t just about delivering on our strategy. It's a competition for something incredibly valuable – our customers' choice. Every time a customer decides where to order, they're picking a side. At the heart of the JET Customer League are our values and behaviours. They guide every interaction, every decision, every innovation. These are the actions we need to perform consistently and brilliantly, to surpass the competition and earn our customers’ loyalty, again and again. Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition. Inclusion, Diversity & Belonging No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day. What else are we delivering? Want to know more about our JETers, culture or company? Have a look at our career site where you can find people's stories, blogs, podcasts and more JET journeys.

items.desc: Your mission Our software catches every error on package leaflets and labels. You make it smarter with AI. You bring AI into Text Verification Tool (TVT) – reliably, securely and in a way our regulated customers can trust. TVT verifies text, images, barcodes and spelling deterministically – a mark of quality for pharma and medtech companies worldwide. As our first AI Engineer, you add AI-supported features on top of these checks, for example OCR and multilingual comparison. You work across our existing product teams rather than in a single team, and most of your time goes into TVT product features, another part is contributing to the AI adoption in the company. Evaluate and prioritise AI use cases for TVT together with Product Management Develop production-ready AI features for TVT (OCR, LLMs, NLP, computer vision) Implement, host, monitor and secure AI services in productive environments Support our product teams in integrating new AI features into product portfolio (Desktop, Web, SaaS) Make sure AI features can be validated and are testable and documented for regulated customers (e.g. GxP) Choose the technical approach, models, tools and frameworks within our architecture and security guidelines Automate internal processes for example in Sales, Support and Operations with AI Your profile Degree in Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning, computer science, data science or a comparable field At least 3 years of professional experience, including hands-on experience with AI/ML or LLM applications in productive systems Strong programming skills and experience with cloud infrastructure and APIs Experience in implementing, hosting, monitoring and securing AI services Experience with document, text or image processing (NLP, OCR, computer vision) A pragmatic mindset: you think in terms of product value and can explain AI to non-technical colleagues Openness to the challenges that come with regulated industries – experience with GxP or medical device software is a plus Fluent English; German and knowledge of our technology stack (C++, C#) are a plus Why us? A key role with real responsibility: you shape how AI becomes part of TVT from the start A product with purpose: TVT helps make sure patients and consumers receive correct information Hybrid working: 3 days in the office, 2 days remote Workation possibility Spendit card after your probation period Fruit, coffee and water – they simply come with the job Team lunches and team events, both global and local A centrally located office About Us Schlafender Hase develops TVT, a content verification platform for regulated industries. TVT verifies text, images, barcodes and spelling across different file formats, languages and layouts, ensuring error-free documentation before you print or publish. Today, more than 440 companies in pharma, medical devices, FMCG/CPG and crop science rely on it. Founded in Frankfurt in 2001 (our name – German for "sleeping hare" – started out as an internal code name), we are now a team of around 40 people, headquartered in Frankfurt am Main with an office in Montréal, Canada. With Maguar Capital joining as a new investor in 2026, we have entered our next phase of growth – and that is where you come in.

items.desc: A position exists for a Research Assistant in the Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge, to work on an exciting new project developing minimally invasive implantable neural probes for brain interfacing. The project will involve the design, evaluation and characterisation of advanced neural interfaces, supported by computational modelling to investigate their electrical performance and safety. The post holder will be located in the Department of Engineering, The Institute for Biomedical Innovation, 11 JJ Thomson Avenue, Cambridge, CB3 0FF. The key responsibilities and duties are to contribute to the design and evaluation of implantable neural interfaces; undertake electrical characterisation and computational simulations using tools such as Sim4Life or COMSOL; analyse and interpret experimental and simulation results; collaborate with researchers working on device fabrication and electrophysiology; maintain accurate research records; and contribute to research reports, publications and presentations. The skills, qualifications and experience required to perform the role are an undergraduate degree in Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Physics or a related discipline, with a postgraduate qualification in neural engineering, bioelectronics or a related field desirable. Applicants should demonstrate knowledge of neural interfaces, implantable bioelectronic devices or related biomedical technologies, together with relevant research experience in device design, testing, electrical characterisation or electrophysiology. Familiarity with computational modelling tools such as Sim4Life or COMSOL is also essential. The successful candidate will have good analytical, problem solving and communication skills, and the ability to work effectively within an interdisciplinary research team. Salary Ranges: £33,662 - £36,320 Fixed-term: The funding is for 12 months or through until 30 November 2027, whichever of these comes soonest. items.desc: Company Description RAISEBOX is a Physical AI R&D company focused on training humanoid robots for real-world industrial work. The team develops advanced dexterous manipulation, navigation, and whole-body control skills for the Unitree G1 humanoid robot. These capabilities are learned from human teleoperation demonstrations and high-fidelity simulation environments such as MuJoCo, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, and GR00T, and then transferred to the physical robot. Located in Taguspark, Oeiras, Portugal, RAISEBOX offers a cutting-edge environment for professionals interested in robotics, AI, and applied research in industrial settings. Role Description The Humanoid Robotics and Physical AI Engineer will work on-site in Lisbon (Taguspark, Oeiras) in a full-time capacity, collaborating closely with a multidisciplinary R&D team. Day-to-day responsibilities include designing, implementing, and testing policies for humanoid robot control, perception, and learning, with a focus on dexterous manipulation and navigation in industrial environments. The role involves developing and integrating machine learning models, including neural networks, with robotic hardware and simulation platforms, as well as building robust software components and tools to support teleoperation, data collection, and sim-to-real transfer. The engineer will debug and optimize code, run experiments in simulation and on real robots, analyze performance metrics, and document results to inform iterative improvements. Participation in code reviews, technical discussions, and joint problem-solving sessions will be key, along with maintaining safe and reliable operation of humanoid systems in the lab. Qualifications Strong foundation in Computer Science and related fields, with experience applying Pattern Recognition techniques to real-world problems. Hands-on experience with Neural Networks and modern machine learning frameworks for control, perception, or reinforcement learning in robotics. Proficiency in Software Development, including clean coding practices, version control (e.g., Git), and debugging in languages such as Python and C++. Familiarity with Natural Language Processing (NLP) and its integration with robotic or interactive systems is a plus. Experience with robotic simulation tools (e.g., MuJoCo, Isaac Lab) and sim-to-real transfer methods is highly beneficial. Background in robotics, control systems, or physical AI, preferably with humanoid or legged robots. Ability to work on-site in Lisbon, collaborate in a research-oriented team, and communicate clearly in English; Portuguese is a plus but not required. Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience. What we offer Formal employment contract; In-house lab with humanoid robot, NVIDIA DGX Spark cluster and access to the Taguspark and IST ecosystem; real technical autonomy in a startup company; 30.000 EUR gross, possible equity participation. Expected start date: December 2027. Applications to luis@raisebox.io, with CV and, if available, links to code or work.

items.desc: Qui sommes-nous ? Grand établissement technologique, Arts et Métiers compte 14 sites et a pour mission principale de former les leaders des industries responsables, qui conçoivent et mettent en œuvre les innovations technologiques et organisationnelles impactantes, indispensables aux transitions énergétiques environnementales et sociétales. Il forme chaque année plus de 6 000 étudiant·e·s du bac+3 jusqu’au bac+8. Par ses formations, ses 15 laboratoires et sa recherche partenariale, Arts et Métiers est un acteur socio-économique au service des territoires. Environnement du poste Le poste est rattaché au projet COMPOSIA et s’inscrit au sein de l’équipe du Laboratoire Angevin de Mécanique, Procédés et InnovAtion (LAMPA). L’équipe du LAMPA possède une expertise dans la mise en place d’essais pour prédire la durabilité des composites ainsi dans la mise en place de méthodes numériques avancées avec notamment des modèles d’IA basés sur la physique qui permettent de prédire des phénomènes physiques avec un nombre de données expérimentales limitées. Le projet bénéficie d’un double financement Angers Loire Développement et Carnot Arts. Dans ce cadre, l’assistant(e) de recherche contribuera aux activités expérimentales, à la collecte et à l’analyse des données, ainsi qu’au déploiement des outils numériques développés dans le projet. Le projet est mené en collaboration avec l’équipe du PIMM (Procédés et Ingénierie en Mécanique et Matériaux), reconnue pour son expertise en intelligence artificielle appliquée aux matériaux et dans l’étude des mécanismes de vieillissement des composites. L’assistant(e) de recherche évoluera ainsi dans un environnement scientifique multidisciplinaire, au contact de chercheurs, enseignants-chercheurs et ingénieurs, et bénéficiera d’un accompagnement lui permettant de développer ses compétences en expérimentation, traitement de données et modélisation des matériaux. Missions et activités principales Le projet COMPOSIA s’inscrit dans le cadre des transitions écologique et numérique. Il vise à développer une méthodologie hybride basée sur des outils d’intelligence artificielle qui combinent données et modèles physiques (IA frugale) pour prédire la durabilité des matériaux composites à matrice thermodurcissable utilisés dans le bâtiment en zone inondable. Dans un contexte de changement climatique et d'augmentation des risques d'inondation en milieu urbain, la surveillance de l'état des ouvrages et la prédiction de leur durée de vie constituent des enjeux majeurs. Le matériau étudié dans ce projet est un composite verre/époxy unidirectionnel, largement utilisé pour le renforcement, la réhabilitation et la réalisation d'éléments structurels grâce à ses bonnes propriétés mécaniques, sa faible masse volumique et sa résistance à la corrosion. items.desc: The role A postdoctoral research position in computational and theoretical photochemistry is available in the School of Chemistry at the University of Bristol, supported by the ERC Consolidator Grant 101229789 In Silico Photochemistry of Atmospheric Molecules in Aqueous Aerosols (ISPAMIA). The project is led by Prof Basile Curchod (University of Bristol, UK). This project will investigate the photochemistry of atmospheric volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in and at the surface of aqueous aerosols. The project will comprise (1) theoretical developments to describe the complex environment created by an aqueous aerosol, from an electronic structure and nuclear dynamics perspective, and (2) the application of these methods to simulate the unimolecular and bimolecular photochemistry of selected VOCs in and at the surface of an aqueous aerosol. This project builds on recent works by our research group on studying the gas-phase photochemistry of atmospheric and complex molecules. The present postdoctoral position will focus on the study of the interaction of selected VOCs with different models of the air-water interface of an aqueous droplet, using machine-learned potentials to accelerate the sampling of ground-state distributions representative of the VOC in different environments. Further details of the In Silico Photochemistry Group can be found at www.in-silico-photochem.com, where a list of the group’s publication can be found as well. What will you be doing? The postdoctoral researcher will be based in the School of Chemistry at the University of Bristol where they will undertake theoretical and computational studies of the interaction of selected VOCs with models of the air-water interface and the bulk of an aqueous aerosol. The key techniques to be employed will involve the training of machine-learned interatomic potentials for the VOC and its interaction with water in different conditions (air-water interface, bulk, but also in the upper part of the 90-10 region of an interface). Ground-state dynamics – quantum-thermostat Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics and path-integral molecular dynamics – will be used to sample the ground-state nuclear distribution for the selected VOCs for the different environments. Photoabsorption cross-sections will be calculated from these distributions following intense benchmarking of the level of electronic-structure theory. You should apply if The position would best suit a talented, motivated, and curious early career researcher with a Ph.D. in Physical Chemistry or Physics and experience in theoretical research of atmospherically related compounds in a complex environment. Some or all of the following skills and experience would be an advantage: experience in using classical molecular dynamics, Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics, path-integral dynamics, and/or development of machine-learned interatomic potentials; experience with coding and scripting for data analysis; ability to communicate complex information clearly and accurately in English, both in written and oral forms; ability to work independently and as part of a team. items.desc: Contract Type Fixed Term Job Type Research Salary Range £39,560 - £46,970 per annum Hours Full Time School/Department School of Education Closing date 20/11/2026 Job ref 5635 Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) is a distinctive, unique institution, rooted in the Liverpool City Region and with a global presence. Our students and staff, past, present, and future, are the beating heart of our city and can be found in every corner of every industry and community. We couldn’t exist anywhere else and have shaped the city in which we belong. Working with the people of Liverpool to improve lives and support communities is at the heart of why we were founded and why we exist today. The School of Education is pleased to invite applications for a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join an exciting new research project focused on supporting children with developmental coordination disorder (DCD often referred to as dyspraxia) in educational settings. We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled researcher to undertake this full-time fixed term appointment for 18 months. You will contribute to research investigating how children with DCD/dyspraxia can be better supported in the classroom and how educational resources can be made more accessible. The post forms part of ‘Lab2School4All’ – an innovative five-year EU Horizon funded project that aims to improve the accessibility of school resources for children with DCD/dyspraxia. Research has shown that many children with DCD/dyspraxia present with persistent challenges related to handwriting and visuospatial organisation, which can create barriers to learning. Working with partners across five countries, the project team will be conducting a range of focus groups, interviews, and targeted experimental studies to explore how primary-aged children with DCD/dyspraxia access and use adapted versions of school textbooks. The findings will inform the development of practical resources and recommendations for AI-based tools that can adapt educational materials for use in mainstream classrooms and specifically create an AI-powered open-source platform designed to automate the adaptation of primary school textbooks. Overall, the project has significant potential for impact in improving accessibility and inclusive education for children with DCD/dyspraxia. You will support the delivery of the ‘Lab2School4All’ strand based at Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU). A key focus of the LJMU team is to investigate effective writing accommodations for children with DCD/dyspraxia. You will lead the recruitment of participants, manage data collection and analysis, and contribute to a predominantly quantitative study evaluating the effectiveness of different accommodations, including handwriting, typing, and speech-to-text. As part of the study, you will administer standardised assessments of motor skills (e.g., the Movement Assessment Battery for Children, third edition) alongside cognitive and literacy measures. You will also conduct interviews with children to explore their experience of using these different writing accommodations. Additional responsibilities will include coordinating research timelines and project meetings, supporting collaboration with project partners in Ireland, France, Italy and Spain, and contributing to the wider management of the project. A unique element of this post is the potential collaboration with other postdoctoral researchers in the partner institutions. The role will also involve dissemination activities, including the preparation of peer-reviewed publications, funder reports, conference presentations, social media engagement, and updates to the project website. In return, we offer an excellent benefits package including generous annual leave entitlement, pension scheme, induction, and development support as well as family-friendly policies. This is an exciting time to join the university as we deliver the LJMU Strategy 2030 and its vision of LJMU as an inclusive civic university transforming lives and futures, by placing students at the heart of everything we do. . If you feel that this is the role you have been looking for and your skills and experience can make a real difference at LJMU, we look forward to hearing from you. items.desc: About SonicPrecision Every year, more than 100,000 patients in the US and Europe undergo catheter ablation for ventricular tachycardia, a heart rhythm disorder that can be fatal. Most procedures happen without real-time tissue feedback: the electrophysiologist burns the tissue, ends the procedure, and hopes that the created lesion has reached the source of the arrhythmia. Published one-year recurrence rates run as high as 50%, which is the clinical gap we are closing. SonicPrecision is changing that. We built a near-field ultrasound sensor into the tip of the ablation catheter. The sensor shows the electrophysiologist what happens inside the tissue while the procedure is still running. For the first time, the physician can confirm that a lesion is deep enough before ending the procedure. We are a Philips spin-out, based in Eindhoven, with an exclusive, worldwide licence to the relevant Philips patent families. Our pre-clinical programme runs in partnership with CARIM at Maastricht University. Our next milestone is First-in-Human: the very first use of the device in patients. The role We are looking for a Clinical Engineer / Clinical Scientist to build and execute our clinical evidence strategy. This is a junior to mid-level role for someone with a clinical, biomedical, or life sciences background who wants to work across cardiology, medical device development, and regulatory science. You work directly with the founders and the R&D team: you build our clinical evidence, build relationships with leading electrophysiologists, and turn clinical insights into product and regulatory requirements. You will: Execute and update the clinical evidence roadmap: study design, publication strategy, and reports, from pre-clinical validation through First-in-Human and approval Help design and run pre-clinical studies with CARIM / Maastricht University Medical Centre (MUMC+): protocols, data collection, and endpoints Contribute to the Clinical Evaluation Report (CER) and Clinical Investigation Plan (CIP) for First-in-Human, working with our regulatory advisors on CE marking under the EU MDR and FDA approval for a Class III device Build our clinical network: find and engage senior electrophysiologists (KOLs) who can act as trial investigators, advisory board members, and early adopters Represent SonicPrecision at scientific conferences (ESC, HRS, Europace, EHRA) and contribute to abstracts and posters Turn clinical insights and physician feedback into clear product requirements, together with the engineering team Follow the literature and new technologies in catheter ablation (VT, AF, PFA, RF, cryoablation, contact force, mapping) and feed what matters into our product strategy and evidence plan What we are looking for Education: Master’s or PhD in biomedical engineering, clinical sciences, medicine, or a related life sciences discipline; a background in (interventional) cardiology, electrophysiology, or medical devices is a strong advantage Experience: 1-3 years; we do consider recent graduates with a strong clinical or MedTech graduation project Clinical knowledge: Familiarity with cardiac electrophysiology, catheter ablation, or interventional cardiology, from clinical research, an internship, or a graduation project Regulatory awareness: Basic understanding of EU MDR, clinical evaluation processes, or GCP/ISO 14155 is beneficial; willingness to build expertise in this area is essential Communication: Able to write clearly and present confidently to clinicians, regulators, and investors. This is an entry-level, remote position perfect for someone eager to launch their career in machine learning and artificial intelligence. You will work closely with data scientists, software engineers, and other teams to develop machine learning solutions that address business and technical challenges. In this role, you will be responsible for preparing datasets, developing machine learning models, evaluating model performance, and helping integrate ML solutions into applications. You will work with structured and unstructured data, identify patterns, and experiment with different algorithms to improve model accuracy and performance. You will also have the opportunity to collaborate with senior engineers and data scientists, gaining valuable mentorship and hands-on experience. You may work with supervised and unsupervised learning techniques, including classification, regression, clustering, and recommendation systems.
