items.desc: As an HCPC registered scientist you will play a pivotal role in supporting one of the busiest stem cell transplantation laboratories in Europe. The Transplantation Programme is licenced by the Human Tissue Authority and accredited by JACIE, making us an attractive centre for a large number of clinical trials investigating cellular therapy products for a range of diseases. In addition, UCLH is also a centre selected to treat patients with licenced commercial products and will soon be participating in the exciting field of Tumour Infiltrating Lymphocyte (TIL) therapies. In order to manage and maintain the high throughput service we provide, strong working relationships with several teams is crucial. The laboratory works very closely with clinical and quality management teams to ensure that we deliver the best possible outcomes for our patients and continue to improve our services. As a dedicated and responsible scientist supporting the laboratory you will find this a challenging and rewarding role. UCLH is one of the largest Haemopoietic Stem Cell Transplant centres in Europe. We perform over 400 transplants per year, provide vital services for UK bone marrow transplant registries and are actively involved in many clinical trials utilising CAR-T therapies. An opportunity has arisen for a responsible and self-motivated HCPC registered scientist to join the laboratory team within the Haemopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation Programme. The team consists of 9 scientists who are all involved in the processing, storage, and distribution of cellular therapy products for patients undergoing transplantation. A rigorous quality management system is in place to ensure that the facility operates within national and international legislation, and provides the best possible care to patients and donors. As part of this small, dedicated team, the post holder will be required to work in a clean-room environment to process bone marrow, stem cells and other cellular therapy products for patient transplant. The post holder will be required to maintain at all times the high standards and quality of this highly regulated service and keep an up-to-date knowledge of Haematology and Stem Cell Transplantation Biology, and current working practices in those areas. University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UCLH) is one of the most complex NHS trusts in the UK, serving a large and diverse population. We provide academically led acute and specialist services, to people from the local area, from throughout the United Kingdom and overseas. Our vision is to deliver top-quality patient care, excellent education, and world-class research. We provide first-class acute and specialist services across eight sites: University College Hospital (incorporating the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing) National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitals University College Hospital Grafton Way Building Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicine University College Hospital Macmillan Cancer Centre The Hospital for Tropical Diseases University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street We are dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of many complex illnesses. UCLH specialises in women’s health and the treatment of cancer, infection, neurological, gastrointestinal and oral disease. It has world class support services including critical care, imaging, nuclear medicine and pathology. We are committed to sustainability and have pledged to become a carbon net zero health service, embedding sustainable practice throughout UCLH. We have set an ambitious target of net zero for our direct emissions by 2031 and indirect emissions by 2040. For the full Person Specification and more information regarding the main responsibilities of this role, please refer to the attached Job Description. Come and be a part of the best NHS trust in England to work for, according to our staff* UCLH top trust to work at in England - In the most recent NHS staff survey UCLH had the highest percentage of staff who said they would recommend us as a place to work, out of all general acute or acute/community NHS trusts in England – for the third year in a row. items.desc: Applications are invited for a Qualitative Research Assistant to join the Medical Sociology and Health Experiences Research Group (MS&HERG) within the Nuffield Department of Primary Care Health Sciences at the University of Oxford. The post is funded for 21 months, from 1 January 2027, by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Policy Research Unit (PRU) in Reproductive Health. The study aims to explore adolescent reproductive health needs and interventions to address these. The Principal Investigators are Dr Abigail McNiven and Professor Katy Vincent, with the wider PRU led by Professor Jenny Hall and Professor Judith Stephenson at University College London (UCL). The post-holder will work closely with Dr Abigail McNiven and Professor Katy Vincent, a post-doctoral researcher at UCL, and the wider PRU team. They will contribute to all aspects of the research study, including ethics and research governance, study recruitment, data collection, qualitative analysis and reporting. Through qualitative analysis, the post-holder will explore adolescent reproductive health concerns through existing literature, survey data and focus groups. There may be opportunities to contribute to additional PRU projects. You will be a qualitative or mixed methods social scientist with a MA or MSc in a relevant social science subject (e.g. sociology, social policy, social geography), demonstrable experience in qualitative and mixed methods, and who is able to use social science theory-driven approaches to analysis. Previous experience of research in reproductive health and/or with young people and/or with policy would be advantageous. The role requires you to have a high level of communication and writing skills appropriate for different audiences. You should have the ability to work autonomously, while collaborating effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team across institutions. The ability to work sensitively and develop rapport and trust with research participants from different backgrounds is also essential. The successful candidate must be able to start in post no later than January 2027. You will be based in the Nuffield Department of Primary Care Health Sciences, Radcliffe Primary Care Building, Woodstock Road, Oxford, OX2 6GG as your normal place of work. Consideration may be given to some remote working days, where appropriate. We expect data collection to be largely face to face, so the research will involve visits to participants across the UK and the necessary travel and overnight stays to enable this. For further information or to discuss the post, please contact Dr Abigail McNiven (abigail.mcniven@phc.ox.ac.uk). “Committed to equality and valuing diversity” Applications for this vacancy are to be made online and you will be required to upload a CV and Supporting Statement as part of your online application. The Supporting Statement should include a cover letter and should also clearly describe how you meet each of the selection criteria listed in the job description. Please also briefly explain how the responsibilities and level of this Research Assistant position align with your current career goals and interests. Click here for information and advice on writing an effective Supporting Statement. Please do not attach any manuscripts, papers, transcripts, mark sheets or certificates as these will not be considered as part of your application. The closing date for applications is 12:00 noon on Friday 27 November 2026. Interviews are expected to be held during the week commencing Monday 14 December 2026.

items.desc: DESCRIPTION Amazon Web Services (AWS) is growing its team of Solutions Architects focused on Education and Research customers within the UK Public Sector. In this role, you will act as a trusted technical advisor, helping universities, research institutions, and other public sector organisations adopt cloud technologies that advance their missions. You will build executive-level technical relationships, serve as the voice of the customer back into AWS, and help these organisations see what is possible with cloud computing. As our Education and Research customer base expands, we need a Solutions Architect who is genuinely curious about emerging technology and motivated to translate that knowledge into practical, well-architected solutions. You will work alongside a supportive Public Sector team, partnering with sales, business development, and specialist teams to guide customers through their cloud journey — from early exploration through production workloads. Key job responsibilities Own the technical relationship with Education and Research customers, providing recommendations on architecture, security, cost optimisation, performance, reliability, and operational efficiency. Build and maintain executive-level technical relationships, understanding each customer's strategic priorities and proactively identifying opportunities where AWS can accelerate their goals. Advocate on behalf of customers internally by translating their feedback into technical requirements for AWS engineering teams and contributing to service improvements. Design cloud-native reference architectures and create technical content such as white papers, blog posts, code samples, and workshops to share best practices with customers and the broader Solutions Architect community. Collaborate with specialist teams across AWS to bring the right expertise into customer engagements and help customers explore new use cases, including generative AI and data analytics. A day in the life You might start your morning reviewing a customer's architecture proposal, preparing recommendations that balance performance and cost. By midday, you could be leading a deep-dive session with a customer's engineering team, walking through design patterns for a migration or new workload. In the afternoon, you may join a peer design review with fellow Solutions Architects, share insights from a recent engagement, or contribute to a workshop you are building. You will regularly connect with specialists across AWS to bring the right expertise to each customer conversation. About the team This role sits within our UK Public Sector team. The team has continued to grow, and we are proud to have welcomed people from different backgrounds who bring unique experiences to our work and to our customers. Our tenured Solutions Architects act as mentors and share their knowledge and experience across the group. We are all passionate about the impact we have on people across the UK, and we care deeply about our customers' missions. We enjoy working together in an environment that is supportive, inclusive, and fun. We respect that everyone has responsibilities and interests outside of work. items.desc: Description This is an exciting opportunity to join Zinc's Information Security team at a pivotal point in its journey. As an Information Security Analyst, you'll play a key role in shaping and strengthening how we approach security across the business, taking ownership of meaningful projects that will have a real impact on our people, products and technology. You'll have the opportunity to drive improvements, introduce new security practices and work closely with teams across the business to make security a shared priority. It's a hands-on role where you'll have plenty of scope to use your technical expertise, influence how things are done and help build a stronger, more resilient security environment as Zinc continues to grow. Key Responsibilities ️ You'll have the opportunity to make a real impact on how Zinc approaches security. Some of your key responsibilities will include: ️ Driving the Security Roadmap – take the lead on delivering our 2-year security roadmap, covering everything from workplace identity and cyber attack protection to workforce security, ecosystem resilience and secure software development. Strengthening Our Security Standards – tackle outstanding audit findings and recommendations, putting the right improvements in place and helping us stay on top of compliance deadlines. Bringing Teams Along on the Journey – work closely with engineering and other teams across the business to drive security improvements, influence decisions and get everyone moving in the same direction. ️ Getting Hands-On – roll up your sleeves and get stuck into the technical work, from implementing new systems to rolling out important security controls. Building Stronger Identity & Access Management – design, implement or mature IAM controls, including Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), Joiner-Mover-Leaver (JML) processes and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Skills, Knowledge and Expertise You'll need hands-on experience with the following, as these are tools and technologies you'll be working with regularly in the role: ️ Google Workspace – practical experience managing and securing Google Workspace environments. ️ AWS – experience working with AWS environments and their security. MDM (Mobile Device Management) – understanding of device management and endpoint security. ️ EDR (Endpoint Detection and Response) – experience using EDR tools to monitor, detect and respond to threats. Threat Intelligence & Vulnerability Management – experience identifying potential threats, assessing vulnerabilities and helping to strengthen security across systems. These are essential requirements rather than nice-to-haves, as you'll be working directly with these tools and technologies as part of your day-to-day responsibilities. Nice-to-Have Experience It would be a bonus if you also have experience with: ️ OWASP SAMM / Secure SDLC maturity models – familiarity with application security frameworks and improving security practices throughout the software development lifecycle. PIM / PAM Implementation – experience implementing Privileged Identity Management (PIM) or Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions. Industry Certifications – qualifications such as CISSP, CISM or CRISC. These aren't essential, but they'd be a great addition to your experience and help you bring even more to the role! We're looking for someone who can combine strong technical knowledge with the ability to bring people along with them. The following skills are essential to succeed in this role: Cross-functional Leadership – ability to work collaboratively across different teams and drive security initiatives throughout the business. Influencing Without Authority – confidence in influencing and gaining buy-in from teams, particularly engineering, even when they don't report directly to you. Prioritisation Under Pressure – ability to manage competing priorities, balance longer-term security projects with urgent demands and keep things moving. Clear Communication – able to explain technical concepts and security risks in a clear, accessible way to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Pragmatism – able to balance the ideal security approach with practical business needs, finding solutions that strengthen security without slowing down delivery. Define and apply clear, proportionate criteria for report certification so colleagues can identify trusted data and understand its meaning and ownership. Data quality and governance: Establish and maintain proportionate data-quality controls, monitoring and reconciliation so the Club can independently verify supplier-delivered data. Apply agreed standards for lineage, metadata, access control, retention and data protection by design, escalating material risks appropriately. Building on our platforms with partners: Act as the Club’s technical counterpart on agreed data-platform programmes by providing source access and data, reviewing technical designs, supporting migration assurance and taking operational ownership of components formally handed over to the Club. You will partner daily with leaders across marketing, sales, partnerships and customer-facing teams, and report to the Chief Revenue Officer. items.desc: Description Cyber Defence Analyst Location: Farnborough Clearance - SC to start, DV for role UNLEASH YOUR POTENTIAL Everything we do is built on a commitment to do the right thing for our customers, our people and our community. Our mission and our values guide the way we do business. The foundations of our Leidos culture are our Values, Beliefs and Expectations by which we select, recognise and reward employees. They create the environment that drives us toward our mission. The Cyber Defence Analyst protects customer services by identifying, investigating and helping to contain cyber threats across a 24x7x365 multi-customer CSOC. The role converts security telemetry, threat intelligence and vulnerability information into timely, evidence-led decisions. Success is demonstrated through accurate alert disposition, complete incident records, decisive escalation, effective handovers and practical improvements to detection and response. Typically knowledge of CSOC or security operations experience, or credible transferable cyber security knowledge, qualifications and practical aptitude, supported by the motivation to develop quickly in the role. Your Key Outcomes and Responsibilities Monitor security alerts continuously and take timely, consistent action in line with agreed service priorities, protecting customer services and reducing the time threats remain undetected or uncontained. Analyse alerts and supporting telemetry from SIEM, EDR and XDR platforms to establish the context, scope, severity and potential business impact of suspicious activity. Distinguish true positives from benign or false-positive activity, document an evidence-based rationale and escalate material risk without delay. Create and maintain complete, accurate cyber security incident records in the relevant IT service management (ITSM) tool, ensuring that evidence, timestamps, affected assets, indicators, actions, ownership and escalation decisions support effective response, handover and audit. Correlate logs and events across multiple sources to identify suspicious patterns, likely attack paths and Indicators of Compromise (IOCs), improving investigative confidence and speed. Map observed adversary behaviour to relevant MITRE ATT&CK tactics, techniques and sub-techniques, supporting consistent analysis, clearer communication and visibility of detection coverage. Create, test and tune threat-hunting queries and, where appropriate, convert validated findings into detection rules that improve coverage, signal quality and analyst efficiency. Apply Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) to investigations and hunting, translating relevant indicators, adversary behaviours and affected technologies into practical detection, prioritisation and response actions. Assess vulnerabilities in context, explaining likely impact, exposure, exploitability and available evidence of exploitation so that stakeholders can prioritise proportionate remediation. Recommend proportionate countermeasures and coordinate agreed containment, eradication and recovery actions to reduce risk and restore secure operations. Proactively identify suspicious activity, exploitable vulnerabilities and security misconfigurations, enabling action before they result in material customer impact. Apply incident response processes, playbooks and prioritisation criteria consistently; contribute evidence to root-cause analysis and lessons learned so that repeat risk is reduced. Produce concise, accurate incident records, reports and shift handovers that make decisions, actions, residual risks, ownership and next steps unambiguous. Safeguard customer information and maintain strict separation, confidentiality and professional discretion when working across multiple accounts. Collaborate with technical teams, customers and other stakeholders to drive investigations and agreed response actions to a controlled, documented conclusion. Contribute to tabletop exercises, post-incident reviews and measurable service improvements that strengthen detection, response and operational resilience. Technology and Process Experience Experience investigating security events and incidents in a CSOC or comparable environment, or demonstrable transferable skills and the ability to develop rapidly. Working knowledge of Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services (AWS). Experience of proactive threat hunting and of using validated investigation outcomes to improve detection and response. Understanding of the Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability (CIA) triad and its practical application when assessing technical and business impact. Current awareness of malware, ransomware and advanced persistent threat activity affecting cloud and on-premises environments. Practical knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK and its use in describing tactics, techniques, sub-techniques and observed adversary behaviour. Experience working within …

items.desc: About Euphoric Euphoric builds AI-first employee benefits administration software for the world's largest and most prestigious employers. We spun out of Peppy Health to take on what we believe is the biggest untouched opportunity in enterprise software. Global employers spend $3–5 trillion on benefits every year. It is their second-largest cost after payroll, yet the category still runs on legacy systems and spreadsheets. Incumbents cannot move fast enough, and AI-first startups have mostly overlooked it. We have two products: GAP (Global Administration Platform) for global benefits teams. It uses LLMs to parse and extract policy documents into a structured ontology, and gives admins spend and utilisation tools across every country they operate in. Navigator , the employee-facing product that helps people understand and use their benefits. We are post product-market fit at seed stage, live with some of the world's largest household-name enterprises, and we land and expand country by country. Our big current focus is flexible benefits and open enrollment. We stay deliberately lean so that the people who join own a meaningful piece of what we build. items.desc: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Deliveroo's Enterprise Systems Engineering team builds and runs the tools our employees use every day: Google Workspace, Slack, Atlassian, identity, and device management. We lean toward building: less "click through the admin console," more writing the automation, integrations, and services that make those platforms work at scale. The team's priorities span a few ongoing areas of work, including: Platform consolidation and integration as Deliveroo continues to grow, including through acquisition. Employee-focused AI tooling that helps people work more efficiently. The communication and collaboration platforms the whole company relies on (Google Workspace, Slack, Atlassian, and similar). Building tools and automation that remove manual work from how the team and company operate. You'll bring real technical strength in one or more of these areas. Some of the work will be clearly scoped; some of it won't be. Working through ambiguous, not-yet-defined problems is part of the role, this is complex, genuinely challenging territory, and a place to learn and grow. You won't be doing that alone: you'll work with senior engineers to break ambiguous problems down, and build your own ability to do that independently over time. It's a hands-on engineering role: you'll be building real pieces of this work yourself, not primarily administering platforms by hand or managing support tickets. items.desc: Over the last decade Real-Time Bidding (RTB) created massive efficiency for the digital advertising marketplace in opening large volumes of inventory, driving down prices and creating the opportunity for smaller sites and apps to thrive. Today it has become a large $300B market that continues to grow at an accelerated pace with a supply chain that remains complex, fragmented, partly opaque and could be even more efficient. In a context where decisions are increasingly made by technology, traditional processes do not apply and there is a need to bring a technological solution to what is essentially a technological problem. Fiducia is a UK company with a US subsidiary headquartered in London, that has been developing the platform of TAG TrustNet, a global cross-industry initiative, involving major trade associations in the US and the UK, and taking the industry to the next level. As an always-on "industry transparency utility, TAG TrustNet is providing the tools to certify the supply chain and allow everyone to be accountable make responsible decisions and improve efficiency. TAG TrustNet is enabling this by automating the reconciliation of data across the supply chain and recording it in an immutable ledger as the Shared Truth: a unified record for every singly ad running across the supply chain made available in near real-time. The recorded data can then visualised in the platform Supply Chain Monitor or exported over an open API. Why work for Fiducia? Competitive salary and stock options Experienced and supportive team members Fast track career development with a forward-thinking company Development of advanced high-impact technology Role Overview We are looking for an experienced and talented individual to join our technology team as Quality Assurance Engineer. Your responsibility is to develop and execute exploratory and automated tests to ensure quality, reliability and security of our cloud environment and platform software components. Our platform is used across the digital advertising supply chain to harmonise, match and record billions of ad impression data points across multiple data feeds. We are using AWS cloud services and Java as primary programming language. The Quality Assurance Engineer needs to have hands-on expertise in tracking quality assurance metrics, designing and implementing tests, debugging software and defining corrective actions. To qualify for the role, you need to be a team player with a solid background in the fundamentals of computer science, distributed computing, cloud systems and software quality assurance. Your proven ability to define and implement quality assurance processes and effectively resolve system malfunctions to meet quality standards in a collaborative team environment will be a critical part of the consideration process. Responsibilities Ensure compliance with quality requirements of our software components and AWS infrastructure in line with company goals Review requirements, specifications and technical design documents to provide timely and meaningful feedback Liaise with development and product teams to identify and clarify system requirements Create detailed, comprehensive and well-structured test plans and test cases Estimate, prioritize, plan and coordinate testing activities Design, develop and execute automation scripts Identify, record, document thoroughly and track bugs Perform thorough regression testing when bugs are resolved Develop and apply testing processes for new and existing products and software components to meet client needs and quality requirements Define and track quality assurance metrics, like defect densities and open defect counts Stay up-to-date with new testing tools and test strategies Timely problem solving Qualifications Minimum 2 years of hands-on experience in software quality assurance of complex software platforms in cloud environments Strong knowledge of software QA methodologies, tools and processes Experience in writing clear, concise and comprehensive test plans and test cases Hands-on experience with both white box and black box testing Hands-on experience with automated testing tools Solid knowledge of SQL and scripting Experience working in an Agile/Scrum development process A degree in Computer Science (preferred) or related engineering field

items.desc: What are we building? At Hard Rock Games, we’re not just making games—we’re crafting experiences that connect people, deliver thrills, and celebrate the spirit of Hard Rock. As the social casino gaming arm of Hard Rock Digital, our teams shape every stage of the journey from concept to launch to live operations, giving our teams the ability to innovate, experiment, and make real impact. With the backing of a globally recognized brand, we combine the agility of a startup with the reach of an entertainment powerhouse. Here, creativity thrives, ideas scale, and careers grow. We’re looking for passionate creators, builders, and innovators to join us in shaping the future of free-to- play gaming. Let’s play hard. What’s the position? Hard Rock Games is hiring a Slot Mathematician to design, model, and validate the math behind our slot games across our game portfolio. You will own the mathematical correctness of every game - from design through player-facing release - ensuring models meet target performance metrics and regulatory requirements. Key Responsibilities Design and model slot game math: reel strips, paytables, symbol weights, bonus features, free spins, and jackpots. Tune models to hit target RTP, hit frequency, and volatility, including multiple RTP variants. Analyze simpler games directly using data analysis tools; write and validate simulations in code for more complex games. Playtest game builds and verify that implemented games match the designed model, payouts, and feature behavior. Produce PAR sheets and comprehensive math documentation for internal review and certification labs (GLI, BMM). Support regulatory certification across jurisdictions by answering lab and regulator questions. Partner with game designers early, advising on feature costs in RTP and impact on volatility. Help build a shared Java codebase of simulators, model libraries and math tools, starting from our existing tools. Work closely with developers from specification through release to ensure correct math implementation. Leverage AI tools to prototype ideas, generate code, and explore possibilities - while maintaining full ownership of correctness. What are we looking for? 3+ years designing math models for slot games with shipped titles in iGaming, Social, or Land- Based environments. Experience in a regulated environment is preferred. Ability to build and analyze slot models directly using data analysis tools - comfortable performing direct mathematical analysis. Strong programming and problem-solving skills; Java preferred, but solid Python, C++, or C# is welcome. Comfort with version control systems like Git and working in shared code repositories. Strong grasp of probability, combinatorics, and expected-value analysis. Ability to manually verify, derive, and explain math results. You understand why a model is correct, not just that it runs. Bachelor's degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related quantitative field. Clear communication skills - explaining math concepts to designers, producers, and regulators. What’s in it for you? Make a visible impact: you’ll own campaigns and events that shape how millions play. Fast-paced execution + brand heritage: build boldly under the Hard Rock name. Competitive compensation with flexible vacation and hybrid work. Be part of a player-obsessed, inclusive team that trusts your autonomy and skills. Influence product strategies, your post-mortems and insights will steer our roadmaps. Roster of Uniques We care deeply about every interaction our customers have with us, and trust and empower our staff to own and drive their experience. Our vision for our business and customers is built on fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment where regardless of background or beliefs you feel able to be authentic and bring all your talent into play. We want to celebrate you being you (we are an equal opportunity employer).

items.desc: We have an exciting opportunity for a qualified Educational Mental Health Practitioner to join the Northumberland Primary Mental Health Team. This post will work directly into the Northumberland Be you Mental Health Support Teams. We are looking for an enthusiastic, dynamic and self-motivated individual with a passion for delivering early intervention and innovative new models of working in children's mental health. The post holder will be responsible for delivering the 3 core functions of the EMHP role. These roles sit within the 'getting help 'sector of the Thrive model. Our established ‘getting help service' provides excellent clinical, case management and peer led clinical skills supervision arrangements, training and CPD. We support a blended/hybrid model of working recognising the value of home life balance. We will ensure we consider suitable arrangements are made to your work and home base to guarantee suitable travel expenses are provided to support in this role. Please note we reserve the right to close this vacancy prior to the closing date once the required number of suitable applications have been received. The role will involve delivering a range of evidenced based low intensity psychological interventions for children and young people with mild/moderate need. These will be delivered individually and in small group based programmes. This will also include the facilitation of a range of psychoeducation sessions and staff training. The role will provide support to schools to improve their the whole school approach to emotional well-being. The post holder will also deliver a consultation and signposting role to a range of early help, targeted and specialist support services supporting children and young peoples emotional health and wellbeing. Engaging proactively with the wider team and our external partners is fundamental to the role and the delivery of the Mental Health Support Team functions. We manage three major locality hospitals at North Tyneside, Wansbeck and Hexham, plus a number of smaller community hospitals and clinics from Tynemouth to Berwick on Tweed, in addition to our state-of-the-art Northumbria Specialist Emergency Care Hospital, the first of its kind in England. We give people greater choice and control over their care to help them to live independently at home and avoid hospital admission where appropriate. High quality patient care is at the heart of everything we do and we strive to ensure every single patient and service user has an exceptional experience with us. We have one of the most extensive patient experience programmes of any trust in England. Part of the delivery will liaising with our system partners and contributing to the wider contribution across the emotional and mental health pathway in Northumberland. To role model compassionate and inclusive leadership in order to shape the creation of a collective leadership culture within the trust. items.desc: Job Overview We are seeking a highly skilled and detail-oriented Structural CAD Technician to join our dynamic engineering team. In this role, you will be the backbone of our structural design process, transforming conceptual ideas into precise technical drawings and models that drive successful construction projects. Your expertise in computer-aided design (CAD) software and understanding of structural systems will be essential in delivering innovative, accurate, and efficient solutions. This position offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to impactful projects while honing your technical skills in a collaborative environment. Duties Develop detailed 2D and 3D structural drawings using CAD software such as AutoCAD, Revit, and MicroStation, ensuring adherence to project specifications and industry standards Create comprehensive schematics and system designs for various structural components, including beams, columns, foundations, and framing systems Utilize advanced modeling tools like SketchUp, 3ds Max, Grasshopper 3D, Rhinoceros 3D, and ArchiCAD to produce realistic visualizations and detailed models for client presentations and design reviews Collaborate closely with engineers, architects, and construction teams to interpret design concepts and translate them into precise technical drawings Assist in the development of construction documents, including plans, sections, elevations, and details that facilitate smooth project execution Review and revise CAD drawings based on feedback or changes in project scope to maintain accuracy and consistency throughout the design process Support system design efforts by integrating graphic design principles to enhance clarity and visual impact of technical documentation Qualifications Proven experience with CAD software such as AutoCAD, Revit, MicroStation, ArchiCAD, and SolidWorks is essential Strong knowledge of structural systems, schematics, and construction processes Demonstrated proficiency in using SketchUp, 3ds Max, Grasshopper 3D, Rhinoceros 3D for modeling and visualization tasks Familiarity with graphic design principles to improve presentation quality of technical drawings Ability to interpret architectural/structural plans and collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams Prior experience in construction or engineering environments is highly desirable Excellent attention to detail combined with strong organizational skills to manage multiple projects efficiently Join us as a Structural CAD Technician and play a vital role in shaping innovative structures through precise design work. We are committed to fostering a vibrant work environment where your technical expertise can thrive while contributing to impactful projects that make a difference. items.desc: An excellent opportunity has emerged to hire a Band 7 Diabetes Dietitian in the Integrated Diabetes Service- North Mid at RFL NHS Foundation trust (based in Enfield Community), to offer expert assistance in enhancing and improving care for patients with diabetes in the community and acute services. We are looking for passionate professionals to become part of a dynamic team that offers development opportunities to enhance their experience in diabetes within a multidisciplinary workforce. Main Duties: To provide autonomous diabetes care for patients with Diabetes using advanced clinical skills and knowledge of diabetes in the community and acute setting. To lead and autonomously manage a caseload of patients with Diabetes, who have multiple and complex needs including complex Type 1 and 2 Diabetes, ante-natal, renal and CGM/pump/HCL therapy within the inpatient and outpatient Diabetes service. To take responsibility for own evidence-based practice and implement and add to the body of knowledge that supports expert practice within Diabetes. To lead and innovate diabetes related specialist practice, both within the Trust and through local networks. To develop diabetes guidelines, protocols and policies for the Trust To develop all staff within the multidisciplinary team, providing support, advice, formal and informal education. To actively contribute to and participate in the delivery of Trust-wide multi disciplinary mandatory training and teaching. To provide specialist advice to inpatient diabetes service by receiving direct referrals from members of other multi-disciplinary teams The Integrated Diabetes Service is a nurse-led service supported by a multidisciplinary team, including a diabetes consultant, clinical nurse lead, diabetes specialist nurses, dietitian, psychologist, healthcare assistant, and a health and wellbeing coach. The service delivers specialised care for adults with Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes, including support for pregnancy, renal, and preconception clinics. Care is provided through a fully integrated model, with close collaboration between community and acute teams. The service adopts a multidisciplinary team (MDT) approach. Clinical activities include assessment, diagnosis, shared decision-making, and the delivery of personalised treatment and management plans, focusing on achieving the three treatment targets and completing the nine key diabetes care processes. This includes comprehensive assessment of patient history and pathology, management of diabetes-related complications, and review of dietary and lifestyle interventions. The service also provides structured education programmes for individuals newly diagnosed with diabetes. items.desc: Where Warwick What I.T. & Communications Type Contract Salary Daily Data Enterprise Architect Utilities Hybrid: 1 day per week in Warwick 6 months+ £950 - £1000 per day In short: We're seeking a strong, senior Data Enterprise Architect to define the data landscape across our business. This is not an ivory tower role. The perfect person would be able to map out and assess the current state of data architecture, work with transformation teams to improve areas while modelling the conceptual and logical piece. You need to have the skills to dig deep where possible and confidently present findings that will be used for decision-making. A hands-on, consultative approach is what we need. In full: Role overview: Establish and evolve the data domain of the enterprise architecture to ensure data is trusted, connected, reusable and ready to support business decisions, regulatory obligations, data products and AI-enabled services. The role will define the enterprise information models, data domains, architectural principles, semantic models and knowledge structures that help manage data as a strategic asset. Working across business and technology teams, the role will ensure information can be consistently understood, governed, shared and reused whilst supporting a federated model of ownership and accountability. Key accountabilities: Develop, maintain and evolve the enterprise data architecture, including architectural principles, standards, information models and current/transitional/target-state designs that support consistent, trusted and reusable data. Define and maintain enterprise information models, data domains, business concepts and key data relationships, ensuring critical information is consistently understood and managed across systems, processes and business areas. Establish architectural standards and patterns for metadata, lineage, master data, reference data and interoperability, enabling data to be discovered, understood, governed and reused. Define the architectural foundations needed to support data products and the necessary operating model (eg federated/hybrid), ensuring data can be shared, consumed and reused consistently across business domains and analytical use cases. Work with architecture, engineering and business teams to ensure new solutions align with agreed data principles, information standards and long-term enterprise objectives. Provide data architecture leadership and assurance into portfolios, projects, programmes and governance processes, identifying opportunities to improve reuse, reduce duplication and strengthen information quality and consistency. Support the development of semantic models, business glossaries and knowledge structures that improve understanding of enterprise information and support AI-enabled services. Work with Data Owners, Data Stewards and delivery teams to ensure ownership, governance, quality and life cycle considerations are Embedded into solution design and implementation. Promote enterprise thinking, helping business areas balance local requirements with wider organisational value, reuse and interoperability. Monitor and improve the maturity of enterprise data architecture capabilities, identifying opportunities to strengthen information management, data sharing, governance and AI readiness. Essential knowledge/experience: Significant experience in enterprise data architecture, information architecture or data leadership roles within a complex organisation. Strong data modelling expertise across conceptual, logical and (to a lesser extent) physical data models, including enterprise information and domain modelling. Strong stakeholder engagement and influencing skills, with the ability to communicate complex concepts to technical and non-technical audiences Experience developing semantic models, ontologies, taxonomies, business glossaries or knowledge structures. Strong knowledge of metadata, data lineage, data quality, master data management and data governance. Experience defining enterprise architecture principles, standards and target architectures. Practical understanding of different data architecture paradigms and styles, including Data Warehouse, Data Lake, Data Lakehouse, etc. Understanding of Data Mesh concepts and federated approaches to data ownership and reuse. Experience with integration, interoperability, APIs and reusable data services. Experience using recognised architecture methods and tools such as ArchiMate, UML, ERD, BizzDesign (preferred), Sparx EA or equivalent. Practical architect experience and ongoing learning of multiple enterprise data, analytics, integration and AI architectures and technology solutions, their differences, pros and cons (eg Ms Azure/Fabric/PowerBI, Databricks, Snowflake, Informatica, MuleSoft). Knowledge of recognised frameworks such as TOGAF, DAMA DMBoK or equivalent industry practice. Candidates will ideally show evidence of the above in their CV in order to be considered. items.desc: Description Plessey are looking for an Industrial Engineer to improve how work flows through our semiconductor fab, from wafer start to finished product. Reporting to the Operational Excellence & Industrial Engineering (OE&IE) Manager, you will join a new team leading continuous improvement across the business. You will run the cycle time reduction programme day to day, own the fab capacity model, and use industrial engineering and Lean methods to find and remove bottlenecks, waste and variation, with a focus on improving cycle time, capacity, cost and productivity. Key Responsibilities Run the cycle time reduction programme day to day: set baselines, analyse queue, hold and process time by module, and deliver improvement actions with module teams. Own and maintain the fab capacity model, keeping tool, process and loading data accurate and up to date. Carry out bottleneck and constraint analysis, and model the effect of product mix, loading and tool availability on capacity and cycle time. Map value streams to find waste, and lead kaizen events and improvement projects. Analyse equipment performance using OEE and equipment performance metrics, and work with Equipment Engineering to improve tool availability and uptime. Develop standard work, line balancing, WIP control and dispatch rules, and layout improvements. Define capacity and standard work requirements for new tools, processes and products. Investigate performance gaps shown by dashboards, form cross-functional teams, and solve problems using structured tools such as A3, 5 Whys and fishbone. Support capacity planning and CAPEX decisions with capacity analysis, simulation and business cases. Support 5S activities across the fab. Size and track the benefits of improvement work. Present at weekly fab performance reviews and monthly IE module reviews, and track actions to closure. Coach module and cross-functional teams in Lean and industrial engineering methods. Skills, Knowledge and Expertise Degree in industrial, manufacturing or mechanical engineering, or a related subject, or equivalent industry experience. Strong analytical skills (key requirement): able to work through large, complex data sets, find root causes and turn findings into practical improvement actions. Proven experience as an industrial or manufacturing engineer in a complex manufacturing environment. Strong experience of capacity modelling, cycle time analysis and bottleneck analysis. Practical experience of Lean tools, including value stream mapping, standard work, line balancing, 5S and kaizen. Structured problem-solving (A3, 5 Whys, fishbone, 8D) and sound statistical analysis. Good understanding of OEE and equipment performance metrics. Advanced Excel for modelling and analysis. Able to lead cross-functional teams and influence at all levels without direct authority. Able to present data and recommendations clearly to engineers and senior managers. Advantage Semiconductor wafer fab experience, including SEMI E10 and fab flow concepts such as X-factor and Little's Law. Experience with MES data, scheduling and dispatching. Experience with Microsoft Power BI or Fabric. Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or above. items.desc: The Department of Acute Internal Medicine is a dynamic, collaborative, and forward-thinking service, led by consultants from a diverse range of specialty backgrounds, including Acute Internal Medicine, Respiratory Medicine, Infectious Diseases, Medicine for Older People, and Emergency Medicine. This breadth of expertise creates a stimulating clinical environment that promotes shared learning, innovation, and excellent patient care. The successful applicant will be expected to both contribute to and benefit from this collective knowledge and multidisciplinary approach. We welcome applications from physicians who are GMC registered with accreditation in General Internal Medicine and who are passionate about delivering high-quality acute medical care within a modern acute medicine service. The clinical duties of the post include the following: 8 Direct Clinical Care (DCC) Programmed Activities (PAs) within Acute Medicine, delivered across both hospital sites as required. Duties include the assessment and management of patients within Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC), the Acute Medical Unit (AMU) and the Acute Floor; reviewing patients referred from Primary Care and the Emergency Department; providing advice and guidance to community clinicians regarding acute medical presentations; and delivering senior supervision, support and teaching to junior medical staff. General Internal Medicine (GIM) on-call commitment , currently 1:8, attracting a Category B low-frequency availability supplement (1% of basic salary). The on-call commitment is undertaken overnight (19:00–08:00) and is primarily advisory, providing senior telephone support to the resident medical team. Attendance on site is rarely required but may be necessary in exceptional circumstances. 2 Supporting Professional Activities (SPA) Programmed Activities , providing protected time for appraisal and revalidation, continuing professional development (CPD), clinical supervision, education and training, audit, quality improvement, clinical governance, and other professional or leadership responsibilities. At UHSussex, diversity is our strength, and we want you to feel included to help us always deliver Excellent Care Everywhere, as shown in our Outstanding for Caring CQC rating. Your uniqueness and experiences will be part of our creative and innovative community where everyone is encouraged to succeed. We have a range of staff networks to help break down barriers, and can offer a buddy to help new members settle in. We’re proud to be a Disability Confident Employer (Level 3) and a Veteran Aware Trust. The Acute Medical Unit (AMU) at the Princess Royal Hospital (PRH) is delivered by consultants from the Acute Medicine department on a rotational basis and is supported by a dedicated junior medical workforce. The unit comprises 27 inpatient beds, with a significant proportion of acute medical activity managed through the adjacent Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) service, reflecting the department’s commitment to ambulatory care and admission avoidance. The service operates in line with the same clinical standards, pathways and consultant-delivered care model as the Royal Sussex County Hospital site, ensuring consistency of patient care and professional practice across the Trust. While the range of on-site specialties is naturally smaller than that available at the Royal Sussex County Hospital, PRH benefits from close collaboration with Respiratory Medicine, Diabetes and Endocrinology, and Medicine for Older People services. In addition, Gastroenterology and Cardiology consultants provide regular on-site input, and patients requiring more complex or urgent specialist interventions can be rapidly transferred to the Brighton campus, ensuring timely access to the full range of tertiary and specialist services available across University Hospitals Sussex. The Royal Sussex County Hospital (RSCH) in Brighton a tertiary referral centre and provides comprehensive acute medical services within a modern Acute Floor environment. The service is centred around a 26-bedded Acute Medical Unit (AMU), which is co-located with the Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) unit, in close proximity to the Emergency Department and Radiology services, facilitating rapid assessment, investigation and treatment of acutely unwell medical patients. Acute Medicine services at RSCH operate within a well-established consultant-delivered model, providing timely senior clinical decision-making and access to a broad range of specialist and tertiary services. The close integration of the AMU, SDEC and Emergency Department supports efficient patient flow, early specialist input and the delivery of high-quality acute medical care across a diverse range of presentations and levels of complexity. items.desc: Overview: OXFIDA (formerly Aioi R&D Lab – Oxford) is an AI R&D company based in Oxford, on a mission to harness AI to understand, predict, and manage risk, helping build a safer, more resilient society. We sit at the intersection of academia and industry, working with Oxford's professors and researchers alongside commercial partners, and combining that expertise with real-world risk data at global scale to turn frontier research into AI that actually ships rather than just gets published. Our work spans AI for insurance underwriting and claims, AI risk governance, privacy-preserving technologies for agentic AI, and quantum optimisation, alongside partnership projects on nature and supply chains and the emerging challenges nobody's solved yet. We build AI products and solutions for insurers, businesses, and public-sector organisations worldwide, and run innovative research projects that push these technologies further, helping people make better decisions in an uncertain world. See risk clearly. The role? We are looking for a Product Designer dedicated to our AI Risk Governance Product, which is currently in development towards launch. The product helps organisations turn fragmented AI system information into risk insights and practical mitigation actions through automated information gathering from documents, incident-informed risk analysis and actionable recommendations. Working with product managers, engineers and AI and governance specialists, you will refine the user experience, deliver implementation-ready designs and drive improvements through launch and beyond. Fluency in both Japanese and English is essential for collaboration with colleagues, customers and partners. Responsibilities: Own UX and UI design for the AI Risk Governance Product, from user research and prototyping through to implementation and ongoing improvement. Design intuitive workflows for automated AI system information gathering from documents, incident-informed risk analysis and actionable mitigation recommendations. Shape early product concepts from ambiguous problems and research insights, exploring alternative directions before converging on a solution. Experience designing complex workflows and information hierarchies, including configurable or admin-facing functionality. Identify shared user needs and workflow patterns across enterprise customers and translate them into coherent end-to-end user experiences, distinguishing core workflows from configurable requirements. Present complex information clearly, helping users understand findings and take appropriate action. Conduct user research and usability testing in Japanese and English, translating findings into product improvements. Rapidly build interactive prototypes using AI-assisted tools such as Claude to test ideas and iterate based on feedback. Collaborate with product managers, engineers and domain specialists to balance user needs, business priorities and technical feasibility. Maintain a consistent, accessible design system, define key interface states and edge cases, review implementation quality with engineers throughout agile development, and communicate design decisions to stakeholders. Collaborating with the Product Manager, engineers and infrastructure engineers to establish a smooth end-to-end workflow, from gathering requirements from clients and the Product Manager through to design and implementation, and to define how it is run in practice. Knowledge, Experience and Qualifications: Essential At least three years of product or UX design experience. A portfolio demonstrating user research, interaction design, visual design and delivery of digital products. Experience taking products from early concept through to delivery, including information architecture and structuring complex domains. Fluency in Japanese and English, both spoken and written, enabling independent user research, workshop facilitation, presentations and documentation. Ability to rapidly build interactive prototypes using AI-assisted tools such as Claude to validate concepts and user flows. Experience designing complex workflows or data-rich interfaces, ideally for B2B or enterprise software. Proficiency in Figma, including reusable components and design systems. Experience conducting and synthesising user research and usability testing. Strong cross-functional collaboration skills and the ability to explain design decisions to technical and non-technical audiences. A degree in Design, Human–Computer Interaction or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience. Desirable Experience with AI-enabled products, risk management, compliance or other regulated domains. Experience designing multilingual products or data visualisations. Familiarity with accessibility and inclusive design practices.

The role focuses on preventing and addressing anti-social behaviour (ASB) and environmental crime across the borough through proactive, intelligence-led patrols, engagement with local communities, and the effective use of enforcement powers where appropriate. CSWs play a key role in tackling issues early, providing reassurance to residents, and helping to reduce harm. In addition to patrol duties, CSWs investigate reports of ASB and environmental offences, gathering evidence from a range of sources, and work with colleagues and partner agencies to identify and deliver solutions. items.desc: UBDS Group helps organisations deliver meaningful digital transformations through modern technology and ways of working. We work across the public and private sector to design and build products, platforms and services that genuinely make a difference to users. In the public sector, that means helping teams design services that are accessible, inclusive and evidence-led, meeting real user needs while aligning with government standards and constraints. We’re looking for a User Researcher who is passionate about understanding people, confident working in delivery teams, and experienced in applying research to shape better public services. The Role As a User Researcher at UBDS, you’ll work as part of multidisciplinary delivery teams alongside designers, product managers, engineers, analysts and client stakeholders. You’ll plan and carry out user research to inform service design and delivery, ensuring decisions are grounded in evidence rather than assumptions. You’ll operate in fast-moving, sometimes ambiguous public sector environments, balancing rigour with pragmatism and helping teams continuously learn from users throughout delivery. This is a hands-on role focused on doing high-quality research and helping teams turn insight into action. What You’ll Do Plan and conduct user research to understand user needs, behaviours and pain points across digital and non-digital public services. Choose and apply appropriate qualitative and quantitative research methods (e.g. interviews, usability testing, surveys, diary studies). Work closely with product managers and designers to shape problem statements, hypotheses and research questions. Synthesize research findings into clear, actionable insights that inform design and delivery decisions. Communicate research outcomes through clear artefacts such as insight reports, personas, journey maps and playback sessions. Support teams to iterate services based on evidence, testing and learning throughout discovery, alpha, beta and live phases. Ensure research activities are inclusive, ethical and aligned with accessibility and safeguarding considerations. Work in line with Government Digital Service (GDS) standards, supporting service assessments where required. Contribute to building research capability in teams by sharing methods, insights and good practice. What We’re Looking For User Research Skills Experience conducting user research in public sector or complex service environments. Strong understanding of a range of user research methods and when to use them. Experience working across different phases of delivery (Discovery, Alpha, Beta, Live). Ability to synthesise research into clear insights that directly influence product and service decisions. Experience working with or aligning to GDS standards, including Service Standard and accessibility requirements. Awareness of research ethics, data protection and consent, particularly in public-facing services. Ways of Working A user-centred mindset and genuine curiosity about people and how they interact with services. Confidence working in multidisciplinary, Agile teams. Ability to communicate clearly with a wide range of stakeholders, including non-research specialists. Comfortable working in ambiguous problem spaces and helping teams make sense of complexity. Strong organisation and attention to detail, including clear documentation of research plans and findings. Willingness to adapt research approaches to time, budget and operational constraints while maintaining quality. At UBDS Group, employees are given unique opportunities to work on cutting-edge projects across a diverse range of industries, exposing them to new challenges and learning opportunities that are pivotal for professional growth. The Group’s culture emphasises continuous improvement, offering ample training programs, mentorship, and the chance to gain certifications that enhance their skills and marketability. UBDS Group fosters a collaborative environment where creativity and innovation are encouraged, allowing employees to contribute ideas and solutions that have a tangible impact on the company and its clients. This combination of professional development, a culture of innovation, and the opportunity to make meaningful contributions makes UBDS Group an attractive place for those looking to advance their careers and be at the forefront of technological and operational excellence. items.desc: About the Role We are looking for an organised, proactive Stock Controller & Assembly Support to join our manufacturing team in Bridgwater. In this dual-function role, you will be the backbone of our workshop operations—managing raw materials, components, and inventory for our high-capacity AI load banks while actively supporting the assembly line to keep production moving smoothly. You will maintain precise stock control, track incoming/outgoing goods against Bills of Materials (BOMs), and ensure our mechanical and electrical fitters have the parts they need when they need them. Key Responsibilities Stock & Inventory Control: Manage goods in/out, inspect incoming deliveries against purchase orders, and record stock movements accurately. Organise workshop store areas, ensuring parts, fastenings, and components are clearly labelled and safely stored. Kitting up parts and materials for production runs according to Bills of Materials (BOMs) and job sheets. Conduct regular stock counts, audits, and highlight reorder levels to prevent production bottlenecks. Assembly Support: Assist assembly fitters with basic sub-assembly, prep work, and material handling (e.g., frame prep, component organization, brackets). Safely operate hand tools, power tools, and manual handling equipment to transport materials around the facility. Support packaging, palletising, and preparing finished load banks for dispatch and transport. Maintain high standards of workshop housekeeping, organisation, and safety across storage and assembly areas. Adhere strictly to company Health & Safety procedures, PPE requirements, and manual handling guidelines. Essential Previous experience in a stock control, stores, warehouse, or production support role within a manufacturing or engineering environment. Strong organisational skills with high attention to detail in record-keeping and inventory accuracy. Ability to read work instructions, packing lists, and basic engineering Bills of Materials (BOMs). Competent in using computerised inventory systems/spreadsheets and basic workshop hand tools. Practical, hands-on mindset with the physical capability to handle manual tasks safely. Excellent communication skills and a team-player attitude. Qualifications Counterbalance Forklift License (preferred, but training can be provided). GCSEs (or equivalent) in Maths and English. Previous experience in a manufacturing, engineering, or technical warehouse environment preferred. What We Offer Competitive salary. Full training and ongoing career development. Friendly, collaborative, and fast-paced team environment. Stable, long-term employment within a growing high-tech sector. Working Hours 40 hours – 8am – 5pm – Mon to Thurs & 8am - 2pm Friday About Powerload – Who We Are and What We Do Powerload is a fast‑growing engineering and technology company specialising in next‑generation load bank solutions for hyperscale AI data centres and mission‑critical facilities. Our work ensures that some of the world’s most advanced digital infrastructures can operate safely, efficiently, and reliably before they go live. We design, manufacture, and support air‑cooled and liquid‑cooled AI load banks that simulate real‑world electrical and thermal loads. These systems allow data centre operators to test and validate their cooling, power, and commissioning processes under precise, controlled conditions. Our solutions help clients reduce risk, optimise performance, and meet demanding project deadlines. With a team combining over 40 years of experience in building services, commissioning, and cooling technologies, PowerLoad delivers engineering innovation built on deep industry knowledge. We support customers across the UK and Europe, providing rapid‑response commissioning support and bespoke engineered systems tailored to high‑density IT environments. Our mission is simple: to power precision in data centre commissioning. We help clients simulate real‑world conditions with accuracy, giving them complete confidence in their infrastructure before it becomes operational. Whether through load bank sales, rental, maintenance, or commissioning support, we play a critical role in the reliability of the digital world. What This Means for You as a Potential Employee Joining PowerLoad means becoming part of a company at the forefront of the rapidly expanding AI and data‑centre sector. You’ll be working with advanced engineering systems, innovative cooling technologies, and mission‑critical infrastructure used by some of the world’s largest operators. Our environment values precision, problem‑solving, teamwork, and continuous development. If you’re looking for a role where your work directly impacts the performance and safety of cutting‑edge digital facilities, PowerLoad offers a unique and exciting opportunity. items.desc: Career Area Technology, Digital and Data Job Description Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc. When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it. Who is CAT Digital? What do we do? Big machines require big thinking. Are you looking for your next big challenge? Cat® Digital is the digital and technology arm of Caterpillar Inc., leveraging the latest technologies, data and AI to build industry leading digital solutions for our customers and dealers. With over one million connected assets worldwide, our teams use data, technology, advanced analytics, telematics, and AI capabilities to help our customers build a better world. Working with a Fortune 100 leader, you can build your career on a global scale and take advantage of development opportunities with emerging technologies. We’ve created an inclusive environment for you to explore your passions, make an impact and do the work that really matters. Join Us. Job Opportunity We are seeking talented individuals to join our team to help us grow our presence, organization, culture, which will drive our digital product development efforts. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technologies and collaborate with top professionals working on very high impact and visibility products. Don't miss this chance to join a forming presence and support digital innovation for a global leader in heavy machinery! What will you do? We are excied to offer one-year fixed-term position at Cat Digital. As Data Scientist , you will work on analytical tasks and projects on huge amounts of data to support data-driven business decisions and development. You will be a part of the team that utilizes AI, data science and statistical analysis to gain insight into asset condition monitoring as well as market and customer behaviors to support aftermarket businesses. Your Responsibility Will Involve Understanding Existing Data Pipelines And Algorithms To Provide Technical And Business Support, With The Goal To Enhance And Optimize Them With New Techniques And Models. You Will As Well Assist the implementation of next-generation techniques (such as weak learning, time series, NLP) supported by AI and agents, including tests, validation and delivery Explore and implement innovative and advanced statistical approaches to improve and transform solutions, including Large Language Model (LLM) concepts and prompt engineering techniques to solve business challenges. Provide support and explainability to technical partners as well as business partners to drive adoption Create documentation, compelling presentations and visualizations to explain complex technical algorithms and impacts into understandable business language What You Have Bachelor/Master or PhD degree (statistics, mathematics, physics, economics, biology or a similar field) Relevant professional experience utilizing quantitative analysis and AI is an advantage Experience with modern GenAI frameworks including LangChain, LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, and CrewAI is an advantage Experience in using Data visualization tools to convey and simplify complex concepts into business value and actions Solid background in using SQL and Python, knowledge of advanced statistical models and methods, fluency in AI as well as curiosity to explore and learn more. Knowledge of ML operationalization (Airflow, Great Expectations, etc.) is an advantage Ability to clearly communicate complex technical ideas, regardless of the technical capacity of the audience. We are looking for someone who can work independently as well as part of a team, who can communicate effectively and efficiently with business partners, and is willing to take ownership of their work. If you have a passion for problem-solving and are constantly looking for ways to optimize processes, we encourage you to apply for this role. What We Offer From day one, you’re set up to thrive at Caterpillar: helpful training, relatable mentors, global experience, competitive salary package, work-life balance, and the growth opportunities you expect with a Fortune 100 company. You power our success, and we are committed to empowering yours. After all, when your work can impact the entire world, it’s important to do work that matters. Additional Information The position has fixed-term contract (12 months) A valid Swiss work permit or Swiss or EU-25/EFTA citizenship is required for this position. items.desc: Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet. Key Facts: Design and build a generative-AI workflow that helps the Celonis Talent Development team create high-quality learning content — faster, more consistently, and tailored to the learner. Flexible start date. Applications are open! Background: In 2011, three students from TU Munich founded Celonis (www.celonis.com), today the global leader in Process Intelligence. Our mission: make Enterprise AI work. More than 1,400 companies — including ABB, Fujitsu, PepsiCo, and Uniper — use Celonis to analyze, design, and operate AI-driven processes. At the core is the Celonis Context Model, combining process data, business knowledge, and intelligence to give people and AI agents the clarity to act reliably. The Talent Development team enables Celonauts, customers, and partners with the learning experiences and leadership programs they need to be successful with Celonis. The Role: Learning content is one of the most powerful levers Celonis has to enable Celonauts, customers, and partners. But the volume, variety, and velocity of content needed keeps growing faster than it can be produced by hand. Also, as business needs change, it is important the content offered is relevant and tied to those needs. Generative AI now makes it possible to rethink how learning content is designed, drafted, maintained, and personalized, while keeping instructional quality and human expertise at the center of the process. Together with the Celonis Talent Development team, your project team owns the question end to end: How can generative AI augment the learning content creation workflow to produce high-quality learning experiences faster, more consistently, and tailored to the different learner needs? You'll get hands-on exposure to how a world-class enablement team works, and the chance to shape practical AI assisted workflows that could change how learning content is created across t Celonis. Your Goals: Research the current state of the art in generative AI for learning, instructional design, and content creation — including tools, techniques, and best practices Map the current content creation process and identify opportunities where AI can add the most value while maintaining quality and consistency. Identify and prioritize high-value use cases (e.g., turning source documents or materials into micro-learning, drafting scripts and storyboards, generating quizzes and assessment items, supporting localization and translation, refreshing outdated content, creating facilitator guides or other support resources) Design and prototype an AI-assisted learning content creation workflow Evaluate the results by considering content quality, relevance, instructional effectiveness, time and effort saved, usability for content creators and opportunities for personalization. Define recommendations and guardrails for responsible AI adoption, including accuracy, human review, accessibility, brand voice, and governance. Pilot the workflow on a real learning program and measure the impact The qualifications you need: You're genuinely curious about generative AI and excited to apply it to a real business challenge You bring the bias-to-action of an entrepreneur and enjoy building new things from scratch, including the ambiguity of an unsolved problem You're interested in learning, enablement, instructional design, user experience or knowledge management Experience with AI tools, prompt engineering, no-code automation, or basic scripting helpful but not required) You are comfortable collaborating with different stakeholders and translating ideas into practical solutions Your enthusiasm is contagious and you can win people over What Celonis can offer you: Pioneer Innovation: Work with the global leader in Process Mining and the Process Intelligence Graph to shape the future of AI-driven business operations. Ownership from Day 1: Every full-time Celonaut is an owner, receiving Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and merit-based refresh grants.
