items.desc: Are you passionate about helping organizations turn complex AI security challenges into clear strategies and practical solutions? At Plain Concepts , our AI Security Studios team helps organizations adopt AI securely and responsibly by defining how risks, controls and responsibilities should be managed throughout the AI lifecycle. As an AI Security Governance Architect , you will help design and operationalize cybersecurity governance frameworks for AI, Generative AI and agentic AI , working closely with security, architecture and business teams. You will act as a cybersecurity subject matter expert for AI governance , translating emerging AI risks into practical security controls, requirements, processes and architecture patterns that organizations can actually implement. Key Responsibilities Define and evolve AI security governance frameworks , covering AI use case registration, risk classification, security controls, approvals, exceptions, monitoring and periodic reassessment. Align AI security governance with recognized standards and regulations , including NIST AI RMF, NIST Generative AI Profile, ISO/IEC 42001, OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and the EU AI Act. Assess AI, GenAI and agentic AI use cases from a cybersecurity perspective , considering risks such as prompt injection, sensitive data leakage, identity and access management, excessive agent permissions, model exposure, third-party AI services, data residency and AI supply chain risks. Translate AI risks into practical security controls , including security policies, technical requirements, architecture patterns, guardrails, evidence requirements, ownership and acceptance criteria. Integrate AI security governance with existing security tooling and processes , including solutions such as HiddenLayer, Sentra and Zenity, as well as GRC, IAM, DLP, SIEM/SOC, cloud security, CMDB and data governance environments. Define and improve AI security governance deliverables , including AI security control frameworks, use case classification models, security requirements, architecture patterns, risk acceptance processes, security review templates, KPI/KRI dashboards and maturity roadmaps. Requirements 8+ years of experience in cybersecurity , with a strong background in security governance, security architecture, risk management, AppSec or Cloud Security. Strong understanding of AI and GenAI security risks , including LLM application security, prompt injection, sensitive data leakage, RAG security, AI agent permissions, model/API exposure, model supply chain and third-party AI services. Experience designing and operationalizing security governance and control frameworks , with the ability to turn policies and risk requirements into practical controls, processes and security requirements. They design, validate and maintain secure OS baselines and oversee patching and vulnerability management to ensure stability, security, performance and audit readiness in regulated environments. Automate repetitive tasks with advanced shell scripting, Ansible, Puppet or equivalent tools to improve consistency, accuracy and efficiency. Update runbooks, procedures and knowledge articles with current practice, known errors and lessons learned. Lead major-incident technical bridges, updating incident managers and stakeholders on root cause, impact and recovery. Review high-risk kernel, clustering, storage and baseline changes, assessing risk and giving technical approval before CAB submission. Design, test and document clustering and HA using Pacemaker, Corosync, DRBD, Oracle RAC dependencies and application-level clustering, including failover. The role spans Windows client and Server OS build and lifecycle, Remote Desktop Services (RDS) and RDP remote-access management, patch management and compliance (WSUS, SCCM/MECM, and Ivanti), software packaging and deployment, OS deployment (OSD), and supporting Windows Server and virtualisation environments. As a Level 10 specialist, the engineer provides advanced troubleshooting and strategic guidance, leads root-cause analysis for major incidents, drives automation, and mentor junior (L1/L2) team members — working within ITIL-aligned service delivery and corporate security standards. Due to the nature of the work and the customers we support, the successful candidate must be eligible to meet UK Government and contractual personnel security requirements, including the applicable residency requirements for the role, and have the right to work in the United Kingdom. Some roles may also be subject to nationality requirements where these are necessary to meet UK Government or contractual security obligations. Please note this role will require attendance on-site 5 days a week. Key Responsibilities Windows Server & Remote Desktop Services (RDS / RDP) Design, build, configure, patch, and maintain enterprise Windows Server platforms — including Windows Server 2016/2019/2022 and 2025 — covering Active Directory, GPO, DNS, and DHCP. Manage and support Remote Desktop Services (RDS) — Session Host, Connection Broker, Gateway, Web Access, and Licensing — including farm design, session management, and user-profile/FSLogix configuration. Administer, secure, and troubleshoot the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) — connectivity, certificates, encryption/NLA, Group Policy controls, and remote-access performance. Endpoint Management — SCCM/MECM, WSUS & Ivanti Design, implement, and maintain the SCCM/MECM hierarchy (Primary/Secondary sites, Distribution Points, Management Points, Software Update Points); define and enforce policies, standards, and operating procedures. Administer WSUS and Software Update Points; manage Ivanti (and comparable endpoint/patch-management platforms) for patching, software distribution, and endpoint control. Monitor site/endpoint health and client status; maintain boundaries, collections, and client settings; perform site backup and disaster-recovery validation. Patch Management & Compliance Plan and execute enterprise patching strategies for Windows client/Server OS, Office, and third-party applications using WSUS, SCCM ADRs, and Ivanti. Configure, test, and deploy Automatic Deployment Rules (ADRs) and Compliance Baselines; monitor compliance reports and remediate non-compliant endpoints and servers. Collaborate with IT Security to align patching with corporate security policies and vulnerability-remediation targets. Software Deployment & Application Packaging Package, test, and deploy applications across enterprise endpoints and RDS hosts using SCCM task sequences; automate deployments with PowerShell and advanced techniques. Resolve deployment issues including application conflicts and installation failures; maintain software inventory, license tracking, and reporting. Operating System Deployment (OSD) & Windows Lifecycle Manage Windows OS imaging, boot images, driver packages, and task sequences; lead in-place upgrades, bare-metal deployments, and device/server refresh cycles. Maintain a library of standardised enterprise images (client and Server) aligned with IT standards; optimise OSD workflows for reliability and minimal downtime. Automation, Reporting & Incident Leadership Drive automation for patching, provisioning, monitoring, and compliance using PowerShell (and tools such as Ansible/PowerCLI where applicable). Develop SQL queries and SSRS reports for inventory, compliance, deployment, and patch status; track KPIs (patch-compliance rate, deployment success rate, client/server health). Lead root-cause analysis for major incidents across Windows, RDS, and endpoint environments; mentor L1/L2 engineers and maintain accurate documentation (CMDB integrity, runbooks). Technical Skills & Experience Essential: Advanced Windows Server administration — Windows Server 2016/2019/2022 and 2025 — including Active Directory, GPO, DNS, and DHCP. Hands-on management of Remote Desktop Services (RDS) — Session Host, Connection Broker, Gateway, Web Access, Licensing — and the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), including secure configuration and troubleshooting. Proficient in Windows client OS, networking, and endpoint security. Expert knowledge of SCCM/MECM — hierarchy, client deployment, site maintenance, task sequences, ADRs, and compliance baselines. items.desc: We are growing. And we are looking for talented people. At Decskill, we believe that technological excellence is driven by human talent. We are an IT consulting company with more than 10 years of consolidated experience in the market, focused on building long-term relationships with both our clients and our people. Mission: As part of an Intelligent Automation and AI team, you will be responsible for designing, developing and continuously improving production-grade AI agents supporting business operations. Contribute to model lifecycle management, including model and provider changes and context window considerations. Analyse cost and latency trade-offs when selecting and implementing AI solutions. Collaborate closely with Business Analysts and technical teams to translate business processes and operational knowledge into AI agent behaviour. Ensure the reliability, scalability and quality of AI solutions in production environments. Work collaboratively within a multicultural and international team. Requirements: 3–6 years of experience in Python development. At least 1–2 years of experience working with LLM/Generative AI applications. Practical experience with at least one AI agent framework, such as: CrewAI LangGraph LangChain AutoGen Similar frameworks Understanding of ReAct-style agent loops, tool calling and structured outputs. Strong knowledge of prompt engineering. Experience with RAG patterns and LLM evaluation techniques. Experience consuming REST and/or gRPC APIs. Knowledge of JSON Schema design. Experience with asynchronous Python. Working knowledge of Docker and Kubernetes. Ability to deploy applications, read logs and safely manage Kubernetes ConfigMaps. Strong testing culture and experience with pytest. Experience mocking LLM calls and designing deterministic tests for non-deterministic AI systems. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to translate business requirements into reliable technical solutions. Strong collaboration and communication skills. Fluent English. A people-first culture, focused on transparency and trust. Teams that value ownership, collaboration and stability. The opportunity to work with cutting-edge Generative AI and Agentic AI technologies. Exposure to real-world AI use cases and production environments. A collaborative and multicultural working environment. The opportunity to contribute to the evolution of AI solutions from development to production.
